Machine-wide limit (owner, 2026-10-12 09:40): VBW as a whole never takes more than about three quarters of the machine's cores, however many projects, sessions and runs are proving at once: one shared budget per machine (a slot store in the user's Claude config folder, each unit of a proof or fix done takes a slot, a run that finds none waits its turn), so runs take turns instead of fighting (today a 12-minute fix done took 87 under four concurrent runs). Same tests, same results, no thrash; the check_jobs setting stays as a per-run cap below it. Goes with T127 (one fix done per fix round). First item after 2.0.34, before the loop

Several vbw fix done runs at once slow each other down (2026-10-12: three in parallel plus another session's run took a 12-minute run to 87 minutes). The fixing workflow has every Dev run its own fix done, so a round with several groups already runs several at once. Decide: the kernel serialises fix done runs (one proof lock per clone, the later ones wait and reuse), or the workflow runs one fix done for all groups at the end; measure first

Stale proof copies: a process killed outright leaves its .vbw/runtime/proof.* copy (13 MB seen 2026-10-12 05:26 from a killed duplicate fix done); the next proof removes copies whose owner process is gone (record the owner pid in the copy folder, as the gate's mutex does), with a test. Part of the machine-wide limit milestone (T128)

A project where the VBW plugin is disabled shows no VBW (owner, 2026-10-12 12:30, a user project): the status line VBW installs is a user-level setting that runs in every project, so it keeps showing after a per-project disable (enabledPlugins false in the project's .claude/settings.json; Claude Code itself reports the plugin disabled there). The status line script checks the project's settings and prints nothing (or the previous status line) where the plugin is disabled; the same for the panel if it turns out to persist. Part of the machine-wide-limit milestone or its own small one

The session must run the loaded plugin's kernel (2026-10-13 14:54): in the v2 worktree the vbw on PATH was the installed release (2.0.34), put there by the SessionStart hook, so every kernel command of the session ran the released code and the record became unreadable to it once an agent wrote a new field through plugin/bin/vbw; with claude --plugin-dir ./plugin the loaded plugin's bin must be the one on PATH and the status line must show the loaded version (replaces T54: --plugin-dir did not override the installed copy); document the local-dev path

Brainstorm B4: every workflow's close-run step (vbw run confirm + run end) is a vbw:lead agent on model.lead, so Fable or Opus is paid once per run for two commands; give the step its own cheap model or let the workflow end the run itself
Brainstorm B2: /vbw:config does not know check_jobs; add the key to plugin/skills/config/SKILL.md (found 2026-10-09)

Cost: at standard and deep, mutation-check a plan's own tests before its build ends, so QA stops finding tests that cannot fail one round at a time (M15: each deep QA round found 1-2 such gaps, about an hour per loop)

Final polish (panel trust, from M18): every band and pane message disappears as soon as it stops being true (P10); no 'VBW needs you' card with buttons in the band (P1); the sound plays once per question, only with Claude Code's own menu (B1); finished agents leave the crew list at once (P4); owner judges it by eye. Do together with P2, P3, P5, P6, P9, T64, T78, T81, T87

Every long VBW step (planning, build, proof, QA) shows what it is doing now and when it should end, as a clock time from how long the same step took before in this project, in the panel, status line and VBW's messages; absorbs T85. Final polish before 2.1.0 (owner 2026-10-10: cosmetics last, core first unless a technical reason makes it urgent)

Before planning finishes, every phase has a rigor tier (express, standard or deep) with its reasons, computed from measured signals (requirement count, planned files and size, risk paths, proven requirements it could break, test coverage), and the approval shows each phase's tier and reasons in one line

An express phase is approved in one step (its requirement, check and plan together), built by one Dev and proved, and runs QA only when a requirement needs a person's judgement or the phase escalated

While a phase runs, VBW raises its tier on its own and records and shows why when a Dev blocks, a fix needs a second round, QA finds a problem in an express phase, the change touches a risk path or grows well beyond its plan, or a proven requirement fails; it never lowers a tier during a run
Which agents run, how many, the QA tier and the models follow each phase's tier through the profile
The tier is chosen automatically by default; the user can force it with vbw config rigor auto, express, standard or deep

Each finished phase records its predicted tier and the outcome (fix rounds, QA findings, escalations), and vbw show reports how often the prediction held; cost is measured per session by the benchmark
On the seven single-task benchmark cases, VBW 2 with automatic rigor passes every case and costs at most twice what plain Claude Code costs, on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5

The benchmark adds at least three multi-requirement projects (a feature on an existing codebase with earlier requirements to protect, a data migration, and a third non-UI project of several requirements), each graded by a deterministic check, run with plain Claude Code and VBW 2, and docs/benchmark.md reports them plainly

requirements.text: The panel shows an estimated time left for the current step and for the milestone, based on how long earlier steps took in this project, and says plainly when it has no basis for an estimate yet

a step that runs past its usual time is 'longer', never negative; with no step running there is no step estimate

the milestone estimate is the running step's time left plus phases left times the usual build plus check time, has no basis without enough build and check history, and is nothing when no phase is left
bad history entries are ignored without a crash or a wrong number
ending a run records one finished step (kind, run, start, end, seconds) in the clone's steps.json, oldest first, only the latest 50, shared by worktrees
the history adds no record field, no schema change and no tracked file, and a damaged or unwritable cache never stops a run from ending
a run ended with no run open records nothing
with no or too little history the panel says plainly it has no basis and shows no time; with enough it shows about N min for the step and the milestone
a step past its usual time says it is taking longer than usual and shows no negative time; idle shows only the milestone; no phase left shows no milestone estimate
a missing or garbled history means no history and no error, and in a linked worktree the history is read from its clone
the history is only read, from the clone cache, with no network, and the shown estimate follows the clock
the estimate code is pure and local, states MIN_STEPS = 3, and the panel reads history only from steps.json
the panel bench measures a refresh that works out two estimates (its CPU budget is judged in the release run, not in vbw prove)
docs/panel.md says how many finished steps an estimate needs, that it is approximate, and where the history is kept

requirements.text: The interview opens with: "Hello, Human! Welcome to VBW. Let me interview you real quick to better adapt to you. What is your level of proficiency?", with the same four options as before

rules.text: the first thing the interview says is exactly the new greeting
the four options follow it in the same order and wording
choosing a level still records it and continues the interview
later questions, follow-up rules and keep order are unchanged
the old opening wording is gone from the skill and docs/interview.md, and the docs show the greeting
the router and interview prompt stay within their budgets
a returning user with a recorded level is not asked the level question again

requirements.text: At every stop, VBW ends its message with one plain line saying what it needs from the user now, or that it needs nothing

rules.text: the router tells VBW to end every stop with one line of what it needs from the user, or nothing
the router stays within its 1,400-word budget

requirements.text: Approval is offered as a choice: VBW asks with the options Approve (first, so Enter approves), Not yet (VBW asks what to change) and the user's own words; picking Approve approves exactly the contract shown, recorded by VBW's own code from the user's answer so Claude can never approve by itself; typing /vbw:approve still works

rules.text: the approval question offers Approve first, Not yet second, and the question names the contract by its 12-character fingerprint
approve with a fingerprint approves the contract it names with the same decision entry as plain approve, once per approval whichever path is used
if the contract changed after the question, approving by its old fingerprint approves nothing and says the contract changed
a malformed fingerprint or a contract not ready for approval is refused and nothing is written
answering Approve to VBW's approval question approves exactly the contract the question named, through VBW's own hook
when the contract changed after the question, Approve approves nothing, and the user is told in plain words and shown the new contract
answering Not yet approves nothing and VBW is told to ask what to change
the user's own words approve nothing and are treated as what to change or a question
any other question, in a VBW project or outside one, changes nothing and prints nothing
when the hook cannot approve (nothing ready, already approved, damaged record) nothing changes, the record is untouched and the user sees one sentence saying why and what to do
the decision is recorded once per approval even when both the choice and /vbw:approve are used
the answer may arrive as a map or a list of answers
the model's own call to approve is still refused by the guard
an answer-shaped message from the model, another tool's result, or a subagent does not approve
the hook bench measures the new hook's cost (its limit is judged in the release run, not in vbw prove) and the kernel stays within its line budget
the router asks for approval with a choice, Approve first, built from the question the kernel prints, and says what to do with each answer; typing /vbw:approve still works
the prompts stay within their budgets
the docs and the README describe the choice, the Approve-first order and that /vbw:approve still works
a real Claude Code scenario shows the choice appearing and Enter approving the shown contract, and says whether it ran

requirements.text: Once the interview knows what is being built, VBW asks the user's permission to look for the best tools for this project (community skills, automated code-safety scanners, code-quality tools such as linters and formatters, unit-test and other test frameworks); on yes, Scouts research current best-in-class options for the project's stack, with sources, and VBW proposes a short list; nothing is installed until the user approves that list; on no, nothing is searched or installed; it is asked once per project, and /vbw:skills runs it again any time

rules.text: the permission question is asked once the interview knows what is being built, as one plain yes/no question that explains each kind of tool
the question is asked once per project: the answer is remembered in the project record and a second pass does not ask again
the interview skill reads the remembered answer and skips the question when there is one
on no nothing is searched or installed, the record shows no, and the flow continues unchanged
on no the interview skill starts no Scout, searches nothing and installs nothing
on yes a Scout per angle (safety, quality, tests, skills) runs in parallel on the project's own stack
each pick carries a source link; a pick without one is not shown
respected open-source picks are proposed; anything else carries a plain warning
the proposed list is short, trusted picks first
a Scout that fails or finds nothing, or an unknown stack, gives a plain note and no error
the skills skill shows each item in plain words (what, why it fits, where from) and lets the user keep, drop or look further for untrusted picks
nothing is installed until the user approves the list; declining, not yet or a partial approval installs only what was approved
for each approved tool the user is asked project only or all projects and the install goes to that scope
when nothing is found or the stack is unknown the skills skill says so plainly and installs nothing
/vbw:skills runs the research at any time, after a yes or a no, from any state of a VBW project
/vbw:skills can store the answer again later and the record stays valid
the skills skill ends every stop with one plain line saying what VBW needs
the interview step ends with the line 'I need your yes or no to look for tools'
the user documentation explains the offer, trusted sources, approval before install, the scope choice and /vbw:skills
a real Claude Code run shows the answer stored once, not asked again, and nothing installed before approval

requirements.text: The recommended tools fit the project and are explained at the user's level
VBW's own real-app test sessions never play the sound aloud and never read or change the user's own panel and sound choices

rules.text: a VBW test session plays no sound aloud
a VBW test session never reads or changes the user's own panel and sound choices
every real-app test project is marked as a test session, and scenarios read only the test keys

requirements.text: When a project has a VBW 1 folder, VBW first reviews it (how much was finished, how recently it was used, whether its plans still match the current code, any work half done) and recommends converting or starting fresh with its reasons in plain words, the recommended option first; the user still chooses

rules.text: a project without a VBW 1 folder gets no review and no message, and no error
the review reports how much was finished, how recently it was used, whether the plans still match the code and any work half done, computed by the kernel from the folder and the repo
an empty folder, a folder with no readable plans, corrupt or partly missing files and a folder not in git each give a review that says what could not be read, never a crash
what could not be read is never recommended for conversion
the recommendation is convert or start fresh with reasons that name the numbers, and the same folder always gives the same recommendation
the review writes nothing, runs no command found in the old folder and uses no network
the kernel with the review stays within 3,500 lines
the choice is remembered in the project record once per project, so a later or resumed interview does not ask again
only convert or fresh is accepted; nothing else is recorded, and a damaged stored choice is refused
start fresh converts nothing and leaves the old folder untouched, and the project stops being asked to convert
convert keeps the old folder in place and the conversion is still marked by legacy done
the interview step comes right after the level answer, before any other question, and is skipped silently when there is no folder or a choice is recorded
the review is shown to the user in plain words at their level and depth, from the kernel's numbers and recommendation, never guessed by the model
the choice is asked with the recommended option first and the other second, each with a trade-off; either can be picked and own words are accepted
convert runs /vbw:convert and reports the result; start fresh records the choice, converts nothing and the interview goes on; the review can be run on demand
the step reads files only and adds one interview step; the router's convert step defers to it; prompts stay within their word budgets
user documentation describes the review, its four facts, the recommendation, each choice, unreadable folders, once-only asking and on-demand use
a real Claude Code run on a fixture with a VBW 1 folder shows the review, the recommendation and the choice, and nothing converted when start fresh is picked
a real Claude Code run on a project without a VBW 1 folder does not ask

requirements.text: Changing the plan mid-milestone (adding or changing phases) keeps each phase's QA pass; QA then checks again only new phases and phases whose own inputs changed

rules.text: adding a phase mid-milestone keeps the QA verdicts of the phases already checked
after the new phase is built, QA is asked to check only the new phase; the others stand
a kept phase whose goal or plan changed in the re-plan is checked again, with that reason

requirements.text: When a project has a VBW 1 folder and the user has not been interviewed yet, VBW opens with the interview greeting and level question, and asks convert or start fresh right after the level answer

rules.text: with a VBW 1 folder and no interview, vbw next at convert says the interview is due, from the level question
after the interview, the convert step does not ask for it again
the router interviews before spec or convert work

requirements.text: The review of an old VBW 1 folder works on Linux as on macOS, including folders not tracked by git

rules.text: with GNU stat, an untracked folder is reviewed from its newest file time
file times in the kernel come only from vbw_mtime

requirements.text: vbw prove runs the approved checks in parallel, except checks marked alone, which still run by themselves; the results are the same as running them one after another, and a proof of many checks finishes in a fraction of the time

rules.text: vbw prove runs the approved checks in parallel, by default up to four at a time
checks marked alone still run by themselves, never beside another check
the passed and failed checks and their recorded results are the same as running them one after another
a proof of many checks runs them side by side, so it takes a fraction of the sequential time (its duration is measured in the release run, not in vbw prove)
a stop signal sent to vbw prove alone waits for its running checks, then cleans up; nothing outlives it
the check gate lock is never taken from a live owner: an empty owner file means retry, and only an owner-less lock left past a wait is taken over

requirements.text: A QA round runs the project's test command once and gives its result to every QA agent of that round, instead of each agent running the whole suite again

rules.text: the result of the one run of the project's test command is handed to every QA agent of the round
the QA agents are told not to run the project's test command again
no agent is started only to run the suite
a run that did not start is said once and no agent retries it
a suite that ran and failed is handed over as failed and is not run again
a project with no test command has nothing to hand over, and a command that did not run in the proof is never handed over as passing

requirements.text: How deeply QA checks a phase follows the size and risk of its change: a small, low-risk change gets a quick check and never a deep one, and a change to wording or documentation alone needs no new check

rules.text: a small, low-risk change (one or two files) gets a quick QA check and never a deep one
a change of three to nine files gets at most a standard QA check
a larger change gets deeper QA in proportion to its size, and a riskier one gets deeper QA however few files it touches
the size never raises QA above what the profile gives
a change to wording or documentation alone needs no new check and is closed without one
a change to code, or to code and documentation together, still needs its check
a project rule that requires a check overrides the documentation exemption: that check runs and decides
documentation is defined once (md, markdown, rst) and the early tier and the Lead use that definition

requirements.text: A small change (one or two files, low risk) goes from the user's request to done through /vbw:vibe without a planning workflow: VBW plans it itself as one plan with its check, the user approves once, it is built, checked and closed

rules.text: a request of one or two [auto] requirements with no risk path is marked small, in a repository of any size
a request of three requirements, a [human] requirement, a risk path or a forced rigor above express is not small
a small change is planned as one express phase with one plan and its check, approved once, built, checked and closed
a change touching more than two files is not treated as small in a large repository and follows normal planning
in the real app a small change goes to done without the planning workflow, with one approval, its check passing and QA quick at most

requirements.text: A project's proof never reuses build output from the working folder: the clean copy has its own build folders (for any language), so artifacts never point into another copy

rules.text: the clean copy has its own build folders for Node, Python, Rust and Go style projects: none is linked to the working folder
the project's environment (dependency folders and env files) is still linked into the copy
a proof never reads build output left in the working folder: deleting those folders does not change the result
build output made during a proof stays in the copy and never reaches the working folder

requirements.text: A plan whose files were already committed (for example by the approval commit) and whose checks pass can be marked done; a blocked or stuck plan never stops unrelated plans from being scheduled

rules.text: a plan whose files were already committed, with no plan trailer, and whose checks pass can be marked done
a plan whose files are committed but whose checks fail cannot be marked done, and the failing check is named
uncommitted changes in a plan's files, and a plan with no commit and no check that could prove it, still block done
a blocked plan never stops unrelated plans from being scheduled by vbw next
the blocked plan is reported by name with its reason
plans that depend on a blocked plan stay unscheduled

requirements.text: While VBW plans, its agents may write only VBW's own files and the test files the plan declares, so a planning run never blocks another session's folders

rules.text: while VBW plans, its agents may write only VBW's own files and test files
a write to any other path during planning is refused with the reason, by file tools and by shell
a planning run never blocks another session's folders

requirements.text: A Dev's command that writes a file outside its plan through a program (Python, Node, Perl or similar) is refused like a shell write outside its plan

rules.text: a Dev's command that writes a file outside its plan through Python, Node, Perl or Ruby is refused like a shell write outside its plan
the same program writing a file inside its plan is allowed
programs that only read, or run tests, are allowed
the hook benchmark measures a program command during a run (its cost is judged in the release run, not in vbw prove)

requirements.text: Reading the plan of record (copying or printing it) or naming the approval command in plain text is never refused as a write or as an approval

rules.text: copying or printing the plan of record is never refused as a write, while writing it stays refused
naming the approval command in plain text (a message, a commit message, an echo) is never refused as an approval
actually running the approval, wherever it is hidden, is still refused

requirements.text: After each agent of a build, fix or QA workflow returns, VBW confirms that its plan state or verdict was recorded, and says plainly which ones were not

rules.text: after a build run, a plan whose state was not recorded is named plainly
after a fix run, a fix whose result was not recorded is named plainly
after a QA run, a phase with no verdict from that run is named plainly
the build, fix and QA workflows confirm after their agents return and name what was not recorded in their output

requirements.text: The test-file edits made while building a phase are approved together once, before the phase is proved, instead of one approval for each edit

rules.text: test-file edits made while building go on without a new approval, and vbw check still runs
one approval before the proof covers all the edits, and vbw next asks for it naming the files
a proof with test files waiting for approval stops and says which files are waiting
a change to the contract's structure, or a contract never approved, still needs approval first

requirements.text: One plan, check or rule can be changed without resubmitting the whole milestone, and a fix round cannot add phases or rename phases nobody asked for

rules.text: one plan can be changed without resubmitting the whole milestone
one check can be changed without resubmitting the whole milestone
one rule can be changed without resubmitting the whole milestone
untouched plans, phases, checks and rules stay byte-identical after a patch, and a patch never carries phases
once work has started, a planning round cannot add a phase for requirements another phase covers or rename a phase, and is refused with the reason

requirements.text: A project setting limits how many checks run at the same time; an approval whose commit fails stops and says why instead of only warning; a workflow ends its own run when it finishes

rules.text: the project setting check_jobs limits how many checks run at the same time, never more than set, and 1 behaves like sequential
an invalid check_jobs value is refused with a clear message and changes nothing
check_jobs is shown by vbw config, kept in the clone, and removed with default
an approval whose commit fails stops and says why instead of only warning
a failed approval leaves no approval in the record or in the consent
a workflow ends its own run when it finishes, on every way out, and never leaves a lease open
ending a run that is not open changes nothing

requirements.text: The VBW panel opens at about a quarter of the terminal width (never narrower than 40 columns); a width the user sets by hand always wins

rules.text: opening by itself the panel opens as placed; after its first docked drawing it asks once for a quarter of the terminal (viewport.columns + props.bodyColumns + 1)
never narrower than 40 columns
/vbw-panel opens at a quarter of the terminal the command was typed in
it asks only once a session, so a width the user dragged (kept by Claude Code) wins; no width is stored as the user choice
an inline drawing, or a missing, zero or odd width, asks nothing and never fails

requirements.text: VBW always asks for approval with the approval menu, where Enter approves; it never asks the user to type /vbw:approve, which still works when the user types it

rules.text: no text VBW hands Claude says to type or run /vbw:approve
when Claude tries to approve, the guard refuses and tells it to ask with the approval menu
the router asks for approval only with the menu and never asks the user to type the command

requirements.text: Every part of the VBW panel (the band, Mission Control, Wrapped) takes its colours from one shared palette: each agent role has one colour everywhere (architect magenta, lead blue, dev green, qa yellow, scout cyan, debugger red, docs pink), and each state has one colour (running amber, done green, failed red, quiet or cut off grey)

rules.text: each agent role has one colour everywhere: architect magenta, lead blue, dev green, qa yellow, scout cyan, debugger red, docs pink
each state has one colour: running amber, done green, failed red, quiet or cut off grey
the band, Mission Control (cards, timeline, team, proof) and Wrapped (card, confetti, sprites, sweep) read the same palette values
no panel file but the palette holds a colour literal, so a surface cannot define its own
an unknown role or state falls back to a neutral grey and does not crash rendering
with colour off a state is still told apart by its own mark and word

requirements.text: In Mission Control's Now tab, each agent card is framed in its role's colour and shows its state as a coloured mark and word (running, done, failed, quiet), so two agents of different roles never look the same

rules.text: each agent card is framed in its role's colour
each card shows its state as a coloured mark and word: running, done, failed, quiet (cut off for a stopped run)
two agents of different roles never render the same frame colour, whatever their state
an unknown role is framed in the neutral grey and does not crash rendering
with colour off the mark and the word still carry the state

requirements.text: In the band, each agent row shows its plan label and spinner in the role's colour, its time and tokens dimmed, and the run's cost in an accent colour in the header

rules.text: each band row shows its plan label and spinner in the role's colour
each band row shows its time and tokens dimmed
the header shows the run's cost in the accent colour, and no accent piece appears without a cost
with colour off the band's states are still told apart by mark and word

requirements.text: An agent's activity is shown as a plain intention (for example editing app-topbar.tsx, running tests, recording P6.7 done) instead of the raw command; a script run through Python, Node or another interpreter is named by what it touches; the verb is coloured and the object dimmed

rules.text: a file tool is shown as an intention such as editing app-topbar.tsx
a test run is shown as running tests, whichever runner
a vbw command is shown as what VBW is doing, such as recording P6.7 done
a script run through python, node or another interpreter is named by the file it runs, not by the interpreter
an inline script, which has no file, is a short generic phrase, never its code
an unrecognised command falls back to a short generic phrase, never an empty line, the raw command or a secret
the verb is coloured and the object dimmed, in the band and on the cards
a long object is truncated to the row width without breaking colour, and no colour code is written into the text
what an agent says, and the quiet, done and failed phrases, stay one line in their own colour

requirements.text: When Claude Code shows a change to .vbw/record.json in the conversation, VBW shows one line saying what happened (for example VBW · build run started) instead of the full diff; the full diff still shows when the user expands the row

rules.text: a change to .vbw/record.json shown as an Edit, MultiEdit or Write appears as one line such as VBW · build run started
the full diff still shows when the user expands the row
a record.json change with no known meaning shows a generic one-line summary
changes to other files, failed calls, odd input and projects outside VBW are untouched

requirements.text: Mission Control's tabs stay visible at the top of the pane however long its content is, and each sentence of the pane shows its key value in colour (progress green, estimate amber, cost in the accent colour, a need of the user yellow)

rules.text: the tabs stay visible at the top of the pane however long the content is and however far it is scrolled
scrolling still moves the content under the tabs
progress is shown in green, an estimate in amber, the cost in the accent colour and a need of the user in yellow
a sentence with no value in it (no requirements, no estimate basis, no cost, nothing needed) stays plain

requirements.text: When an agent starts, its new row in the band flashes briefly in its role's colour (about a second), only when the motion setting is full

rules.text: when an agent starts, its new row flashes in the role's colour for about a second
the flash happens only when the motion setting is full
the flash ends on its own, the band is redrawn, and the row is back in its normal colours

requirements.text: The proof copy shares no writable folder with the working folder: git-ignored files and folders (dependencies, env files) are copied in, as a copy-on-write clone where the file system offers one, never linked; so a tool that refuses linked folders or writes into its dependency folders (for example pnpm 11 recursive runs and its dependency check) behaves in the proof as in the working folder, and nothing a proof does changes the working folder

rules.text: no git-ignored path in the proof copy is a symbolic link; each is a real file or folder with the working folder's content
a write inside node_modules passes in the proof and the file does not exist in the working folder afterwards
a check that fails when node_modules is a link (the pnpm 11 refusal) passes in vbw prove as in vbw check
after a proof every file and link of the working folder, git-ignored ones and workspace links in node_modules included, is byte-identical
links inside a copied folder are copied as links; a relative one keeps resolving in the copy; an absolute one into the working folder is reported with its path
the copy uses a copy-on-write clone first and falls back to a plain copy where the clone is refused, with the same result
build-output folders are not brought into the copy
.git and .vbw paths are never copied into the copy
an ignored folder that cannot be read fails the proof before any check runs, naming the path, and leaves no copy behind
an interrupted proof removes the copy completely and never deletes anything outside it
the copy is removed after the proof, read-only folders included
docs/proof.md states that git-ignored files are copied, not linked, with the pnpm example and the clone-or-copy fallback

requirements.text: After a proof, VBW checks the working folder for links that point into its proof copies and names each one with how to repair it, so damage left by an earlier VBW is found; with none, it says nothing

rules.text: after a proof, links in the working folder (git-ignored folders included) whose target, absolute or relative, is inside .vbw/runtime/proof.* are each printed on their own line with path, target and repair
the repair for a pnpm project is to delete node_modules and run pnpm install; otherwise to re-run the project's install command
with no such link, nothing extra is printed; a link pointing elsewhere in .vbw or outside the project is not reported
the scan changes nothing in the working folder, does not follow links and skips .git
the scan runs also when the proof stops early with an error, and a failing proof still fails the same way
the scan never turns a passing proof into a failing one
on a 50,000-file working folder the scan names the stale links and the proof passes (its time is measured in the release run, not in vbw prove)
docs/proof.md describes the warning and the repair

requirements.text: In one proof, a check waiting for an alone check keeps waiting as long as that check is still running; a proof never aborts because a check waited: a check that cannot run is reported as not run with the reason, every other result stands, and the proof prints no shell job warnings

rules.text: a check waiting for an alone check keeps waiting as long as the alone check runs, with no fixed time limit, and then runs and reports
the proof prints no shell job warning while checks wait for an alone check
an interrupt during a wait removes the wait registration and leaves no gate file behind
when the holder of the gate dies, a waiting check takes over and runs
a check that cannot run is reported as not run with the reason, and the proof does not abort
every other result stands and is recorded, and a not-run check counts as not passed
no shell job warning is printed in bash 3.2 or bash 5, including when a check's runner ends early
VBW_CHECK_WAIT_SECONDS is removed from the code and the docs no longer say it ends a wait

requirements.text: Every agent of a VBW workflow (build, fix, QA, planning) records its own result through VBW (a plan's state, a fix's state, a phase's verdict) even though Claude Code marks a workflow's task text as not coming from the user; in the real Claude Code app a workflow ends with every result recorded and nothing recorded by hand, and the project's test command is named in what QA is told

rules.text: each agent role (Dev, Docs, QA, Lead) holds the duty to record its result in its own instructions, even when the task text is marked as not from the user
the QA agent's instructions name the project's test command and where to read it
QA is told the project's test command, with its result when it ran, or plainly that there is none
a workflow reports complete only when every agent's result was recorded
edge: when one agent's recording is missing, the closing report names it
error: a workflow with an unrecorded or interrupted result is not reported as complete

requirements.text: A workflow's closing step (confirm what its agents recorded, then end the run) is done by an agent whose own instructions allow it; it never refuses, and when it cannot finish it says which command to run by hand

rules.text: the closing step (confirm, then end the run) is done by the Lead, whose own instructions allow it and say it never refuses
all five workflows close with the Lead, never the read-only Scout
when the closing step cannot finish, the output names the exact commands, with the session, to run by hand
planning does not report planned when a phase has no recorded plans

requirements.text: Choosing Approve in the approval menu approves the contract it names whatever text, spaces or line breaks follow the fingerprint in the question

rules.text: choosing Approve approves the contract the question names, whatever text, spaces or line breaks follow the fingerprint
a different fingerprint approves nothing and the user is told the contract changed
a malformed fingerprint approves nothing and the kernel says what a fingerprint is
the user's own words are never an approval

requirements.text: In an autonomous run, while this session's proof or workflow is still running in the background, the stop hook does not ask for that step again and spends no autonomous step on it

rules.text: while this session's proof runs in the background, the stop hook asks for nothing and spends no autonomous step
while this session's workflow run is open, the stop hook asks for nothing and spends no step
once the background step finishes, the stop hook resumes normally
a background step of another session does not suppress this session's hook, and a dead proof leaves nothing that does

requirements.text: A fix for a failing project command can commit the files it changed to make that command pass, even when no plan lists them, and the commit names the fix

rules.text: a fix for a failing project command commits the files it changed even when no plan lists them
the fix commit names the fix
files the fix did not change or name, and files the user staged, are not committed
error: no files, an unchanged file, .vbw/ files, an unknown fix, or a requirement fix is refused and commits nothing

requirements.text: After the plan changes (a new plan, a changed plan or a re-plan), VBW asks for approval only with the approval menu; it never tells the user to type /vbw:approve

rules.text: after a plan change VBW asks for approval only with the approval menu: doctor and the router never tell the user to type /vbw:approve
no kernel output after apply, spec sync or a changed plan tells the user to type /vbw:approve

requirements.text: In the balanced profile the Architect runs on Opus; QA is never below Sonnet in any profile

rules.text: in the balanced profile vbw config models gives the Architect opus
the planning workflow started with the balanced models runs the Architect on opus
QA is sonnet or opus in every profile (quality, balanced, budget) and every rigor tier (express, standard, deep)
vbw config set model.qa haiku is refused with a message naming the allowed models, and the setting is unchanged

requirements.text: Planning splits each phase into plans that touch separate files wherever the work allows, so as many plans as possible build at the same time; the approval shows the number of build waves and how many plans the widest wave runs at once

rules.text: the approval shows the number of build waves and how many plans the widest wave runs at once

each shard runs its timed files (tests/timed-*.bats) alone after its parallel batch
the tool lint and the hook and panel benchmarks run in shard 1 only
a failing test file in a shard, in the batch or among the timed files, makes that shard fail
an invalid shard argument (zero, out of range, not a number, malformed) exits 2 with the usage line and runs nothing

requirements.text: When a push changes no shipped code, tools or docs, CI runs only the test files that changed, and skips the tests when only the VBW record or saved test results changed

rules.text: a changed plugin file means the full suite
a changed docs file or root document means the full suite
a changed tools file outside the saved results folders means the full suite
a change to the CI setup (.github/) means the full suite
a push of only saved test results runs no tests
a push of only the VBW record and spec runs no tests
a push of only tests/*.bats files runs just those files
the record or results plus a test file runs just that test file
a changed test helper, helpers file or fixture means the full suite
an unknown path means the full suite
a test file deleted by the push is not run
a renamed file counts under its new path, and a file moved out of shipped code still means the full suite
every commit of the push counts, not only the last one
an unknown previous tip (new branch, missing commit, rewritten history) means the full suite
results folders are those the record names (project.results) at both tips; CI guesses no folder
this repository's record names tools/l3-results/ and tools/baseline/results/ as saved results
the script's answer always carries a reason, and the wrong number of arguments exits 2 with a usage line
CI checks out the whole history and decides the scope from the push's old and new tips, or the pull request's base and head, before any test runs
the choice and its reason are printed in the run log
the full suite runs unless the answer is some or none, and a failing scope script fails the job
the changed test files run with bats under the target bash on macOS and both Linux jobs, the list passed through env
every test job always runs and reports success when no tests are needed (no job-level condition)

requirements.text: When a fix after QA changes only documentation, the next full proof reuses the project test command's earlier passing result instead of running it again; any change to code, tests or a check's files still runs it

rules.text: after a commit that changes only documentation the test command did not read, vbw prove reuses the test command's latest passing result, and every check and command that did not read it, instead of running them
the summary line marks the test command as reused, and a proof that reused it passes but is not a full proof
the kind of file does not matter: .md, .markdown, .rst and .txt files no run read all let the result be reused
changes to VBW's own .vbw/ files, alone or with documentation, still allow the reuse
a committed change to a code file the test command read makes it run, even with documentation changes after it
a documentation or test file the test command read makes it run, even when it is a Markdown file no check lists
a Markdown file an approved check lists and reads makes that check run, and a file a check names in its run words but never opens makes nothing run
uncommitted changes to code in the working folder make nothing run: the proof runs on the committed code
a change to the test command's words makes it run
a failed latest test-command run is never reused
a quick command run standing in for the test command is never reused as the test result
a second vbw prove with nothing committed since the passing proof runs everything fresh (D173)
an unfinished or interrupted earlier proof (its marker left behind) is never reused
vbw prove --full reuses nothing: after a documentation-only commit it runs every check and every command
vbw qa record and vbw ship accept a proof with the reused test result, and vbw qa record still refuses a proof in which the quick command stood in

docs/proof.md explains that a proof reuses the test command's result when nothing it read changed, never by the kind of file, what still makes it run, and that vbw prove --full reuses nothing, with the documentation-only rule and its limit gone
docs/record.md describes how the reused test result is kept in the evidence

requirements.text: A phase that was escalated (raised after a blocked plan, a failed fix or a failed QA) is verified at the QA depth of its raised tier; the small-change discount applies only to phases that never escalated

rules.text: a phase with at least one escalation gets its raised tier's cell depth at the qa step, whatever its number of files
an escalated phase of at most two files is not lowered to quick
an escalated phase of three to nine files with no risk path is not capped at standard
the depth never goes above what the profile's cell gives the raised tier
a phase that never escalated keeps the discount: at most two files quick, three to nine at most standard
a tier forced with vbw config rigor and never escalated counts as never escalated
a blocked plan, a fix needing another round and a failed QA each lead to the raised depth
the QA round's tier reflects the raised depth when an escalated phase is among those to verify

requirements.text: vbw todo add, sort, done and drop commit the record when they change it, so the project is left clean, and never take the user's own staged files with them

rules.text: vbw todo add, with or without --sort and --size, commits the record and the commit names the new item
vbw todo sort, done and drop commit the record and the commit names the item and what happened to it
files the user staged stay staged, unchanged, and are not part of VBW's commit
files the user changed but did not stage, VBW's spec included, are not part of VBW's commit
vbw todo list never commits
a command that changes nothing makes no commit
a refused command (unknown id, a closed item, wrong usage) changes nothing and commits nothing
when git cannot commit (a failing hook, no git identity) the change is kept, the command succeeds and a warning gives git's reason and says to commit the files yourself
the commit goes through record_commit, not a second copy

requirements.text: By default VBW runs at most as many checks at once as the machine can carry (about three quarters of its processor cores, at least one), instead of 4 on every machine; the check_jobs setting still overrides it

rules.text: with no setting the limit is three quarters of the processor cores, rounded down, at least 1
the machine default is never more than 64
a core count that cannot be read gives 1 and VBW keeps working
a proof with no setting runs at most the machine default at once
check_jobs N (1 to 64) overrides the machine default, default returns to it, and invalid values are refused
vbw config shows the value in use and whether it is the machine default or set
docs/proof.md describes the machine-sized default
the old 'default 4' wording is gone from docs, help and code comments
a core count that is not a whole number (10.5, 12abc, 08) gives a limit of 1 and VBW keeps working

requirements.text: When several Devs or fix groups work at once, the checks they run together stay within that same machine-sized limit, and fix groups share one run of the project test command instead of each running it

rules.text: several vbw check processes at once never run more checks together than the limit
vbw prove beside vbw check processes share the same limit
with check_jobs 1 only one check runs at a time across processes
a check waiting for a free slot waits instead of failing, and its timeout counts from its real start
a slot held by a VBW process that died is freed
checks marked alone still run with nothing else beside checks from other processes
every Dev of a fix round is told not to run the project's test command or its quick command, only its own checks
every Dev of a fix round is told the whole test command runs once, in the proof after the round
a fix for a failure of the test command itself may run only the failing tests it needs
the Dev instructions say this
docs/proof.md describes the shared limit and docs/workflows.md the single test run of a fix round
the check_jobs limit is read once per process, so a setting changed while checks run does not change how many run at once

requirements.text: Every vbw command works on a project whose record (.vbw/record.json) is larger than the operating system's command-line limit (over 1 MB, as long-lived projects reach): no record-sized data is ever passed to a helper program as a command-line argument

rules.text: On a record over 2 MB (history lists and one field each over 128 KB), status, next, spec check, triage, todo list, config, interview and every show view answer exactly as on the equivalent small record
spec sync, spec add, apply, apply --patch and approve behave the same on the large record
A whole build (run start/confirm/end, commit, plan done/block/reset), check, prove and prove --full behave the same on the large record, whose proof results alone exceed 128 KB
tier raise, qa finding and qa record, fix done, req accept and req reject behave the same on the large record
decide, todo add/sort/done/drop and recommend behave the same on the large record
No command prints 'Argument list too long' on the large record
A write on the large record leaves valid JSON with the change and every earlier entry, nothing lost or cut
The commits a write makes on the large record hold only the record and the files the command names, the same as on the small record
The session-start hook, the Bash and file guards and the approve hooks answer the same on the large record, with and without a run, and print no error
The status line and the panel show the same on the large record and print no error
tools/bench-hooks.sh measures every guard input and the status line on a record over 2 MB; whether they are within their limits is judged in the release run, not in vbw prove
No shipped shell line hands the record or a value built from all of it to jq through --arg, --argjson, --args/--jsonargs or a here-string
The rule's self-tests catch every planted violation (the record, values derived from it, a function's RECORD parameter) and let pipes, --slurpfile, --rawfile, small values and comments pass

docs/record.md says a record of any size is supported and why

requirements.text: A guard's cost per tool call stays within its budget however long the record grows: every record that has checks keeps the protected check files as one short list near its top (record format 4), and the guards read only that list, never the checks themselves; there is one way to read it, with no size threshold

rules.text: vbw init and every later write leave schema 4 with keys schema, lease, protected, checks first
with 0, 1, 50, 51 or 2,000 checks the record is format 4
a record with no checks carries an empty protected list
a record with checks carries every check file once, in sorted order
a check with no files adds nothing and a file several checks share appears once
a contract change that edits or removes a check drops the files no remaining check names, in the same write
a contract change that adds or edits a check adds the newly named files, in the same write
a record an older VBW wrote (schema 1, 2 or 3, no list) is read by every command without a corrupt error
the next write turns an older record into format 4 and keeps every other entry unchanged
there is no migration command
a schema-4 record without the list is corrupt for every command, which names protected
a list that differs from the checks' files (missing, extra, out of order, repeated, not a list) is corrupt, naming protected
a record below schema 4 that carries a protected list is corrupt
record.sh and record.jq hold no 50-check threshold
under a build or fix run an agent's Edit, Write or Bash change of a listed file is refused with today's message
under a build or fix run an unprotected file the run may write is not refused
the main conversation, another session and calls outside a run get the same answers on format 4 and on an older record
under a build or fix run an agent's file write on a record without the list is refused, saying it must first be saved by this VBW
a file named only under checks, not on the list, is not seen by the guards
common.jq has no code that reads the checks and no 50-check threshold
a VBW that reads up to schema 3 says the project needs a newer VBW on every record this VBW writes, and never calls it corrupt
the status line shows the same on a format-4 record with 0 and 60 checks as on schema 3, with no error
the panel shows the same on a format-4 record with 0 and 60 checks as on schema 3, with no error
the session-start hook says the same on a format-4 record as on schema 3
the hook benchmark measures every guard input on records of 51, 500 and 2,000 checks against one hook limit, judged in the release run, not in vbw prove
docs/record.md describes format 4 for every record with protected after lease, and says older records are read and converted on their next write
docs/guards.md describes one read path, the protected list, and the refusal on a record without it
neither guide mentions a 50-check threshold or this VBW writing schemas 1 to 3
vbw init and every command that writes the record rewrite the glance in the same locked write, holding the record's schema, lease and protected list exactly, besides the status line's fields
the glance the kernel writes is newer than the record even when both are written within the same second
a failed glance write leaves the record write done and the guards reading the record, never the glance written before it
after the record changes outside vbw, the next vbw command rewrites the glance from the record
while the glance is current the guards answer from it alone with a normal jq parse, never reading the record
a missing glance, or one that is not a readable file, not JSON, empty, or lacks schema, lease or protected, gives the answers of the record
a glance that is not newer than the record gives the answers of the record

after git checkout, git reset or a hand edit of the record (in place or saved as a new file) within the glance's own second, the guards answer from the record, for a changed lease and a changed protected list

with no run, a plan, build or fix run, another session's run and the main conversation, the guards give identical answers from the glance and from the record for protected check files, files outside the run, secret files, the record and the consent file
a forged glance with an empty protected list or no lease, older than the record, changes no answer

under a plan, qa, map, build or fix run an agent's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or Bash write of the glance (redirect, cp, tee, sed -i, a program) is refused, saying it is written only by vbw, as for the record
outside a run the main conversation's write of the glance is not refused
outside a VBW project the guards give no answer and print no error, with or without a stray glance
hooks.json, the doctor's guard self-test and the guards' jq files hold no --stream and common.jq no event-stream code; the doctor's guard self-test passes with and without a glance
docs/guards.md says the guards read .vbw/runtime/glance.json and read .vbw/record.json when the glance is missing, not newer, or the record changed by a checkout or a hand edit
docs/guards.md and docs/record.md say the glance is never the source of truth
docs/record.md says the glance holds schema, lease and protected for the guards
no guide says the guards stream the record or read only its beginning

requirements.text: VBW's speed checks fail only on a real slowdown: a hook's own cost above 20 ms per call, or the status line above 60 ms; when the machine is too busy to measure (starting the shell and jq alone takes longer than the hook limit) the check reports the machine as busy and does not fail

rules.text: a guard whose own cost (its CPU time minus the sh and jq startup) is above 20 ms per call fails the bench, and the line names the input, the cost and the 20 ms limit
a hook doing extra work well over 20 ms on a quiet machine still fails the bench: a real slowdown is caught
a guard whose own cost is at or below 20 ms per call passes, and the old relative limit (1x the startup) is gone
the status line above 60 ms per call fails the bench on the small record and on the record over 2 MB, the line naming the cost and the 60 ms limit
without settings the limits are 20 ms per hook call and 60 ms for the status line
when the sh and jq startup alone is above the hook limit, the bench prints that the machine is too busy to measure, with the startup and the limit, judges nothing and exits 0
with a startup below the limit the same run judges every guard and the status line as usual
VBW_HOOK_BUDGET_MS and VBW_STATUSLINE_BUDGET_MS override the two limits, and the busy threshold follows the hook limit
CI sets no hook or status line limit of its own: it runs with the local defaults
docs/guards.md states 20 ms per hook call and the busy-machine report, and no 8 ms or relative limit
docs/statusline.md states 60 ms and no 30 ms limit
the hot-path rule in CLAUDE.md states 20 ms per hook call, 60 ms for the status line and the busy report, and neither 8 ms nor 30 ms

requirements.text: The timed speed checks run once per release (in CI and in the local run before a push), not in every vbw prove, so a proof never fails or waits because the machine is busy

rules.text: bash tools/test.sh with no option runs the lint and every test file except tests/timed-*.bats, and neither tools/bench-hooks.sh nor tools/bench-panel.sh
bash tools/test.sh --release runs the lint, both benchmarks, every other test file in one parallel batch, then the timed files alone
the release run fails when a benchmark, the batch or a timed file fails
bash tools/test.sh --quick still runs, without the benchmarks and without any timed file
the CI shards together make one release run: shard 1 runs both benchmarks and every timed file runs alone after its shard's batch
--release with any other argument exits 2 with the usage line and runs nothing
CI runs the release way: the jobs without a shard run bash tools/test.sh --release and the shard jobs their share
no test file of the default run measures a duration (the bash or wall clock, or a speed benchmark at its real limit); the 24-check proof time and the 50,000-file scan time are timed tests
docs/proof.md says the timed speed checks run in bash tools/test.sh --release and that vbw prove does not run them
the testing section of CLAUDE.md names the release run, says vbw prove does not run the timed checks, and makes it the local run before a push
CONTRIBUTING.md names the release run as the local run before a push

requirements.text: vbw prove never stops a project's test command only because the machine is busy: its time limit fits a large project's full test run on a loaded machine, and a project can set its own limit

rules.text: without a setting vbw config shows 3600 seconds and vbw prove gives the test command 3600 seconds (60 minutes) before stopping it
vbw config set command_timeout SECONDS sets the project's own limit; vbw config shows it and later runs keep and use it
vbw config set command_timeout default returns to 3600 seconds
vbw prove stops the test command at the project's limit and records it as timeout
the report of a stop says the test command was stopped by its time limit, names the limit in use and says vbw config set command_timeout raises it
a limit that is not a whole number, is zero, negative or above 86400 is refused with a message naming 1 to 86400 and changes nothing
a test command that ends within the limit is recorded as before: pass, or fail with its exit code
a check's own timeout is unchanged: its default stays 300 seconds and its timeout field still stops it
docs/proof.md states the default limit, 3600 seconds (60 minutes), and no longer 900 seconds
docs/proof.md says how a project sets its own limit, the range 1 to 86400 and how to return to the default
docs/proof.md says what a stop by the limit looks like and how to raise the limit
a command stopped by its limit is reported with the limit in use, never the seconds it was measured to run

requirements.text: vbw config rigor works under macOS /bin/bash 3.2: setting a mode re-tiers the unstarted phases and saves the record, as it does under bash 5

rules.text: under /bin/bash, vbw config rigor deep and then auto succeed, re-tier the unstarted phase and save the setting

requirements.text: VBW's own test suite passes under macOS /bin/bash 3.2: a test that edits the record by hand also drops the status line's side file, as a kernel write would refresh it

rules.text: the rigor and QA-model tests that edit the record by hand pass when bats runs under /bin/bash

requirements.text: A milestone can re-plan a requirement it reopened from a shipped milestone: a full vbw apply accepts phases that cover it, and every vbw apply refusal names the mode it came from (full apply, --add or --patch)

rules.text: a shipped requirement whose text changes in the spec is reopened: vbw spec sync moves it to the current milestone with status open
a full apply whose new phase covers a requirement reopened by a text change is accepted
a full apply whose new phase covers a requirement reopened by a proof type change is accepted
after that apply the shipped phase keeps its id, title, requirements, goal, criteria, tier and every plan with its status
a full apply covering a shipped requirement that was not reopened is refused, naming the requirement and its milestone
full apply refusals name 'full apply': input that is not JSON, an unknown field, an invalid tier, an open run, a changed started plan, a missing rule, a tier below its floor
--add refusals name '--add': not JSON, an unknown field, an invalid tier, a phase id in use, a missing rule, a tier below its floor, an open run
--patch refusals name '--patch': not JSON, phases in a patch, an unknown field, a changed started plan, a rule naming no check, an open run
an unknown option prints the usage line naming the three modes and exits 2, changing nothing

requirements.text: A re-plan can add a new phase for more work on a requirement that a started phase already covers; the started phase and its finished plans stay exactly as they are

rules.text: a full apply that keeps a started phase and adds a new phase for its requirement is accepted
vbw apply --add with a new phase for a requirement a started phase covers is accepted

after a full apply the started phase keeps id, title, requirements, goal, criteria, tier, reasons, predicted tier and escalations, and its started plan keeps phase, requirements, files, order, tasks and status
the same holds after vbw apply --add
a phase with an escalation and no started plan counts as started and keeps its tier and escalations
a re-plan that drops a started plan is refused, naming the plan
a re-plan that changes a started plan is refused, naming the plan

requirements.text: A re-plan can change the goal and criteria of a phase that has not started

rules.text: changing only the goal of a phase that has not started is accepted; its id, title, requirements and plans stay
changing only the criteria of a phase that has not started is accepted
changing both goal and criteria of a phase that has not started is accepted
changing the goal of a started phase is refused, naming the phase and pointing to a new phase
changing the criteria of a started phase is refused, naming the phase and pointing to a new phase
a phase with an escalation counts as started even when every plan is planned
vbw apply --patch still refuses any phase change

requirements.text: A re-plan never raises the tier of a phase that has started or finished; the minimum rigor is judged for unstarted phases only

rules.text: a started phase whose signals now call for a higher tier is not refused and keeps its tier, reasons and predicted tier
the same holds when the re-plan gives the started phase no tier
a finished phase (every plan done) keeps its tier, reasons and predicted tier
with the tier forced to deep, a started phase keeps its tier and a phase that has not started gets deep
with the tier forced to express, a started phase keeps its tier and a phase that has not started gets express
with the tier forced to standard, a finished escalated phase keeps its tier and reasons

an escalation is never lowered by a re-plan, in automatic or forced mode

requirements.text: A fix that follows a QA finding can add its regression test: the fix run may create new test files, registered as checks of the finding's requirement, and edits to an approved check file wait for one approval by the user before the proof

rules.text: during a fix run for a QA finding the Dev may create a new test file, with a file tool or Bash
during that run the Dev may edit an approved check file of the finding's requirement
a check file of another requirement stays blocked; the message names it and gives the next step
vbw fix check registers the new test as a check of the finding's requirement, and vbw show req names the fix it came from
one approval question names every new or changed check file of the fix, and nothing runs them before it
without the approval vbw prove runs none of them, names the waiting files and the next step, and the fix stays open
once approved, vbw prove runs the new test
a later change to an approved test waits for a new approval (consent by content hash)
outside fix runs for QA findings (a build run, a fix run the proof opened, another session) check files stay protected as before

requirements.text: A [human] requirement the user wants to judge later can move to the next milestone, keeping its id, its checks and its history

rules.text: the verify and vibe skills keep the three answers, and Skip for now is recorded with vbw req skip
with nothing skipped, vbw next asks for the verdict as before
when only skipped [human] requirements remain, vbw next offers to ship and names them (detail.later)
no such offer while other work remains
judging now changes nothing in the record
shipping now counts only what was proven or accepted and names the moved requirement
after vbw milestone start the moved requirement is in the new milestone, open, with the same id, text, proof, rules and history
in the new milestone vbw next offers the moved requirement for judgement
the spec line stays as it was and vbw spec sync neither resets nor duplicates the moved requirement
an [auto] requirement is never skipped or moved
a [human] requirement with an open fix from the user's rejection does not move

requirements.text: Every refusal VBW gives while a plan changes (vbw apply, vbw run start, the guards) says what to do instead

rules.text: every refusal of a full apply ends with its next step ('Next: ...')
every refusal of vbw apply --add ends with its next step
every refusal of vbw apply --patch ends with its next step
every refusal of vbw run start ends with its next step, including a run open in this session or another one

every block of the file and Bash guards (secret files, the record, the consent file, the status file, another session's files, protected check files, files outside the plan, read-only runs, vbw approve by an agent) ends with its next step
a guard that failed during a run blocks with a next step

requirements.text: --help or -h on any vbw command prints that command's usage and changes nothing (no record write, no commit)

rules.text: the test walks the kernel's dispatch list, so a new command without help fails
vbw CMD --help and -h print the command's usage on stdout, exit 0 and change nothing, for every dispatched command
the flag right after a subcommand prints the usage and does not do the subcommand's work
help works while a run is open and from a session that does not own it
help works outside a VBW project and creates nothing
a text argument that only contains --help is still taken as text

requirements.text: Before a push, the release run adds only the timed speed checks and the benchmarks when a passing full proof already covers the same code (only version files and the changelog changed since); otherwise it runs everything

rules.text: with only the version files and the changelog changed since a passing full proof, the release run runs only the benchmarks and timed files and names the proof
the same holds when the version change is committed
any other changed file, committed or not, runs everything and names it
a new untracked file runs everything and names it
with no proof recorded the release run runs everything and says why
when the last full proof failed the release run runs everything and says why
a partial proof never counts as a full one
a failing benchmark or timed check still fails the shorter run
the CI shards run their whole share whatever proof is recorded

requirements.text: During a VBW run, a VBW guard that crashes, cannot start or times out blocks the action it guards instead of letting it through; outside VBW projects and outside runs nothing changes

rules.text: during a run a guard that crashes blocks the write or command, saying the guard failed and to run vbw doctor
during a run a guard whose file is missing or unreadable blocks
during a run a guard that cannot start because jq is missing blocks
during a run a guard past its time limit is stopped and the action blocked; docs/guards.md states the limit
during a run a record the guard must read and cannot parse blocks the action
in a VBW project with no open run a failing guard lets the action through as before
outside VBW projects a failing or missing guard changes nothing and prints nothing
with intact guards a run gets their ordinary answers, and the doctor's guard self-test passes

requirements.text: Every proof, including the full proof that QA and shipping require, re-runs only the checks a change can affect and reuses the passing result of every other check; a check is affected when a file it lists or a project file it reads has changed since its last pass

rules.text: A check whose test reads a project file it does not declare runs again when a commit changes only that file (the case D181 missed)
A commit that changes only files no check read reuses every check, each naming the proof it came from

vbw qa record, vbw next and vbw ship accept a proof that reused results and no longer demand vbw prove --full
vbw fix done picks checks with the same rule: a finished requirement's check runs when a file it read changed, even one no plan of the fix lists, and an unaffected check is reused

Recording read lists adds no tracing tool as a runtime dependency

requirements.text: The project's test command re-runs only the test files a change can affect when the project's test runner can run single test files; otherwise it runs whole; a one-file fix in VBW itself proves in minutes, not the whole suite

rules.text: With an approved single-file form each test file runs on its own and the whole test command does not run
