The Lead's proposal through vbw apply is written into the spec's Test files section for the user to approve
A change to a file read by one test file runs only that test file and reuses the others, naming their proof (a one-file fix proves in minutes, not the whole suite)
A new or changed test file runs
A test file whose last result failed runs again though nothing it read changed
Deleting a file a test file read, or adding a file to a folder it listed, runs that test file
Test files run several at a time
A failing test file fails the proof and the proof names it
A test file an approved check runs runs only as that check, and neither the test command nor the quick command runs beside an approved form
vbw prove --full runs every test file on its own and reuses none
VBW's spec declares bats on one file over every tracked tests/*.bats except the timed speed files
VBW's shell lint stays watched as its own project command, bash tools/test.sh --lint, which runs only shellcheck over tools/
The Lead proposes the single-file form through vbw apply, with the runner's documented syntax
docs/proof.md and docs/workflows.md explain the form, its approval, what happens without it and how test files are counted

requirements.text: When VBW cannot know what a change reaches, the proof runs everything and says why: the file system records no reads, this clone has no recorded run, the last proof was cut short, nothing was committed since the last passing proof, or a file was added or deleted that no recorded run read or listed the folder of; a changed approved command, single-file form or list of test files re-runs only what runs through it; the proof summary says how many checks and test files ran and how many were reused

rules.text: when the file system does not record which files are read, the proof runs everything and says so
a clone with no earlier recorded run runs everything and says so
a proof that was cut short makes the next proof run everything and say so
an added or deleted file that no recorded run read and no recorded run listed the folder of runs everything, and the summary names it
a content change to a file no recorded run read runs nothing
a changed approved command, single-file form or list of test files re-runs only what runs through it, never everything
several causes are each listed, one per line, under one ran everything line
every summary, full or not, prints checks: N ran, M reused and test files: N ran, M reused, and a reused result names its proof
docs/proof.md lists every cause with the message the summary shows, both counts, and that a changed command, form or test list re-runs only its own units

requirements.text: When the declared test-file form leaves no file to run as a unit of its own (every file it matches already runs as an approved check), the proof records no nameless unit, counts the test command as covered by those checks, and says so; when the form matches no tracked file at all, the proof fails the test command and names the form

rules.text: every file the form matches runs as an approved check: the proof passes the test command as covered, records no nameless unit, and the summary says why no test file ran
the form matches no tracked file: the proof fails the test command, names the pathspecs and opens the fix
a matching file added later runs as a unit of its own

requirements.text: Before a push, the release run reuses the last proof when it passed, left no command skipped and no quick command standing in, and only the version files and the changelog changed since, whether or not it reused earlier results (a reused result is one the read lists still vouch for); it then runs only the benchmarks and the timed speed checks; otherwise it runs everything and says why

rules.text: a passing proof that reused results is reused by the release run: only the benchmarks and the timed files run, and the proof is named
a proof that skipped a command not yet approved is not reused, and the reason says so
a proof where the quick command stood in for the test command is not reused, and the reason says so

requirements.text: While the contract cannot be approved yet (a check file is missing, the spec and the record differ), vbw next does not offer the approval question: it says the contract is not ready, names each problem and the step that fixes it, so the user is never asked to approve a contract that approval would refuse

rules.text: a check file that does not exist yet gives no approval question: action contract, not gated, the problem and the next step named
a spec edited and not synced gives no approval question and names vbw spec sync
several problems are all listed
once every problem is fixed the approval question comes as before, and an approved contract is not examined again
vbw approve still refuses an unready contract

requirements.text: The test helper leaves the repository before its git calls and turns off background git work (garbage collection, maintenance), and the test that checks this runs the helper in a plain shell, never a bats run inside a bats run, so the suite gives the same result on macOS bash 3.2 and on Linux bash 5

rules.text: a helper that reads the repository it runs from is seen and fails the check, and the current helper passes it, run in a plain shell
the helper turns off gc and maintenance in the test gitconfig

requirements.text: VBW records what each run and each milestone cost in tokens and money, from the facts Claude Code provides, so the kernel can read the totals per run and per milestone and compare them with a ceiling

rules.text: each status line render in a VBW project writes the session's figures (session, usd, in, out, at) to .vbw/runtime/cost.SESSION.json by temporary name and rename, never the record; no cost field leaves it unchanged; an unwritable folder still renders; an unsafe session id writes nothing
vbw run start keeps the opening figures on the lease; vbw run end appends the run with cost end minus start and commits it with the record
a run with no figures at start or end, or no session id, is recorded with cost null, never 0
the active milestone's total is the sum over sessions, from first figure without a baseline; vbw ship freezes it; vbw milestone start records baselines; no spend counts twice
vbw show costs prints the totals, the sessions seen and each run's share in plain words; --json returns one object with milestones, runs and what is unknown, with the remedy, never a guess
vbw show costs --ceiling USD: exit 0 under, exit 1 reached at or above, exit 1 cannot tell with no figure; a USD that is not a positive number is a usage error (exit 2) that changes nothing

the validator accepts well-formed cost data (frozen total, unknown cost and lease.cost included) and refuses unknown keys, bad kinds, missing fields, bad times, negative or non-numeric figures and unknown milestone ids as corrupt; a record without cost data stays valid
only kernel commands write cost data to the record: the status line script never names the record as a write target

a real-session scenario with the status line on ends with vbw show costs --json reporting a known, non-zero cost for the run and the milestone, of the same order as /cost, saved under tools/l3-results
docs/record.md documents the costs field, lease.cost and the schema; docs/statusline.md the side file; docs/costs.md the command, its JSON, the ceiling and unknown

requirements.text: vbw approve compares every section of the spec with the record, the Test results list included, so an edited list that was not synced cannot be approved as the record's list

rules.text: a Test results list that differs from the record (folder added, removed or renamed, section removed or added) is refused by vbw approve with exit 1 and both lines, and no decision, commit or consent is written
the same unsynced edit makes vbw next say the contract is not ready and name vbw spec sync, never the approval question
no section and no folders compare equal; the same folders in the same order compare equal; another order or a missing side does not
after vbw spec sync the same vbw approve proceeds
an unsynced edit in each section (Requirements, Commands, Test files, Test results) is refused, one test per section
docs/proof.md names the four sections compared and says an unsynced spec cannot be approved

requirements.text: The proof's cause "nothing was committed since the last passing proof" fires only when the project's code is the code that proof proved (its recorded tree), never from the subject of the last commit, so a record commit landing after other commits does not re-run everything

rules.text: the cause fires only when the last proof passed, the project's files equal evidence.tree and the committed code equals evidence.head; the commit subject is never read
T116: a proof passes, code commits land, a record commit with the proof's subject lands last: the next vbw prove names no such cause and re-runs only the units that read the change
a second vbw prove right after a passing proof with nothing changed names the cause and runs everything (D173)
vbw fix done never names the cause and reuses every unchanged pass right after a passing proof (D270)

the reuse rule's reason 'proving again with nothing committed' comes from the same tree comparison, and no code in plugin/lib reads the commit subject (the proof commit's words appear only where the commit message is written)
with no evidence, or a last proof that did not pass, the cause never fires
docs/proof.md's causes table and D173 paragraph state the rule as the trees of the last passing proof, never the commit subject

requirements.text: vbw fix done prints what it ran and what it reused, checks and test files, with the counts the proof summary prints, and saves the test files it ran in the run store so the next proof reuses them

rules.text: one line per check that ran: id, status, seconds and 'ran: <reason>'; a failing one adds the last line of its output
a reused check keeps its line with the time of the pass it reused
one line per test file that ran, a passing one included; a failing one adds the last line of its output
after the per-unit lines, 'checks: N ran, M reused' (N + M = candidate checks) and 'test files: N ran, M reused' print every time, as 0 ran, 0 reused when nothing was judged
a fix of the test command judges every test file of the form by the one reuse rule: the failed file runs, a changed file runs, the rest are reused and counted
every test file fix done runs is saved in the clone's run store and the next vbw prove shows it as reused (proof of <time>)
a cause prints once as 'every candidate check runs: <cause>' and the count lines still print the true numbers
closing outcomes and the exit code are unchanged: fixed, closed, broke finished work, still failing, non-zero when any fix could not close
docs/proof.md's vbw fix done section shows the per-unit lines and the two count lines

requirements.text: During a run, VBW's guards deny any write by an agent to a path outside the project folder (a file write or a shell redirect, /tmp included), saying where the run may write instead; outside runs and outside VBW projects nothing changes

rules.text: a file write to a path outside the project during a run is denied, naming the path, with a next step
a shell redirect to a path outside the project during a run is denied the same way
a relative path that climbs out of the project is denied; inside the project the lease rules decide as before
no run open, or outside a VBW project: the guards give no answer
docs/guards.md states the rule

requirements.text: With vbw loop start ITEM... --ceiling USD the user delegates approval to the loop for the named backlog items: a contract whose requirements are exactly those items (their recorded text, nothing more) is approved by the kernel without a question, recorded as approved by the loop on the user's behalf; any other contract still waits for the user

rules.text: vbw loop start ITEM... with a ceiling choice records the loop in the record and commits it: the items in the order given with a snapshot of each one's backlog text, the ceiling and its mode, the session, the start time and every known session's figures as the baseline; vbw loop status prints all of it from any session

the ceiling is the user's choice at start: --ceiling USD, --ceiling USD --finish-item or --no-ceiling; with none of them, with --finish-item alone, or with a USD that is not a positive number the loop refuses to start as a usage error (exit 2) and nothing changes

no item, an unknown item, a closed item, the same item twice, a loop already on (naming vbw loop stop), a current milestone with requirements that is not shipped, or --ceiling with no cost figure (naming vbw statusline on or --no-ceiling) is refused with what to do instead, and nothing changes

vbw loop stop from the starting session or any other session marks the loop stopping with the time and the session and vbw loop status says so; with no loop on it says so and exits 0; a second stop changes nothing; the loop step reads the stop from the record before its next step, after a running workflow of its own session has ended

a contract whose requirements are exactly the loop's items (every requirement's text equals one item's recorded text, each item matched at most once, nothing else but a [human] requirement an earlier ship carried over) is approved by the kernel's loop step without a question: consent for the fingerprint, the shape, the approved-contract snapshot, the project commands and the test-file form, as vbw approve writes them

the delegated approval is recorded as approved by the loop on the user's behalf: a decision naming the loop's start time, the items and the fingerprint, and the approval commit; vbw next then moves past approve, and a second step approves nothing again

any other contract waits for the user as today: a text differing by one character, an extra requirement, a requirement matching an item not on this loop's list, no loop on, a stopping loop, or a contract that is not ready (a missing check file, spec and record differing); vbw next answers approve or contract, nothing is approved, no consent is granted, no decision is recorded

the approval by delegation happens only inside the kernel's loop step: the Bash guard denies vbw loop start, vbw loop next and vbw loop park from any tool call with pinned texts while stop, status and help stay allowed; the /vbw:loop skill is user-invoked only and arms the loop in its preamble with the user's own arguments; no other skill arms it

vbw loop status shows the spend so far (the sum over known sessions of the current figures minus the baseline, computed as a milestone's total), the ceiling, and one word: under, reached, or cannot tell; cannot tell counts as reached under a ceiling and not with --no-ceiling

vbw loop --help and vbw help list the command, its sub-commands and the three ceiling forms; docs/loop.md documents start, stop, status, the ceiling modes and the exact delegated approval rule with its decision text and consent entry; the record's format validates the loop field and docs/record.md describes it

requirements.text: /vbw:loop runs the unattended cycle for the loop's items in order (milestone, plan, approve by delegation, build, prove, fix, QA, ship): an escalated fix is retried once, then its item is parked with the reason and the loop moves to the next item; a [human] requirement is skipped for the user to judge later; the loop stops at the cost ceiling, at the end of its list, or when the user runs vbw loop stop from any session, and leaves .vbw/loop-report.md saying what shipped, what was parked and why, and what it cost

rules.text: /vbw:loop arms the loop with the user's own arguments and shows in one message the items in order, the ceiling and its mode, that approval is delegated for these items only, what never happens and how to stop from any session; /vbw:loop stop runs vbw loop stop and says what the loop was doing; the steps are the router's, run the same way; the loop never asks under guided autonomy, takes planning decisions with the recommended option recorded as chosen by the loop, accepts no suggestion, never runs vbw auto on, never approves and never asks the approval menu

one kernel command, vbw loop next --json, does every step that needs no agent: it opens the item's milestone titled with the item (vbw milestone start, or renamed when empty), adds the item's text as its one requirement ([auto], or [human] for a backlog text starting with [human]), marks the item in progress, approves by delegation, ships, marks the backlog entry done, opens the next item and answers done at the end of the list; plan, build, fix, qa and prove come back as vbw next gives them with the same detail, rigor, effort and profile fields; vbw next stays pure; a run the loop opens carries the same lease as any run and ends through vbw run end; the loop never calls vbw approve

the Stop hook gate drives the cycle in the loop's own session: it blocks the stop with the next loop step, never counts it against autonomy_cap, asks for nothing while this session's proof runs in the background, and lets the session stop with one message once the loop reports done or stopped; in any other session the gate ignores the loop

a [human] requirement at the accept step is skipped by the loop, never accepted or rejected on the user's behalf; the ship moves it to the next milestone and the report lists it as waiting for the user's judgment

with the default ceiling the loop stops before a step at or above the ceiling, or when the spend cannot be told, with that reason; with --finish-item the item runs on to its ship and then the loop stops; with --no-ceiling there is no comparison; the loop stops at the end of its list and on vbw loop stop from any session, naming the user and the session; a running workflow is never killed; an action the loop cannot do, or a run of another session, stops the loop with the reason, the item and the step, recorded in the loop state

.vbw/loop-report.md is written when the loop ends and refreshed each time an item ends: what shipped (item, milestone, requirement, the commits), what waits for the user (skipped [human] requirements, the stop reason) and what it cost (the total and each item in dollars and tokens, unknown where no figure was seen, never 0 or an estimate); the record stores the same facts and vbw loop status after the end says the loop ended, why, and names the report

docs/loop.md describes the cycle, the stops, the report and the skill; docs/next.md names the loop step and that vbw next is unchanged; docs/workflows.md and README say the loop's steps are not counted against autonomy_cap

the first escalation of an item is retried with vbw fix retry and recorded against the item, and a blocked plan is reset once; a second escalation, a plan blocked again or a scope violation parks the item: its commits since the milestone began are reverted with git revert commits (history kept, a user-edited or untracked file left as it is), its requirement, phases, plans, checks, rules and fixes are removed with its spec line and check file, the milestone is parked with the reason and its cost frozen, a decision names the item, the reason, the revert commits and how to bring the work back, the backlog entry stays open, the record is committed and the next item starts; after a park vbw prove passes the earlier checks, vbw next offers the next milestone, vbw status and vbw show roadmap show the parked milestone, and vbw loop park by hand with no item in progress refuses
vbw loop park is callable only by the loop step: the Bash guard denies it from any tool call, an agent's or the main session's, with the pinned text, with or without a loop on and with a stale glance

the report's parked section names each parked item, its reason, its revert commits and how to bring the work back; the loop's total cost includes parked items' cost and the record stores the item's reverts and cost

requirements.text: The loop never pushes, releases or publishes: nothing it does leaves the project, every ship stays local for the user's review, and the guards that hold for any run hold for the loop's runs

rules.text: while a loop is on the Bash guard denies for every caller, the main session included, git push in any form, gh release, gh pr create, npm publish, cargo publish, twine upload, gem push, docker push and the deploy commands of vercel, netlify, fly, heroku and wrangler, each saying the loop never leaves the project and naming /vbw:loop stop with a pinned text, from the glance or the record alike; words in text, reads and the project's own commands stay allowed; once the loop has ended or outside a loop today's rules stand and a plain git push stays allowed; the hook bench measures the loop case
vbw ship run by the loop makes no tag, no push and no call to a remote: with a remote configured the remote's refs and the tags are unchanged after a loop's ship

the guards that hold for any run hold for the loop's runs: under a loop with a lease open a builder is denied the record, a path outside the project, a protected check file, vbw approve, git commit and git push, while the plan's own file stays writable

tools/l3-suite.sh has a loop scenario (two backlog items, one that ships and one whose fix escalates twice and parks, a small ceiling) in its default list and header, writing its own honestly labelled result, with the outcome checked in the record, the report file and git; docs/loop.md, docs/guards.md and README describe the loop, its limits and the promise: nothing approved without a record of who approved it, nothing leaving the project

requirements.text: Machine-wide limit (owner, 2026-10-12 09:40): VBW as a whole never takes more than about three quarters of the machine's cores, however many projects, sessions and runs are proving at once: one shared budget per machine (a slot store in the user's Claude config folder, each unit of a proof or fix done takes a slot, a run that finds none waits its turn), so runs take turns instead of fighting (today a 12-minute fix done took 87 under four concurrent runs). Same tests, same results, no thrash; the check_jobs setting stays as a per-run cap below it. Goes with T127 (one fix done per fix round). First item after 2.0.34, before the loop

rules.text: the machine limit is three quarters of the processor cores (vbw_cores), rounded down, at least 1 and at most 64
a core count that cannot be read gives a machine limit of 1
the machine limit is not a setting: vbw config refuses one and check_jobs does not change it
the slot store is <claude-config-dir>/vbw/slots.json: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.config/claude-code when it exists, else ~/.claude
one kernel function (vbw_claude_dir) finds the Claude config folder and the status line's settings lookup uses it
a run writes nothing outside the project but the slot store, and leaves no store behind once nothing holds or waits
tests use a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR inside their own folder, never the host's Claude config folder
the slot store code holds to the bash 3.2 floor and works under /bin/bash
a run whose check_jobs is above the limit runs exactly as many units at once as the limit
across two projects each proving 6 units plus a vbw fix done, never more unit commands run at once than the limit (3 with 4 cores)
project commands and test files each take a slot like checks
check_jobs stays a per-run cap below the limit: check_jobs 2 never runs more than 2 units at once
a check_jobs above the machine limit never lifts a proof above the limit
a unit gives its slot back when its command passes, fails or times out
a freed slot goes to the waiting run holding the fewest slots
between waiting runs holding the same number of slots, the one that waited longest goes first
an alone check keeps its per-project meaning, takes one machine slot, and an alone check in one project with shared checks in another both finish at limit 1
a vbw run inside a unit's command, on the same store, takes no slot of its own and never waits for its parent
a unit that waited reports the same status, exit code and output as alone, and its timeout counts from its command's start
the slots of a run killed outright are taken over by the next run to look at the store
a run interrupted with Ctrl-C ends and gives its slots back at once
the store's lock is taken over when its owner process is gone

when the store cannot be written, prove, check and fix done run to the end under check_jobs alone, results unaffected, and print once 'vbw: the computer-wide limit was not in force: cannot write PATH; this run was limited by check_jobs (N) alone'

a damaged store never stops a run: it runs under check_jobs, prints once 'vbw: the computer-wide limit was not in force: PATH is damaged (delete it to restore the limit); this run was limited by check_jobs (N) alone', and the file is left as it was
vbw prove, vbw check and vbw fix done whose units waited end with 'waited N s for other VBW runs on this computer (limit L of C cores)'
with an unreadable core count the waited line reads '(limit 1, as this computer's core count could not be read)'
a run that never waited prints no waited line: its output is unchanged
vbw config prints the machine limit right after check_jobs: three quarters of the cores, shared by every VBW project on this computer, not a setting
with check_jobs above the machine limit, the vbw config line says the machine limit applies; at or below it, it says nothing more
with an unreadable core count the vbw config line names limit 1 and why

docs/proof.md explains the limit, what takes a slot, where the store lives, equal turns, unchanged results and timeouts, recovery of gone runs, the unwritable or damaged store and the lines a run prints
CLAUDE.md names the slot store in <claude-config-dir>/vbw/ as the second exception to 'Nothing outside the project', with R181 as its source, and the user docs say the same

requirements.text: Several vbw fix done runs at once slow each other down (2026-10-12: three in parallel plus another session's run took a 12-minute run to 87 minutes). The fixing workflow has every Dev run its own fix done, so a round with several groups already runs several at once. Decide: the kernel serialises fix done runs (one proof lock per clone, the later ones wait and reuse), or the workflow runs one fix done for all groups at the end; measure first

rules.text: Before any change, a measurement is recorded as a decision naming the fixture (tools/measure-fix-round.sh with its parameters) and, for three groups each running its own vbw fix done, the wall-clock minutes, the checks and test files run, and how many ran more than once

The measuring tool runs one fix round on its fixture either per group (each group's own vbw fix done, all at once) or as one vbw fix done, and prints the minutes, the checks and test files run, and the count that ran more than once (0 for one vbw fix done)
The measuring tool refuses a missing or unknown mode and a group count below 1
After the change, a later decision supersedes the before measurement with the same fixture and the same before figures, plus the after figures of the same round, where 0 ran more than once
The decision names the chosen approach (one vbw fix done per round, run by the workflow after every Dev returns) and the rejected kernel lock, with reasons drawn from the measured figures
With N groups (N of 1 or more) the fixing workflow runs vbw fix done exactly once per round, after every Dev has returned
In a stubbed run with three groups the prompts hold exactly one instruction to run vbw fix done, and it lists every fix whose Dev reported done
No Dev prompt tells the Dev to run vbw fix done; each tells it to commit its fix and check it with vbw check on its own fixes' checks only, never the whole test command
plugin/agents/dev.md never tells the Dev to run vbw fix done, says the workflow runs it once for the round, and tells a fixing Dev to commit and check with vbw check
The closing Lead's own instructions (Close a run) include the round's vbw fix done, waited for to its end
A fix whose Dev reported blocked or stopped before reporting is left out of vbw fix done, and the workflow result and log name it with its status
When no Dev reported done, no vbw fix done runs
A blocked Dev's fix left out of the round's real vbw fix done stays open, and vbw run confirm names it
In the round's one vbw fix done, a fix with uncommitted changes stays open and is named, and the other fixes close
In the round's one vbw fix done, a fix whose files serve a failing check of finished work stays open and is named, and the other fixes close
In the round's one vbw fix done, a test-command fix whose test files still fail stays open and is named, and it closes once they pass
The workflow result says which fixes closed and which stayed open, each open fix with its reason, also in the log
Without a session (args.session missing) the one vbw fix done still runs, by an agent of its own, before the workflow returns

When the agent running the round's vbw fix done stops or reports a failure, with or without a session, the log gives the exact vbw fix done with the fix ids to run by hand, and the round is not complete

The instruction to run vbw fix done says it may pass one shell command's 10-minute limit, to wait for it in the background and read its whole output, and it comes before vbw run confirm and vbw run end
After the round, vbw run confirm counts every closed fix as recorded and names every fix still open
The vbw prove after the round reuses the results the round's vbw fix done saved: no check runs twice
The output of vbw fix done is unchanged: one line per check or test file, then both count lines, then one line per fix
docs/workflows.md's vbw:fixing row says the workflow runs one vbw fix done after every Dev returns, and its vbw fix done row names the Lead's closing step, not the Dev

docs/workflows.md's run-closing text says the fixing workflow's closing Lead runs vbw fix done before vbw run confirm, that it still runs without a session, and that a stopped closing agent leaves the vbw fix done to run by hand
No user doc still says a Dev runs vbw fix done (the recording section and the one-test-run section of docs/workflows.md, and docs/proof.md)
The workflows stay within 1,500 lines of JavaScript, every agent within 900 words, and all prompts within 22,800 words

requirements.text: Stale proof copies: a process killed outright leaves its .vbw/runtime/proof.* copy (13 MB seen 2026-10-12 05:26 from a killed duplicate fix done); the next proof removes copies whose owner process is gone (record the owner pid in the copy folder, as the gate's mutex does), with a test. Part of the machine-wide limit milestone (T128)

rules.text: every new proof copy names its owner process (pid) in its folder name, made in one step before anything is copied
after a proof is killed with kill -9, the next vbw prove removes the copy whose owner has ended
vbw fix done removes a copy whose owner has ended, before making its own
a copy whose owner process is still running is never removed or changed, also while another cleanup runs at the same moment
removing a dead copy deletes its git worktree entry: git worktree list and .git/worktrees no longer name it
read-only folders inside a dead copy are removed, and removal never follows a link out of the copy
a copy with no owner recorded is removed when older than 24 hours and kept when newer, even when its name is all digits
two cleanups at once never make a proof fail or print an error, and a half-removed copy is finished by the next proof
a dead copy that cannot be removed leaves the proof's result unchanged and prints one warning line naming the folder left
the proof's result (pass or fail, and which checks ran) is the same with and without leftover copies
docs/proof.md says copies record their owner and the next proof removes leftover copies, with the 24-hour rule for owner-less ones

requirements.text: A project where the VBW plugin is disabled shows no VBW (owner, 2026-10-12 12:30, a user project): the status line VBW installs is a user-level setting that runs in every project, so it keeps showing after a per-project disable (enabledPlugins false in the project's .claude/settings.json; Claude Code itself reports the plugin disabled there). The status line script checks the project's settings and prints nothing (or the previous status line) where the plugin is disabled; the same for the panel if it turns out to persist. Part of the machine-wide-limit milestone or its own small one

rules.text: a project whose .claude/settings.json sets enabledPlugins "vbw@vbw-marketplace" to false: VBW's status line script prints nothing and exits 3
the user's settings.json false with the project silent hides VBW; the project's true over the user's false shows it
the project's .claude/settings.local.json wins over its .claude/settings.json and over the user's file, both ways
the user's settings file is found as VBW finds it: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.config/claude-code when it exists, else ~/.claude
started in a subfolder, the settings are read from the nearest folder up holding .git
missing settings files, an absent entry, another plugin turned off or a file that is not valid JSON leave the usual four lines and exit 0
where VBW is on, the script's output is byte-for-byte unchanged and the session's cost file is still written
where VBW is off, the status line writes or creates no file anywhere in the project
vbw-statusline.sh never runs the saved earlier status line or any command from the settings
where VBW is off, the setting runs the user's earlier status line with the same JSON input Claude Code sent, its command kept as written (quotes, spaces, variables, environment prefix)
where VBW is off and no earlier status line was saved, the setting shows nothing and exits 0
where VBW is on, the setting shows only VBW's lines and never runs the earlier status line
with no input and stdin left open, the setting does not hang
vbw statusline on updates an older VBW setting in place, keeping its refresh interval, other fields and the saved earlier status line, and changes nothing when run again
vbw statusline status reports 'on: the VBW status line' for the updated setting, and vbw statusline off restores the earlier status line exactly or removes VBW's

rules.text: a finished build records each plan done with its id, its tier, its tasks and its own seconds from the run's start to its vbw plan done, and the note counts the parts done as before
a plan's tier is its phase's at that moment, standard when the phase has none, and a plan the run left unfinished is no unit
a fix round records its fixes and the highest tier of their phases
planning records how many open requirements of the milestone it planned
QA records the phases it checked, each with its tier
entries written before (kind, seconds, parts) stay readable beside the new ones and the latest 50 of each kind are kept
a damaged or unwritable history or runs store never fails a step and only means no end time yet
a plan's expected seconds are the median seconds per task over the latest 10 finished plans of its tier, times its tasks; another tier and older plans do not count
a build wave's expected time is its longest plan's, never the sum of its plans
with fewer than 3 finished plans of the tier that recorded tasks, a plan takes the median seconds per plan at that tier
with fewer than 3 finished plans of the tier, a plan takes the median seconds per plan of any tier
builds that recorded only parts still count by today's rule, the median seconds per plan times the wave's plans
with fewer than 3 plans in all there is no end time and no guess
vbw next --json's step, the note vbw run start writes and run start's sentence use the new expected times in D425's unchanged wording, within a minute of each other
a fix round's expected time is the median wall time of the latest 10 fix rounds at its tier, whatever the fix count
a fix round with fewer than 3 rounds at its tier takes the median of any tier, and fewer than 3 rounds in all give no time
planning's expected time is the median seconds per open requirement over the latest 10 planning steps that recorded a count, times the requirements to plan now
with fewer than 3 planning steps that recorded a count, planning takes the median planning time as today
QA's expected time is the sum over its phases of the median seconds per phase at the phase's tier, else per phase of any tier, else today's median QA time, else none
a proof records every unit it ran with that unit's own seconds, in vbw prove and in the proof inside vbw fix done
a proof's expected time is the sum of its units' last recorded seconds in runs.json times the median ratio of wall time to summed unit time over the latest 10 proofs that recorded units, rounded
a unit never run before counts as the median of the proof's known units
without proofs that recorded units, proofs that recorded only parts give today's time per unit; with fewer than 3 finished proofs there is no time

vbw next --json carries road {seconds, end, rounds, basis, say}: the waves still to build at their longest plan, one proof per wave over the phase's checks not yet passed, QA where the tier needs it, and the usual fix rounds each as one fix round plus one proof plus one QA recheck
the usual fix rounds per tier are the rounded median of outcome.fix_rounds over the latest 10 finished phases of that tier (1, 2, 2 and 5 give 2)
with fewer than 3 finished phases of a tier the road counts no fix rounds for it and the sentence says so
a wave already built leaves the road, and a built phase whose checks are not passed still counts one proof
before planning the road is the planning step alone and its sentence says the rest follows once the work is planned; it never guesses the unplanned work
when any needed piece has no basis, road.end and road.seconds are null and say names the missing kind; a made-up time never appears

requirements.text: A task break (vbw mutate PLAN taskK) without --check runs the plan's own rule checks, and is refused only when one of those fails on the unbroken code, so an early plan of a requirement that later plans complete can still break its tasks (T165, T159; user-project feedback 2026-10-16)

rules.text: a task break without --check runs the checks of the rules the plan owes: every rule naming it plus every rule of a requirement it completes
a check shared by several owed rules runs once, and no check of another requirement runs
the unbroken run judges only the checks the break runs: a red check of a rule the plan does not owe does not refuse the break (the T159 case)
an owed check red on the unbroken code refuses, writes nothing, names the check and the three ways out: make it pass and commit, --check ID, or --none REASON naming the completing plan
a plan owing no rule runs the checks of its requirements as before, and its refusal adds that it owns no rule and that the Lead names a plan on each rule

--check narrows the run to the named checks of the plan's requirements and refuses another requirement's; a rule break runs its own check as before; the record and the output list exactly the checks that ran
the plan files are byte-identical to their last commit after a red, a survivor or a refusal, and the new code is bash 3.2 with JSON only through jq

rules.text: vbw commit --fix FIX MSG FILE... for an open requirement fix of any source commits the named changed check files of its requirement with VBW-Fix and VBW-Req trailers, touching only them and leaving staged work staged
the commit message is validated as today
a check file of another requirement is refused, committing nothing, naming that requirement
a code file is refused, committing nothing, pointing to vbw commit PLAN
a path under .vbw/ or outside the project is refused, committing nothing
an unknown or non-open fix is refused, committing nothing
a named file that did not change is refused with nothing to commit
a fix of a [human] requirement has no check files to commit and is refused the same way
a project-command fix keeps today's behaviour, and a QA fix's check files commit as today (R160 unchanged), with both trailers
after the commit vbw fix done runs and names the file as waiting, vbw next asks the approval naming it, vbw prove refuses until then and runs the file after
the commit is listed under its requirement by vbw show req, and the proof's scope check blames no plan for it

plugin/agents/dev.md and the fixing workflow's Dev instruction say a requirement fix commits its own requirement's check files with vbw commit --fix, code goes through the plan, and the files wait for one approval

the file guard denies any other check file during the run with its documented answer, naming the file and the files the fix may edit; a QA fix keeps the vbw fix check advice, a proof's fix gets none
a project-command fix opens no check file
a run of a proof's fix and a QA fix together opens both requirements' own check files and allows new test files

docs/workflows.md's vbw commit --fix row, docs/guards.md's fix-run row and docs/proof.md's fix section say a requirement fix commits its own requirement's check files, code goes through the plan, and the files wait for one approval

in vbw fix done a pass removes that unit's kept file and a reused unit leaves it

vbw check keeps the complete output of every failing or timed-out check and says where it is under the check's own line, whose meaning is unchanged; a passing check removes nothing; --expect-red keeps nothing
two vbw check runs of the same check at once each leave a whole file, never a half-written one

vbw show fix lists under each failing check, test file and project command full output: PATH and failing tests: with one line per name recognised: TAP/bats, cargo test, pytest, go test, jest, vitest, mocha, each name once

rules.text: a broken file put into the proof copy gets a modification time strictly newer than every file in the copy, build output included, so a time-based build rebuilds it and the break is red
the restored file gets a time strictly newer than every file in the copy, so the next unbroken run rebuilds the clean code instead of judging the broken build
the time is set later than the newest file in the copy even when that file is stamped ahead of the clock: the kernel never relies on now
a break that deletes a file is judged on its absence: nothing is stamped and no file is created

rules.text: vbw prove prints, just before its verdict line, 'VBW's own work: X of Y min' (minutes with one decimal; Y the command's wall-clock time)

vbw prove prints 'ran again: N of M units; top reasons: <reason> (count), ...' with at most three reasons, most frequent first, ties in the units' order, from the units' own reasons and the whole-proof causes

requirements.text: A rule whose check judges only what the record holds (a measurement kept as a decision, for example) can pass the mutation step: vbw mutate PLAN Rn.k --none REASON is accepted for a rule only when the check's last recorded read list names none of the files of any plan of its requirement, so no code VBW builds could change its outcome; the kernel verifies this from the run store, records the reason with the rule, and refuses it otherwise with the files that could break it (found 2026-10-20: M42's before and after decisions blocked their plans)

rules.text: vbw mutate PLAN Rn.k --none REASON is accepted (exit 0, the entry written) only when the rule's check has a current recorded run with a read list, no git flag, and no read file or listed folder covered by a files entry of any plan of Rn, done or not

a files entry covers a read file when it is the same path, a folder entry (dir/) containing it, or *; it covers a listed folder when it covers that folder or is a file directly inside it, never when it only lies deeper down
the acceptance prints one line naming the check, how many files and folders it read and that none belongs to the requirement's plans, then the recorded reason

a read list naming plan files is refused, nothing written: each read file or listed folder with the plan or plans covering it, ending 'break the rule in that code instead'; a plan whose files are * is named as covering every file
a run that read the project through git is refused saying its files are unknown; a run with no read list is refused saying the file system recorded none

an empty reason, extra words after it, --check with a rule, an unknown plan, a rule number the requirement lacks or a plan not serving the requirement are refused as today, nothing written and no run made

the judged run is the check's last recorded run in the clone's run store, used only while current: its approved definition unchanged and, between its tree and the committed code, no file on its read list changed or deleted and no listed folder's listing changed, whatever its pass or fail

with no run of the check in the store, or a stale one, the command runs the check once in a clean copy of the committed code with read tracking on, records that run in the store as vbw prove would (status, read list, tree, time), says it made that run, and judges that list

the accepted entry is {rule: {req, text}, none, at, head} with head the 40-hex commit of the committed code the judged run was current for; the validator accepts it and refuses a rule none entry carrying checks, result, files or what, or lacking head or the rule's req and text; a task none entry keeps its shape
the write leaves the contract fingerprint unchanged, so nothing waits for approval again
at standard and deep, vbw plan done counts a rule covered when any plan of its requirement has a red break of it or an accepted --none entry for it; a rule with neither is still listed as missing
the Next: line of that refusal names both ways: vbw mutate PLAN Rn.k "what you broke" FILE..., or --none REASON when the check reads nothing the plans build
a task --none keeps its meaning at deep and nothing changes at express
vbw show plan lists the entry as 'Rn.k: no code could change its outcome: REASON' under mutations:, and vbw show plan --json carries it
docs/workflows.md ('The mutation check') no longer says a rule cannot be recorded --none and says when a rule may be, how the kernel verifies it from the recorded read list, and how the refusals read

docs/proof.md ('The mutation check') says a rule whose check judges only the record is recorded --none after the kernel verifies its read list, and that the command may run the check once and record that run

requirements.text: The scope check does not judge a commit that a later commit on the branch exactly undoes: the later commit's change is the exact inverse of the earlier one's (verified with git, file by file), whoever made it; a partial or edited revert is still judged (found 2026-10-20: T169's five commits, reverted by hand after park refused, shared plan ids with M42 and blocked its proof)

rules.text: a commit with a VBW-Plan trailer naming a plan of the current milestone is not judged when a later standing commit on the branch exactly undoes it, whoever made it and whatever its message says (a hand git revert, a plain commit by another author with no revert line)

exact means git's own view, file by file: the same set of paths, and for each path the undo takes it from the commit's new mode and blob back to its old mode and blob; a file added is deleted, a file deleted is added back with the same content and mode, a mode-only change is put back
an edited undo (one extra line), a partial undo (one of two files restored) or an undo touching an extra path is not exact: the commit is judged as today and the violation names the file

an undo that is itself exactly undone by a later standing commit clears nothing: a revert of a revert leaves the original judged; a re-apply after a revert is a fresh commit, judged on its own when it carries a trailer, and the first commit is judged again
each standing commit clears at most one commit, the nearest earlier one it is the mirror image of: a chain of apply, undo, apply, undo leaves all four unjudged
the undoing commit is not judged either when it carries a trailer naming a plan of the current milestone, and is listed with itself as commit and its original as by

evidence.undone lists one {commit, plan, by} with 40-hex ids per cleared commit whose trailer names a plan of the current milestone, newest pair first, [] when none; a cleared commit naming a shipped milestone's plan is not listed
the proof's summary prints, after its scope line, one line per entry in the form 'scope: <12 hex> (<plan>) undone by <12 hex>, not judged'
a commit of the current plan that nothing undoes is judged in today's words, evidence.passed and scope[] keep their shape and vbw next's scope action is unchanged
the scope check runs the same number of git processes for 5 plan-trailer commits as for 50 with no undone pair: one git log walk plus at most one ancestry check per undone pair found
a commit undone by hand with an edit is still judged and nothing is listed; an exact hand revert with no park is no longer judged and is listed with the revert as by
a park's recorded revert that merged over a later edit of the same file still clears its commit through the park's list, and the entry names the park's revert as by

the record validator accepts evidence without undone, with [] and with well-formed entries, and refuses an entry missing commit, plan or by, an id that is not 40 hex digits, a plan id of a wrong shape, an extra field or a non-array, naming evidence.undone, while passed and scope keep their rules
vbw show evidence prints one line per undone entry in the summary's words after the scope lines, and prints nothing for a record written before the field, which still reads

docs/proof.md step 4 of vbw prove states the exact-undo rule in plain words (exactly undone, file by file, mirror image, an undo of an undo clears nothing, the undoing commit is not judged either, a partial or edited revert is still judged) and names the summary line; the sentence 'A commit reverted by hand is still judged' is gone
docs/record.md's evidence row documents undone with its shape {commit, plan, by}, 40-hex ids, [] when none, and that a record written before the field still reads
docs/loop.md keeps the park's rule and says the loop's park and a hand revert clear a commit the same way, so a scope violation parks an item only for a change that is still in the code

requirements.text: The user can name git-ignored paths that a proof's clean copy leaves out (community runtime report, 2026-10-26: an 18 GB ignored data folder was copied into every clean copy). A named path that is not git-ignored is refused by name; a listed path with nothing at it (not created yet, or absent on this computer) is accepted, since there is nothing to leave out. The contract (vbw show contract) lists the paths left out, and a clean copy made with them holds none of them, while every other ignored path is still copied in.

rules.text: the spec parser reads a '## Clean copy' section as one path per bullet, kept as written with its line number, and gives null without the section
a spec without the section leaves the record without the field, syncs as today and prints nothing about the clean copy
vbw spec sync writes the listed paths to project.leave_out, prints 'clean copy leaves out: a, b', and removes the field, saying so, when the section is gone
vbw spec check accepts a good list and counts the paths left out of the clean copy

an absolute path, a path with '.' or '..' segments, or one under .vbw/ or .git/ is a parse error naming its line, refused like a bad Test results folder; a path named twice is refused with the second line

vbw spec check and vbw spec sync refuse a listed path git does not ignore (tracked, or untracked but not ignored) naming the spec line and the path with 'is not git-ignored: only ignored paths are copied in, so only they can be left out', leaving the record unchanged

vbw spec check and vbw spec sync accept a listed path with nothing at it (nothing to leave out; a clone without the data folder syncs its spec), vbw spec check naming it as not here now so a mistyped path is noticed, and the record keeps the path as written
a folder whose files alone are ignored, with nothing tracked or stray inside, is accepted
record.jq accepts a record without project.leave_out and refuses an empty, duplicated, absolute, '..', .vbw/, .git/, empty-string or non-array list, naming the field
vbw init's starting spec.md has a '## Clean copy' section explained in an HTML comment in the style of the other sections, with an example bullet inside the comment, so a fresh spec lists nothing
the list is part of the contract: adding a path changes the fingerprint, the contract reads NOT APPROVED and the approval question is asked again
vbw show contract prints exactly one line 'clean copy leaves out: data/, cache/' when paths are listed and no such line otherwise
vbw show contract --changes names the new list and the old one ('clean copy leaves out: data/, cache/ (was data/)', 'none' for an empty side) when the list changed since the last approval

an edited, unsynced Clean copy section cannot be approved ('spec.md and the record differ (vbw spec sync)') and vbw next says the contract is not ready with that reason instead of offering the approval question; after the sync vbw next offers approval
vbw prove's copy holds the other ignored folder whole and nothing of the listed one, while build folders stay out as before
when only files inside the listed path are ignored (git lists them one by one), none of them enters the copy either
vbw fix done, vbw mutate's single form, vbw mutate --run and the one run of vbw mutate Rn.k --none make their copies without the listed path
a listed path that no longer exists at copy time changes nothing: the proof passes as before, and the next vbw spec sync accepts the path
a spec without the section copies every ignored folder in, as today
leaving a path out changes no result: after listing it, the next proof passes with the same statuses, reuses every unit and the check's read list in the run store is the same

docs/proof.md has a Clean copy section stating the form, the refusals, the contract line and --changes, and that every clean copy skips the listed paths while the other ignored paths are copied in; its approval paragraph lists Clean copy among the compared sections
docs/record.md documents project.leave_out as the spec's Clean copy list, part of the contract, absent when none

tools/l3-suite.sh has the leaveout scenario (in ALL and the header) seeding an ignored data folder listed under Clean copy, reading the record, vbw show contract and a probe the check writes from the copy, never the screen
the committed tools/l3-results/leaveout.json (L3, passed, dated 2026-10-26 or later) shows the contract naming the path, leave_out ['data/'], a passed proof and a copy without the data

requirements.text: When a proof or a mutation run copies ignored data by plain copy (the file system offers no copy-on-write clone) and the data copied exceeds 500 MB, the command prints one line naming the largest ignored folders copied, their sizes and how to leave them out; a copy-on-write clone, or less data, prints nothing.

rules.text: a plain copy of more than 500 MB of ignored data prints exactly one line on stderr starting 'vbw:' naming the three largest ignored folders with their sizes (GB or MB, one decimal, largest first), not the fourth, and the way out 'list them under ## Clean copy in .vbw/spec.md, then vbw spec sync'
the line changes nothing: verdict, evidence, record and exit code are the same with the line and with a threshold too high for it
nothing is printed when every ignored path was cloned copy-on-write, however large
nothing is printed at exactly 500 MB of plain-copied data (512000 KB); one kilobyte more prints the line
VBW_PROOFCOPY_PLAIN_KB, a test-only variable, lowers the threshold so sizes measured with du -sk on small real files print the line
nothing is printed when nothing ignored exists
with two copy slots the line prints once and each ignored path's size is read once per command, not once per copy
the size reading counts in the copies step of VBW's own work (evidence.own.copies)
vbw fix done, vbw mutate's single form, vbw mutate --run and the one run of vbw mutate Rn.k --none print the line once when their plain copy exceeds the threshold, and the break's verdict stands

docs/proof.md names, beside its copy-on-write paragraph, the 500 MB threshold, the one vbw: line with the largest ignored folders and their sizes, the way out, the three silent cases and that the line changes no result

requirements.text: vbw mutate (the single form and --run) ends with the time of VBW's own work by step, in the form the proof uses: copies, the unbroken run, each break's checks, slot waits and saving; the breakdown never changes a break's verdict.

rules.text: a red rule break ends with 'VBW's own work: X of Y min' and '  steps of W s: copies A, unbroken B, break Rn.k C, waits D, saving E' (one decimal each), the steps summing to W within rounding, after the result lines, with the recorded entry's keys and the files' restoration unchanged
a survivor keeps its exit 1 and its line, the breakdown following it
a task break names its entry 'break taskK'
a break caught by a check file waiting for approval keeps its lines, the pending marking and exit 0, the breakdown coming after them

the figures are measured: a check that takes a second on broken code puts at least 1.0 s into the break's entry, more than the unbroken one, and the steps sum to the wall; the own-work line keeps the proof's rounding to tenths of a minute, so a run under three seconds reads 0.0 min
a refusal (checks red on the unbroken code, a dirty check file, a stale queued break) ends with its message as today and prints no breakdown
--queue, task --none and Rn.k --none print no breakdown
vbw mutate --run one at a time ends with one entry per break ('break R1.1', 'break R1.2') in queue order after the last result's lines, the entries recorded as before
vbw mutate --run with breaks side by side names the wave's targets in one entry ('breaks R1.1 R1.2')
waits is the time the run waited for a computer-wide slot (at least 1.0 s when another project held the only slot) and the slots line still comes last, after the breakdown
without a wait the waits entry reads 0.0 and nothing follows the breakdown

docs/workflows.md's mutation-check section shows the two lines in their printed form, names each step (copies, unbroken, a break named by its target, waves in --run, waits, saving), says the figures are measured and sum to the wall, that the breakdown changes nothing, and that a refusal, --queue and --none print none

requirements.text: VBW's own plan files (.vbw/record.json, .vbw/spec.md, .vbw/map.md) are never hidden by a project's git ignore rule for files (community runtime report, 2026-10-26: a project-wide *.json rule hid the record and the clone got no plan): vbw init writes un-hide lines for them in VBW's own .vbw/.gitignore and says so in one line, and an existing project gets those lines the next time VBW commits its files. When a rule hides the whole .vbw folder, which no line inside it can undo, vbw init says so naming the rule's source line and the fix, vbw doctor fails with the same, and vbw approve refuses with that message instead of committing nothing; the record's own commits are never silently skipped.

rules.text: vbw init writes .vbw/.gitignore as runtime/, !record.json, !spec.md, !map.md, !.gitignore and prints exactly one line saying VBW keeps its plan files visible to git through .vbw/.gitignore
in an initialized project vbw init adds only the missing lines, keeps the user's lines, says so once, and leaves a complete file byte-identical and silent when run again

with a project-wide *.json or *.md rule in the project's .gitignore, no own file is hidden: VBW's next commit commits the record and .vbw/.gitignore, printing no warning, and the spec is visible to git as an untracked file until the next full commit (approve, run end, ship) takes it, as in a project without such a rule
the same holds for a rule in .git/info/exclude and in a global excludes file
an existing project (.vbw/.gitignore holding runtime/ alone) gets the un-hide lines at its next VBW commit, .vbw/.gitignore committed along with the record, leaving .vbw clean

with a rule hiding the whole .vbw folder (.vbw/ or *), vbw init prints the hidden file with the rule's source as git check-ignore -v gives it (file:line:pattern) and the fix 'remove that line, or change it to .vbw/runtime/'
vbw doctor prints the same as a fail line with its fix line and exits 1; without such a rule it says nothing about hidden files
vbw approve refuses with that message, exit 1, adding no decision, granting no consent (the contract stays NOT APPROVED) and making no commit

vbw next names the hidden file among the reasons the contract is not ready instead of offering the approval menu; with the rule narrowed to .vbw/runtime/ it offers approval and the approval commits the record
record_commit's non-strict form prints a 'vbw: warning:' line naming the hidden file, the rule's source line and the fix, and never commits the hidden file silently

docs/record.md names the un-hide lines, that vbw init writes them and an existing project gets them at its next VBW commit, that the project's .gitignore is never edited, the whole-folder case with what init, doctor, approve and other commits say, and the fix
docs/diagnostics.md documents the doctor's fail line for a hidden own file, its git check-ignore source and its fix

tools/l3-suite.sh has the hiddenrecord scenario (in ALL and the header) seeding a *.json rule and reading git and .vbw/.gitignore, never the screen; its committed result (L3, passed, dated 2026-10-26 or later) shows the record committed, the un-hide lines and at least one record commit
the greenfield scenario records plan_files_unhidden and its committed result from this code shows it true

requirements.text: When a rule names its plan, vbw show plan tells the Dev which rules and checks are this plan's and which are another plan's: a rule naming another plan is marked with that plan and whether it is built before or after this one, a check that serves only other plans' rules is marked as that plan's (red until it is built, not this plan's to pass), and the rules shown as this plan's are exactly those vbw mutate counts as the plan's own (those naming it, plus every rule of a requirement it completes); the Dev's red-first and green steps use only the plan's own checks, and a red check of another plan's rule is never a blocker; rules naming no plan keep today's listing (found 2026-10-26 in the taskbreak real-user run: P1.1's Dev blocked twice on P1.2's red C2, 'R1.2/C2 needs shout.sh, but the plan's only file is greet.sh', and the main session re-planned P1.1 to own shout.sh)

rules.text: own_rules($p) in VBW_JQ_DEFS gives, as [{req, n, text, check, plan}], the live rules of the [auto] requirements plan $p serves that name $p, while another plan of the requirement is open; [] for an unknown plan or a plan of [human] requirements only
a plan that completes a requirement (every other plan serving it is done) owns every live rule of it, those naming a done plan and those naming no plan (plan null) included

own_rules is independent of the phase's tier; owed_rules($p) equals own_rules($p) at standard and deep and is [] at express or without a tier, so vbw plan done, steps.sh and road.jq count the same rules as before
a retired rule is left out of own_rules and the other rules keep their numbers

cmd-mutate.sh's task break takes its check ids from own_rules and holds no second definition of the owner computation; its fallback (every check of its requirements) and its 'owns no rule' wording stay

in vbw show plan P, a rule of P's requirements that is not P's own and names another plan Q is listed as today followed by ' [Q's, ORDER]': 'built before this plan' when Q's build wave comes earlier, 'built after this plan' when later, 'built beside this plan' when the same
ORDER is 'done' when Q is done, 'blocked' when Q is blocked, and 'built after this plan' when P is done (out of the build waves) and Q is open
a rule that is P's own (naming P, naming no plan, or any rule of a requirement P completes, one naming a done plan included) is listed byte for byte as today

a check is listed as today followed by ' [Q's: red until it is built, not this plan's to pass]' when at least one live rule points at it and every live rule pointing at it is another plan's; several plans are joined 'P1.2's and P1.3's'
a check pointed at by any own rule, or by no live rule (a retired rule only), is listed exactly as today; a plan whose requirements are all [human] shows no mark

vbw show plan --json keeps every field it has today and adds to each rule plan (the named plan or null), own, and when not own order (done, blocked, before, after, beside); to each check own and, when not own, plans (the ids whose rules it serves)

the two readers agree: the checks of the rules --json marks own are exactly the keys of the checks map a task break records, for the early plan while the other is open and for the completing plan after the other is done
a project whose rules name no plan prints exactly today's listing, and its --json marks every rule and check own
dev.md's red-first step runs vbw check --expect-red on the plan's own checks only (those vbw show plan leaves unmarked), and its green step ends when every own check passes

dev.md says a check marked another plan's stays red until that plan is built, is never a blocker and never DEVN-04, and is at most named in notes; the DEVN-04 row keeps 'plan cannot work as written' and excludes a file another plan owns for its own marked rule
docs/workflows.md's vbw show plan row names the marks for another plan's rules and checks, and the doc shows both marks as printed and names the ORDER words
docs/workflows.md's task-form bullet points at the rules vbw show plan leaves unmarked, and the doc says red-first and green use only the plan's own checks and another plan's red check is no blocker

docs/proof.md's paragraph on a rule that names its plan shows both marks as printed, names the ORDER words, and says the Dev's steps use only the plan's own checks and another plan's red check is no blocker
scenario_taskbreak reads vbw show plan P1.1's marks (R1.2 built after this plan, C2 red until it is built) from the transcripts' tool results, never the screen, as the fact show_plan_marked
scenario_taskbreak records early_plan_never_blocked: no vbw plan block P1.1 tool call in the transcripts and P1.1's recorded files still exactly ["greet.sh"]; the earlier facts stay
the committed taskbreak result from this code (dated 2026-10-26 or later) passed with show_plan_marked and early_plan_never_blocked true

requirements.text: A Dev can strengthen a check that the mutation step found unable to fail (a survivor) even when its check file also holds other requirements' checks: vbw commit accepts a plan's edit to a check file named by the check of one of the plan's own rules, the edit waits for the user's approval before the proof as any check edit (the whole diff shown at the approval), and the survivor can then be re-run; a check file that none of the plan's own rules' checks name is still refused by name (T192; P170.5, 2026-10-26)

rules.text: the kernel holds one definition of the check files a plan may strengthen (the files of the checks of its own rules, open once a survivor is recorded), in record.sh's shared jq defs beside own_rules; cmd-commit.sh holds no second one

after a survivor of the plan's rule, the file guard lets a build agent write a check file that a check of the plan's own rules names, one shared with another requirement's check included; a file only another requirement's check names stays protected; before any survivor every check file is protected
after a survivor, vbw commit PLAN MSG FILE commits a check file named by a check of the plan's own rules, shared or not, with the plan's VBW-Plan and VBW-Req trailers

a check file that no check of the plan's own rules names, or any check file before a survivor of the plan, is refused by name with the rule stated and a Next line; the words 'no other requirement's check file is the plan's to commit' are gone

after the commit, the same break run again prints 'TARGET survives the approved check; caught by the pending one: F', exits 0, records the break red with pending [F] and strengthened [F], and says the pending file still needs the one approval before the proof
the strengthened shared file waits for the approval: after the build vbw next asks for it by name, vbw prove refuses until it is approved, and the proof's scope check counts the commit as the plan's
vbw show contract --changes prints, under each changed test file line, the complete diff between the approved content and the file as it is now, every hunk, committed or not
when the approved content of a changed test file is not in the project's git history, --changes says so in one line and prints no diff

docs/proof.md, docs/record.md, docs/guards.md, the Dev prompt (step 4 and DEVN-04) and the router's approve step say the rule in the same words: the checks of the plan's own rules, shared files included, the rest refused by name, the whole diff shown before the approval question

requirements.text: vbw apply refuses, naming the check and both plans, a check whose rules are owned by two plans of one milestone that build one after the other, directly or through a shared file, because the earlier plan's mutation step would find the check red on unbroken code; the Lead's spec states the rule in words (T187; M43: P166.1 and P168.1 blocked)

rules.text: in every mode, a check whose live rules name two undone plans of the milestone, one in the other's after directly or through a chain, is refused before anything changes, naming the check and both plans and why, with the mode's name and a Next line; the record is unchanged
the same refusal when the two plans share a file under the wave rule, with no after between them
no refusal when the check's rules name one plan or none, when one of the two plans is done, or when the plans build beside each other; a retired rule counts for nothing
rules.retired: R215 refuses a check two open plans own even when they build beside each other (a shared wave: the first Dev's mutation step would run the check before the other Dev committed); the non-refusals this rule kept (one plan or none, one plan done, a retired rule) now live in R215's edge rule, pinned by C488

rules.text: the Lead's brief says a check's rules belong to one plan: plans of a requirement that build one after the other give each plan's rules a check of their own (a separate test file, or the same file with a case filter as a distinct check)
docs/proof.md's Rules section and docs/workflows.md's list of what vbw apply refuses name the refusal and its reason (red on unbroken code)

requirements.text: vbw apply refuses, naming the requirement, a requirement whose rules name an owning plan on only some of them: every rule names a plan, or none does, so each rule's owner is defined for vbw show plan and for the task break (T191; P170, 2026-10-26)

rules.text: in every mode, a requirement whose live rules, as the document leaves them, name a plan on some and not others is refused naming the requirement and the counts, with the mode's name and a Next line; the record is unchanged
a --patch reword that names a plan on one rule, or takes it off one, and leaves the requirement mixed is refused the same way
every rule naming a plan, or none naming one, is accepted; retired rules are not counted
the Lead's brief rule 7 (Rules) says the plan is named on every rule of the requirement or on none
docs/workflows.md's list of what vbw apply refuses and docs/record.md's requirements row say a plan is named on every rule or on none

requirements.text: A full vbw apply keeps a started plan's note (its blocked reason) together with its status and recorded breaks, so the reason survives planning of a later phase (T190; P169.3, 2026-10-26)

rules.text: a full apply that re-sends a blocked plan as is keeps its status blocked, its note and its recorded breaks; vbw show plan and vbw show roadmap print the reason after the apply
vbw apply --add and --patch keep the note the same way
a plan without a note gains none from an apply; the note goes only when a kernel command changes the plan's status (vbw plan reset, vbw plan done)
docs/record.md's plans row and docs/workflows.md's vbw apply row say a started plan keeps its note with its status and breaks across every vbw apply

requirements.text: The Clean copy documentation is exact: docs/proof.md quotes vbw spec check's missing-path wording as the kernel prints it and says a listed path is one word per line (a path with a space cannot be listed, as for Test results folders); and the clean copy reads the leave-out list once per copy, not once per ignored entry (M43 QA notes, 2026-10-26)

rules.text: docs/proof.md's Clean copy section quotes the missing-path sentence exactly as cmd-spec.sh prints it (spec.md line N: PATH is not here now, so nothing is left out for it yet); 'does not exist here now' is gone
vbw spec check prints that one sentence for a listed path with nothing at it: the kernel-side pin of the words the docs quote
docs/proof.md says a listed path is one word per line: a path with a space cannot be listed and is refused with its line number, quoting the refusal's 'expected "- <path>"' wording
a line like '- my data/' is refused by vbw spec check and vbw spec sync with its line number and that wording; the record is unchanged

proofcopy_make parses project.leave_out once per copy into the bash array PROOFCOPY_LEFT and proofcopy_entry reads only it (no here-string, no jq call, no record read per ignored entry), with the expansion guarded under set -u; the existing clean-copy cases pass unchanged

requirements.text: vbw apply refuses, naming the check and both plans, a check whose rules two open plans of one milestone own, whatever their order, the same wave included: the first Dev's mutation step would run the check before the other Dev committed, a race that fails only sometimes; the refusal keeps R211's words for plans that build one after the other and says the plans build beside each other for a shared wave, and the Lead's brief states that a check's rules belong to one plan (T193; Architect note, M44 planning 2026-10-27)

rules.text: in every mode (full apply, --add, --patch), judged on the record as the document would leave it, a check whose live rules name two different plans of the milestone that are not done (a blocked plan counts as not done) is refused before anything changes, naming the check and both plans, with the mode's name and a Next line; the record is byte-identical after the refusal

when B builds after A (A in B's after directly or through a chain, A's and B's files overlap under the wave rule, or A's wave comes before B's in waves($m) on the merged record judged as if no plan were blocked), the message keeps R211's words, 'C is owned by two plans that build one after the other (WHY): A and B; the earlier plan's mutation step would find C red on unbroken code', WHY being 'B builds after A', 'A and B share a file' or 'A builds in an earlier wave than B'

when neither builds after the other and they would share a wave, the message reads 'C is owned by two plans that build beside each other (a shared wave): A and B; the first Dev's mutation step would run C before the other Dev committed, a race that fails only sometimes'
no refusal when the check's rules name one plan or none, when one of the two plans is done, or when the check belongs to a requirement of another milestone; a retired rule counts for nothing

the Lead's brief rule 6 says a check's rules belong to one plan and that several open plans of a requirement, whatever their order and the same wave included, each get a check of their own (a separate test file, or the same file with a case filter that is a distinct check), because vbw apply refuses a check whose rules two open plans own
docs/proof.md's Rules bullet and docs/workflows.md's list of what vbw apply refuses say the refusal covers any two plans not yet built, order or not, and name the race for a shared wave

requirements.text: Every refusal of vbw apply ends with its own Next line naming the fix, and the Next lines of the mixed-owner refusal (R212) and the two-owner refusal (R211, R215) are pinned word for word, so a dropped arm can never pass as the generic fallback (M44 QA note, 2026-10-27)

rules.text: apply_next answers the ordered and the beside two-owner messages with one arm, 'give each plan's rules a check of their own (a separate test file, or the same file with a case filter as a distinct check), or move the rules to one plan', and the mixed-owner message with 'name a plan on every rule of the requirement, or on none (vbw apply --patch rewords a rule: {"rule": "Rn.k", "plan": "P1.1"})'; fed each message directly, it never answers with the fallback text

every refusal cmd-apply.sh builds itself is answered by an arm of its own: for every full, --add and --patch refusal case the Next line differs from the fallback arm's text, except the record validations (an unknown requirement, a plan for no phase), named in the test file as taking the fallback by design

the R211, R215 and R212 cases of tests/apply-refusal-modes.bats assert the refusal's whole last line word for word ('Next: give each plan's rules a check of their own (a separate test file, or the same file with a case filter as a distinct check), or move the rules to one plan' and 'Next: name a plan on every rule of the requirement, or on none (vbw apply --patch rewords a rule: {"rule": "Rn.k", "plan": "P1.1"})'), not only a 'Next: ' prefix

requirements.text: vbw mutate takes the pending and strengthened files of a break from strengthen_files, the one definition of R210, never from the files of the checks the break happened to run, and the header of the test file that pins R210 says exactly what its cases pin (M44 QA note, 2026-10-27)

rules.text: the tool collects, across every shell file under all the DIRs it is given, the writer functions: a function whose body holds a builtin write that the tool's rules judge to run in the function's shell, and, to a fixed point, a function whose body calls a writer under those rules; a function writing through vbw_out, '( printf ... )', 'printf ... | cat' or 'printf ... > "$f"' is not a writer

inside a loop fed by a process substitution, a call to a writer function in the loop's own shell is refused like a direct printf: FILE:LINE:text of the calling line, then the writer's name and where it writes (FILE:LINE), exit 1; a writer defined in another file under another DIR is known; a two-step chain (a calls b, b writes with echo >&2) is refused at the call of a
