plugin/lib/core.sh vbw_cores accepts a core count with trailing junk: the pattern '[1-9][0-9]*' means a digit, a digit, then anything. A reader answering '10.5' or '12abc' is accepted as a whole number, then $((cores * 3 / 4)) dies with 'arithmetic syntax error' (checked in bash: 'n=10.5; echo $((n*3/4))' fails). The criterion says the first whole number is taken and VBW keeps working when the count is unusable. tests/check-jobs-machine.bats only tries '2.5' (single digit then dot), which the pattern happens to reject. Fix: accept only all-digit values (for example reject any value matching *[!0-9]*, then require at least 1), and add '10.5' and '12abc' to the unreadable-count test.

plugin/lib/checks.sh checks_gate_enter calls vbw_check_jobs on every check (line 143), and each parallel check runs in its own subshell (checks_run_all), so the limit is read (getconf + jq) once per check, not once per process. Plan P100.2 and the comment at lines 101-103 say 'read once per process'. The comment is wrong and the plan is not followed; a setting changed mid-run is seen by only some checks. Fix: read the limit once in the process (for example pass it from checks_run_all/checks_run) or correct the plan and the comment.

The stop report prints how long the command actually ran, not the limit in use. plugin/lib/cmd-prove.sh prove_summary prints '(\(.value.seconds | floor) s)'; seconds is the whole-second wall clock measured by checks_exec (bash SECONDS), which is >= the limit and can be limit+1 on a loaded machine (the exact case this phase is about). So the line can say '(3601 s)' for a 3600 s limit, or '(3 s)' for a limit of 2, though the criterion says the report names the limit in use. tests/command-timeout.bats test 3 checks only for '2 s' and would fail intermittently when the run reads 3. Fix: print the effective limit (settings.command_timeout // 3600, the same value prove_commands uses) in the summary line, and pin it in the test with a run that reports seconds above the limit.

A shipped milestone whose ship saw no figures (no frozen total) is not kept unknown: costs_milestone_total (plugin/lib/costs.sh) has no status check, so vbw show costs (cmd-show.sh show_costs loops over every shipped id) recomputes it from the current side files minus a baseline that does not exist, i.e. from each session's first figure. Once the status line is turned on, every old shipped milestone that has no total (in this project M1 to M23) would show the whole session spend, and the same dollars would also count in the active milestone. That breaks the criterion 'no session's spend counts in two milestones' and 'never a guess'. tests/cost-milestones.bats only covers a shipped milestone WITH a frozen total. Regression test: ship a milestone with no side file, then write a side file (figures s1 2 1000 100), start the next milestone? no: just run 'vbw show costs --json': the shipped milestone must stay usd null and sessions 0 and be listed in unknown.milestones, and the sum of the milestones' usd must not exceed what the sessions report.

The benchmark does not measure the status line with the cost write in place. tools/bench-hooks.sh statusline() feeds {session_id, workspace, cwd, model} with no cost or context_window, so the new side-file branch (select in statusline.jq, split and mv in vbw-statusline.sh) never runs in the 60 ms measurement, yet the criterion and plan P125.1 say the budget holds 'with the write in place'. I measured by hand with a cost field and a bad session id (jq part only, no write allowed in a QA run): about 27 ms per call with and without cost, so the budget is probably fine, but the promised measurement cannot show a regression in the write. Regression test: make bench-hooks.sh feed total_cost_usd and token totals for the status line cases (and a safe session id in a project with the record), and fail if the side file was not written.

docs/costs.md lists the JSON fields of 'vbw show costs --json' incompletely and contradicts the output: milestones[] also carries title (the table omits it), and runs[] also carries session, started and ended (the table lists only id, kind, milestone, cost). Regression test: tests/cost-docs.bats should compare the field names in docs/costs.md with the keys of a real 'vbw show costs --json' (milestones[0] and runs[0]) and fail on any missing.

Two runs started within the same second get the same run id (kind plus the start time to the second), so .costs.runs holds two entries with one id and vbw show costs cannot tell them apart. Seen in tests/cost-milestones.bats test 3 on an idle machine: both qa runs became qa-20261012T030650Z and the test fails; under load it passes by timing. Run ids must be unique: a run that would repeat an id of .costs.runs gets a numbered suffix. Regression test with a fixed clock, and test 3 then deterministic.

plugin/lib/proofreuse.sh proofreuse_proved has two clauses no test can fail on: 'evidence.contract equals contract_hash now' and the per-command 'store fp equals proofreuse_command_fp' loop (D291). Every fixture (tests/proofcauses-lib.bats prove_passed, tests/proofreuse-rule.bats ~line 248, tests/proof-cause-tree.bats) records a contract and record fingerprint that match, and no test records a mismatching evidence.contract or a drifted command fingerprint with tree, head and record otherwise equal. Deleting either clause leaves the suite green. They also look redundant since D296: the contract hash is made of the record's structure plus the check files (already in evidence.record and evidence.tree), and commands live in the record. Regression test (or remove the clause): a prove_passed fixture with only evidence.contract changed, and one with a command's store fingerprint changed (tree, head, record equal), both asserting proofcauses_find and proofreuse_allowed name no 'nothing was committed' cause/reason.

docs/proof.md line 677 (causes table row) and the D173 paragraph (~line 714) state the cause's conditions as tree, head, record fingerprint and passed, but not the conditions D291 added and the code enforces: the proof must be of the contract now approved (evidence.contract) and every project command as it last ran. A reader who edits an approved check or command and proves again cannot tell from this row why no cause fires. Regression test: tests/proof-cause-tree-docs.bats should grep the row for 'evidence.contract' (or whatever wording replaces it once the redundant clause question in the other finding is decided) and for 'evidence.record'.

A figure that goes down makes the record unwritable. costs_diff (plugin/lib/costs.sh) is plain END minus START and nothing checks the sign: with an opening figure above the closing one it returns {usd:-1,in:-200,out:-30} (I ran it). vbw run end (plugin/lib/cmd-run.sh) puts that into costs.runs, and record_update then refuses it ('refused: costs.runs entries need ... non-negative numbers'), so the run can never be ended and the lease stays open. The same applies to vbw ship: costs_milestone_total subtracts the baseline from the latest figure per session with no floor, so a session whose figure fell below its baseline gives a negative total that the validator refuses, and the milestone cannot be shipped. A fall can come from a side file replaced by a restarted or resumed session, or a hand-edited file. For a night shift that means a stuck project, not an 'unknown' cost. Fix: a decrease means VBW cannot tell, so costs_diff returns null (cost unknown) when any field of END is below START, and costs_milestone_total counts a session whose latest figure is below its baseline from its first figure (or leaves it out) instead of going negative. Regression test (tests/cost-runs.bats and tests/cost-milestones.bats): write a side file at 2.00 USD, run start, rewrite it at 1.00 USD, run end must succeed with cost null; then a milestone with a baseline above the latest figure must ship and show a non-negative total.

Alternative if you prefer to narrow the promise: remove 'programs that write files' from the docs row.

plugin/lib/cmd-fix.sh (end of cmd_fix, the block after proofreuse_save/testfiles_save) prints 'checks: N ran, M reused' BEFORE the test file lines, then the test file lines, then 'test files: N ran, M reused'. docs/proof.md 'Reusing an unchanged pass' (the text block at about line 786) shows an output that vbw fix done cannot print. It shows the cause line 'every candidate check runs: this clone has no earlier recorded run' AFTER the unit lines (the code prints it BEFORE them, cmd_fix right after proofcauses_find), shows 'C2 unchanged since its pass' reused while a cause is active (a cause makes every candidate run, so nothing is reused), shows 'ran: <reason>' parts under a cause (the code leaves them out under a cause: wmap is filled only when no cause), and puts a test file line between check lines (the code prints all check lines, the checks count, then test file lines). tests/fix-done-docs.bats only greps single lines for presence, so it cannot catch the contradiction. Regression test: tests/fix-done-docs.bats should check the example's line order and coherence (cause line first; no 'ran:' part and no reused line in an example that has a cause; or show two separate examples, one without a cause and one with), ideally by comparing against output a fixture really prints.

During a plan run, a shell redirect to a path outside the project that begins with ~ or $HOME is not denied. The guard reads the text of the redirect target, not what the shell turns it into, so it treats ~/tests/a.test.js or "$HOME/tests/a.test.js" as a project-relative test file and lets it through; bash writes it into the home folder. Probe (guard-bash.jq, plan lease, Dev agent): "echo a > ~/tests/a.test.js", "echo a > $HOME/tests/a.test.js" and echo a > "$HOME/tests/a.test.js" all give no answer (allowed). Under a build lease the same forms are denied, but only by accident and with the wrong reason ("~/src/pay.txt is outside this run's files"), not the R177 outside-the-project reason. The goal says any redirect outside the project is denied, so this is a gap. Fix: treat a redirect or write target that starts with ~, or contains $ or a backtick or $( (an expansion the guard cannot resolve), as outside the project during a run (refuse with the outside-the-project reason). Regression test (tests/guard-outside.bats): under a plan lease, a Dev Bash call with a redirect to ~/tests/a.test.js, $HOME/tests/a.test.js and "$HOME/tests/a.test.js" must be denied with "outside the project" and Next:; the same redirect to tests/a.test.js stays allowed.

The device-file exception in run_write_denial (plugin/hooks/common.jq: /dev/null, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, /dev/tty are not refused) is a rule docs/guards.md promises, but only /dev/null is exercised (indirectly, tests/hooks-guard.bats line 200: npm test > /dev/null 2>&1 && ...). Nothing tests /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr or /dev/tty, and tests/guard-outside.bats has no test that a redirect such as 2>/dev/null is still allowed under a run, so narrowing or widening the regex would pass every test. Also not in plan task 1 or any recorded decision (D289, D300 say nothing of devices); a /dev/null exception is clearly needed, but the plan or a decision should record it. Regression test (tests/guard-outside.bats): under a build lease, "ls 2>/dev/null", "echo x > /dev/stderr", "echo x > /dev/stdout", "echo x > /dev/tty" are allowed, while "echo x > /dev/sda" and "echo x > /dev/null/x" are denied with "outside the project". Also record the exception in a decision. Minor wording: for a read-only run with an empty file list the refusal reads "there only nothing: its agents only read"; say "there nothing" instead.

A shell redirect written as >&FILE or >& FILE (bash's 'stdout and stderr to FILE', the same as &> FILE) to a path outside the project is not denied during a run. Probe (guard-bash.jq, build lease and plan lease, Dev/Lead agent): 'echo a >&/tmp/a', 'echo a >& /tmp/a.test.js' give no answer (allowed), while 'echo a &> /tmp/x' and 'echo a > /tmp/x' are denied. Cause: simple() in plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq drops any redirect whose rest starts with & (meant for fd copies like 2>&1 and >&2), so a >& redirect to a file is dropped whole (D304 'fd redirects stay whole' only covers the numeric form). The criterion says a shell redirect to /tmp or another outside folder is denied. Fix: treat >&WORD (and >& WORD) as a file redirect unless WORD is digits or -. Regression test (tests/guard-outside.bats): under a build lease and a plan lease, a Dev Bash call 'echo a >&/tmp/a' and 'echo a >& /tmp/a' is denied with 'outside the project' and Next:; 'ls 2>&1', 'echo a >&2' and 'echo a >&-' stay allowed.

tests/guard-outside.bats does not check that the refusal names the path for a shell redirect, a relative climb or an interpreter write. The criterion says each denial names the path; only the first test (Write to /tmp/scratch.txt) asserts that the output holds the path. denied_outside checks 'outside the project', 'Next:' and the scratch advice, never the path, so a change that makes the guard-bash redirect rule pass a different string (for example the project-relative form, or the empty string) to the denial would pass every test. Regression test: make denied_outside take the expected path as a second argument and assert the reason contains it, for 'echo hi > /tmp/scratch.txt', the '../outside.txt' write, the python3/node writes to /tmp/q and /tmp/q.js, and the '../outside.txt' interpreter write.

The clobber redirect >| (bash noclobber override) is mishandled by the guard in plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq (simple() / commands()). commands() splits the command on |, so "echo a >| /tmp/x" becomes "echo a >" and " /tmp/x"; simple() then ends with .next set and no target, and the D304 fallback adds the placeholder "`...`". Probes (build lease, files [src/pay.txt], Dev agent, guard-bash.jq run with the hook inputs): "echo a >| /tmp/x" is denied but the refusal reads "`...` cannot be resolved by the guard (~ or a shell expansion), so it counts as outside the project" instead of naming /tmp/x (criterion 1: the denial names the path). Worse, "echo a >| src/pay.txt", a write to the plan file itself, is also denied with that wrong reason, although criterion 2 says inside the project the lease rules decide as before (before this phase the target was silently dropped, so it was allowed). Fix: do not split on the | of a >| token (or treat >| as a redirect operator before splitting) so the real target is read. Regression test (tests/guard-outside.bats): under a build lease a Dev Bash call "echo a >| /tmp/x" is denied and the reason names /tmp/x and says outside the project; "echo a >| src/pay.txt" is allowed. Low severity (>| is rare). Not a finding, noted for the summary: tee, cp, mv, dd of=, curl -o, touch, mkdir and sed -i aimed outside the project are not refused during a run; the goal and docs/guards.md scope this rule to file-tool writes, shell redirects and inline interpreter programs, so this matches the agreement.

Test gap: the 'where the run may write' part of the outside-the-project refusal is pinned for only 2 of its 4 wordings. plugin/hooks/common.jq outside_denial has four branches: plan run ('the project's test files and .vbw/'), fix run for a failed proof command (files null, 'project files'), build/fix with plan files, and read-only (files []). tests/guard-outside.bats pins only the build wording (via denied_outside, which checks the path, 'outside the project', 'Next: ' and the scratch advice, never the 'there only ...' clause) and the read-only wording (map run). grep -rn "project's test files and" tests returns nothing, and no test sends a plain /tmp file write or redirect under a plan run, the run the Lead was in when the incident happened (the plan-run test only uses ~ and $HOME forms). Probed by hand against the guard: plan-run /tmp/dbg.bats is denied with the right text today, so behavior is correct; changing the plan branch to say 'project files' would pass every test. Regression test: in tests/guard-outside.bats start a plan run and require a Write to /tmp/dbg.bats be denied naming the path, containing "there only the project's test files and .vbw/" and the scratch Next line; do the same for a fix run for a failed proof command (files null) expecting 'there only project files'. Minor, same file: the first 'out=' line of the test 'outside a VBW project the guards say nothing' calls vbw_hook inside bash -c (a function bash -c cannot see), errors are swallowed and the value is overwritten on the next line, so it is dead code; drop it.

Dead code is still in tests/guard-outside.bats, in the test 'R177: outside a VBW project the guards say nothing'. Its first 'out=' line runs vbw_hook inside 'bash -c', but vbw_hook is a shell function that bash -c cannot see (tests/helper.bash has no export -f; probe: bash -c 'type vbw_hook' gives 'not found'). The error is swallowed by '2> /dev/null || true' and the value is overwritten by the next 'out=' line, so the line checks nothing. Finding F157 asked for it to be dropped and was marked fixed, but commit e4532e3d only added 25 lines and removed none. Regression test: not a behavior test; remove the line, and keep a check (for example in tests/standards.bats or this file) that no bats test calls a helper function from inside 'bash -c' without exporting it.

A file-tool write (Write/Edit) to a project file whose name holds a dollar sign, a backtick, or starts with a tilde is denied during a run as "outside the project", even when the file is listed in the plan. Probe (build lease, files [src/pay.txt, app/routes/$id.tsx], Dev agent, plugin/hooks/guard-file.jq with project root /proj): Write /proj/app/routes/$id.tsx gives deny "…/$id.tsx cannot be resolved by the guard (~ or a shell expansion), so it counts as outside the project: … there only its plan files (src/pay.txt, app/routes/$id.tsx)". The reason contradicts itself (the file is in the plan list), and the Dev cannot write its own plan file. Remix / React Router route files are named $param.tsx, so this blocks real builds. Before this phase the same write was allowed (covered by lease.files). Cause: run_write_denial in plugin/hooks/common.jq applies unresolved_path (^~|[$`]) to every path, but the file tools receive a literal absolute path that no shell ever expands; the "guard reads text, never expands" reasoning of D304 only holds for Bash redirect targets and git checkout arguments. The same false denial hits a single-quoted redirect target (echo x > 'app/routes/$id.tsx' is shell-literal) because simple() restores the quotes before the test. Not pinned: tests/guard-outside.bats F147 test only checks a ~ file write is refused, no test writes a plan-listed file with $ in its name. Fix: apply unresolved_path only to Bash-derived targets (pass a flag from guard-bash.jq, or call it there), and keep file-tool paths on project_path; optionally let a quoted target count as literal. Record the narrowing in a decision (D304 says "write target"). Regression test (tests/guard-outside.bats): under a build lease whose files include app/routes/$id.tsx, a Write to <project>/app/routes/$id.tsx is allowed, a Write to <project>/app/other/$x.tsx is refused as outside the run files (not as unresolvable), while an unquoted Bash redirect to $HOME/x stays denied.

loop_park_reverts (plugin/lib/loop-park.sh) skips every commit that touches ANY .vbw/ file, even one that also changes code. The variable is outside=1 and is set to 0 on the first '.vbw/*' path, so a commit changing src/x and .vbw/map.md is silently not reverted and not named in the 'left unreverted' list. The plan and the comment above the function say: revert the commits that touch any file outside .vbw/. The park would then leave the item's code in the tree while the record says the item is gone. No test covers a mixed commit. Regression test: in tests/loop-retry-park.bats add an item commit that changes tests/greet.sh (or src) and .vbw/map.md together; after the park, assert it is reverted (a Revert commit exists, the code file is gone).

The Bash guard can be walked around, so a tool call can arm the loop. guard-bash.jq loop_call (line 142-146) lets any command through that has --help or -h anywhere in its arguments, but 'vbw loop start' treats the next word after --session as a session id. I ran, in a scratch VBW project, the hook on 'vbw loop start --session --help T1 --no-ceiling': the hook allowed it, and running that command armed the loop ('loop on: T1; no ceiling; session --help'). The criterion says the guard denies vbw loop start from any tool call. Regression test to add in tests/loop-guard.bats: 'vbw loop start --session --help T1 --no-ceiling' and the same with -h must be denied with the pinned START_TEXT (fix: only a --help/-h that is the sub-command's own first argument is exempt, or the kernel refuses a --session value that starts with a dash).

Two of the 'waits for the user' tests never reach the matching rule they claim to test. In tests/loop-approve-waits.bats, 'differs by one character' and 'matches an item not on this loop's list' put a requirement in the milestone whose text is not the item's; vbw loop next then ends the loop inside loop_open_item ('M1 has requirements of its own and is not shipped ... step open', action stopped) before loop_delegate/loop_matches run. I reproduced this in a scratch project: loop next answered stopped with that reason. These two tests would still pass if loop_matches always returned true, so the criterion 'one character differs / item not on the list waits' is not pinned. Regression test: reach the delegate step with the item in progress (let vbw loop next open the item, then change the requirement text by one character, or swap it for another backlog item's text, and re-plan) and assert nothing is approved, with a mutation check that loop_matches returning true makes it fail.

Unplanned behavior in vbw loop start: the 'current milestone has requirements and is not shipped' refusal now ignores a [human] requirement carried over by an earlier ship (cmd-loop.sh lines ~114-116, added in commit 0ab70375 under P127.2, whose plan lists no change to loop start). P127.1's plan and the criterion say the refusal applies to any requirement of the current milestone. No test in tests/loop-start.bats covers the exception (only tests/loop-approve.bats uses a carried-over human requirement, after start), and docs/loop.md's refusal table does not mention it. Either record the decision and document it, or remove it. Regression test: in a loop_project human fixture, 'vbw loop start T1 --no-ceiling' succeeds (or is refused, per the decision), and docs/loop.md states which.

A stopping loop whose session is gone cannot be ended or replaced, and the refusal's advice goes in a circle. Only the starting session's Stop hook (cmd-auto.sh line 59, .loop.session == session) runs loop_next, which is what turns 'stopping' into 'ended'. vbw loop start then refuses with 'a loop is already on. Next: run vbw loop status ... or vbw loop stop', and vbw loop stop answers 'already stopping' and changes nothing (I ran both in a scratch project). The criterion says each refusal names what to do instead; here the named remedy does nothing. Regression test: with a loop stopping and its session no longer running, the user has a documented command that ends it (or vbw loop start replaces a stopping loop), and the refusal text names it.

The Stop hook gate does not tell the loop step which session it runs for. auto_gate (plugin/lib/cmd-auto.sh) reads the session id from the hook's stdin but calls auto_loop_gate -> loop_next -> loop_step without exporting it; loop_step (plugin/lib/loop-step.sh) decides 'my own run' with vbw_session, which is VBW_SESSION_ID or CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID only (plugin/lib/core.sh:88). The skill's hook command (plugin/skills/loop/SKILL.md frontmatter) sets neither, and every other call in the skills passes VBW_SESSION_ID=${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} because the environment cannot be relied on. When the variable is empty, a build/plan/fix/QA run that this same session opened (lease.session = s1) is judged 'a lease of another session', and the loop ends with 'a run of another session (s1) is open' while its own workflow is still running. The criterion 'asks for nothing while this session's proof or workflow still runs' is therefore only met for the proof mark. tests/loop-gate.bats has no case with an open lease, and its gate helper pipes JSON to 'vbw auto gate' with no session in the environment, so this path is untested. Regression test: in tests/loop-gate.bats, start a loop for s1, open 'vbw run start build P2.1' as s1, then run the gate with session_id s1 and no VBW_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in the environment: it must print nothing and leave .loop.ended null (red today by reading the code; fix: auto_gate exports VBW_SESSION_ID=$session before the loop step).

The loop report's Shipped section prints the requirement id as 'none' for an item whose backlog text carries a marker. plugin/lib/loop-report.sh looks the requirement up with '.text == $i.text', but a loop item keeps its text with the '[human] ' (or '[auto] ') marker (loop_start stores loop_norm of the whole backlog text) while the requirement's text has the marker stripped (loop_item_text). Checked with the report's own expression on {item text '[human] The greeting feels friendly', requirement R2 'The greeting feels friendly'}: it returns "none". The criterion says the report names, for each shipped item, the item, milestone, requirement and commits. tests/loop-human-skip.bats and tests/loop-cycle.bats never read the requirement id on a Shipped line of a marked item. Regression test: ship a '[human] ...' item (and an '[auto] ...' item) through the loop and assert the Shipped line contains the requirement id (for example 'R2') and not 'none'; fix: compare against loop_item_text of the item's text.

A second 'vbw loop stop' no longer 'changes nothing'. The criterion and the plan (P127.1 task 4) say a loop already stopping prints that and changes nothing (no write, no commit). Since commit ec8cbf77 (the fix for QA finding F170) the second stop ends the loop: plugin/lib/cmd-loop.sh loop_stop calls loop_end, which writes .loop.ended, writes .vbw/loop-report.md and commits. docs/loop.md (line 68) and tests/loop-stop.bats (last test) describe the new behaviour, but R178's rule text still says 'a second stop changes nothing', and the test named 'stop with no loop on says so and exits 0; a second stop changes nothing' now asserts the opposite (.loop.ended != null). No recorded decision amends the criterion, so spec, test name and code disagree. Options: (a) recommended: record a decision that a second stop on a stopping loop ends it (the way out when its session is gone) and reword the R178 rule and that test's name; (b) revert to 'changes nothing' and instead let 'vbw loop start' replace a stopping loop whose session is gone. Regression test: one that fails if the requirement text, test names and loop_stop disagree, i.e. rename the test to say a second stop ends a stopping loop, and keep a separate test that stop on an ended or absent loop changes nothing (project_sum equal before and after).

Untested branch in the delegated approval: loop_delegate (plugin/lib/loop-step.sh) refuses to approve when vbw next's approve answer carries detail.files (docs/next.md row 4a, the approval of edited test files), and the plan (P127.2 task 2) and docs/loop.md both promise 'never the test-files-edited approval of row 4a'. No test exercises it: grep for '4a' or 'detail.files' in tests/loop-*.bats finds nothing, and tests/loop-approve-waits.bats covers only text differences, extra requirement, unlisted item, no loop, stopping, missing check file and spec/record drift. Removing the '(.detail.files == null)' clause would leave every loop test green, and the loop would then approve changed test files on the user's behalf. Regression test: in tests/loop-approve-waits.bats, make the contract approved except for an edit to a check's test file bytes with a built phase (row 4a), run the loop step with a loop whose items match, and assert nothing is approved, no consent is granted, no decision is recorded and vbw next still answers approve with detail.files; it must fail when the clause is removed.

The loop's outward guard (plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq, def loop_outward) only skips global options for git (git_words). For every other command it takes the first word that does not start with '-' as the subcommand, so an option VALUE or a toolchain selector before the subcommand hides the publish. I ran the def on parsed commands: 'cargo +nightly publish', 'npm --tag next publish', 'docker --context x push img' and 'gh -R a/b release create v1' all come out ALLOWED, while 'npm publish --tag next' and 'git --no-pager push' are denied. The phase says these commands are denied for every caller while a loop is on, and 'cargo +nightly publish' is a normal way to type it. Regression test to add in tests/loop-outward-guard.bats: under a loop, denied_as for 'cargo +nightly publish', 'npm --registry https://r.example publish', 'docker --context x push img', 'gh -R a/b release create v1', each with the pinned text; and the allowed list must still pass (gh -R a/b release list, cargo +nightly build).

The L3 loop scenario (tools/l3-suite.sh scenario_loop, committed tools/l3-results/loop.json) never exercised a real revert. The committed result has facts.revert_commits = 0, so the check 'the revert commits are in git' and the report check for revert hashes loop over an empty list and cannot fail. The plan (P129.4) asks for the revert commits present in git and the report naming them; commit 6667f15e changed the scenario so T2 fails by construction before any code commit, and allowed zero reverts. The result's not_tested list does not say that the git-revert path of a park was not run at L3 (it lists a remote, a mid-item ceiling, a [human] item, more than two items, Claude Code versions). The revert path is covered at L1 only (tests/loop-retry-park.bats). Regression test to add: either the scenario gives T2 a code commit so the park must revert it and the check fails when n_rev is 0, or loop.json/not_tested must say 'a park that reverts committed code' whenever facts.revert_commits is 0, pinned in tests/l3-loop.bats (a result with revert_commits 0 and no such not_tested entry fails).

Untested criterion: 'each item matches at most once'. plugin/lib/loop-step.sh loop_matches implements it (a requirement text may appear no more often than the loop has items with that text; I ran the rule on one item 'a b' and two requirements 'a b' and 'a  b': it answers no, correct). But no test exercises it: tests/loop-approve.bats, tests/loop-approve-waits.bats and the matches() test (F168) never put two requirements with the same text in the milestone, and 'vbw spec add' does not refuse duplicate texts, so the case is reachable. Replacing the count comparison with a plain 'every wanted text is in the item list' keeps every loop test green and would let the loop approve a contract that has an extra requirement duplicating an item's text. Regression test: in tests/loop-approve-waits.bats, loop with T1 only, add 'Visitors can read a greeting' twice, plan it, run the loop step; assert nothing is approved, no consent, no decision, vbw next still answers approve (and a second item with the same text makes it approve).

Two behaviours differ from the P127 plan text with no recorded decision. (1) plugin/lib/cmd-loop.sh loop_start (lines ~114-116) ignores a [human] requirement carried over by an earlier ship when it checks 'current milestone has requirements and is not shipped'; P127.1 and the criterion list that refusal without the exception. Found as F169, closed by documenting it (docs/loop.md) and adding a test, but 'vbw show decisions' has no decision for it (D322 is the only loop decision after D317). The test tests/loop-start.bats 'F169' also asserts '.milestone == .milestone' in jq, which compares a value to itself and cannot fail; it should check that R2 sits in the current milestone M2. (2) plugin/skills/loop/SKILL.md preamble has three lines (the 'vbw interview' line was added in commit 32ff7493 for R39, under P128.4); P127.3 says the preamble block has 'exactly two lines' and tests/loop-guard.bats does not pin the count. The R39 reason is sound, but it is an unrecorded change to P127.3's agreement. Fix: record one decision per item (vbw decide) naming the carried-human exception and the interview line, and make the F169 test assert the requirement is in M2. Regression test: tests/loop-start.bats F169 test must fail if R2 is not in the current milestone; tests/loop-guard.bats should pin the preamble's lines (interview, loop start, loop status).

The loop stalls silently, with no stop reason and no report, when a kernel step it runs in-process refuses. Evidence (read from code, not executed; a scratch test could not be written under the QA guard): plugin/lib/loop-step.sh loop_ship_item calls cmd_ship directly, and plugin/lib/cmd-ship.sh line 20 does vbw_die 'the proven work is not committed' for ANY untracked or modified file outside .vbw (git status --untracked-files=all), while vbw next still answers ship because the proof runs on a clean copy of HEAD. vbw_die ends the whole process (core.sh exit). In the Stop hook, plugin/lib/cmd-auto.sh auto_loop_gate takes 'step=$(loop_next)', which comes back empty, so the case falls to the block branch, jq reads nothing and prints nothing: the session stops, loop.ended stays null, .vbw/loop-report.md is not refreshed, and the next stop does the same. Same for the open step: loop_open_item's die text goes to stderr inside $(...), so the stop reason becomes ' (item T1, step open)' with the real cause lost. This breaks the phase criterion 'anything the loop cannot do without the user stops the loop with the reason, the item and the step, recorded in the loop state and the report' (P128.1 stops line). No tests/loop-*.bats test drives a failing ship/open (grep for 'not committed' in tests/loop-*.bats finds nothing). Regression test to add: in a loop fixture, leave an untracked file (e.g. stray.log) after the proof, run vbw loop next as the loop's session and through vbw auto gate; assert loop.ended.reason names 'not committed' with the item and step ship, the gate prints a systemMessage ending the loop, and .vbw/loop-report.md exists. Fix direction: have the loop step run the kernel action so a die is caught (run it in a subshell and capture stderr) and call loop_end with 'ACTION needs you: <message> (item T, step ACTION)'.

The loop's outward guard now blocks harmless reads and the project's own commands that merely contain a trigger word anywhere after the command name. Since b1df6d14 (the F175 fix), loop_outward in plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq (has($x) over every non-option word) matches the word at any position, not only as the subcommand. I drove the guard with a loop on (guard-bash.jq with a record holding .loop) and these are all DENIED: 'cargo test publish' (denied as cargo publish), 'cargo build -p publish', 'npm run publish', 'npm test -- publish', 'gh issue list --label release' and 'gh pr list --label release' (denied as gh release), 'docker run --name push ubuntu' (denied as docker push). The R180 rule says words in text, reads and the project's own commands stay allowed; a builder who runs a test filtered by the word 'publish' is blocked with a text claiming it ran cargo publish, which can park a good item. 'npm run publish' and 'gh issue list' were allowed before the F175 fix, so this is a regression. docs/guards.md says nothing of it. Regression test for tests/loop-outward-guard.bats: under a loop the allowed list also holds 'cargo test publish', 'npm run publish', 'gh issue list --label release', 'docker run --name push ubuntu', while 'cargo +nightly publish', 'npm --tag next publish', 'docker --context x push img' and 'gh -R a/b release create v1' stay denied (the subcommand is the first word after the command's own options and their values, not any word).

Untested branches of the park (plugin/lib/loop-park.sh). The criterion says a file the user staged or edited by hand is left as it is. The only test, tests/loop-retry-park.bats test 1, edits README.md and adds scratch.txt, files no commit of the item touched, so it passes whether or not the protection exists. Nothing exercises: a commit touching a file the user edited or staged (left unreverted and named 'you changed F'), a check file the user changed (kept, 'left in place'), a revert that conflicts ('does not revert cleanly'), or the user's staged file staying staged after a revert. Deleting the 'hand' comparison or the vbw_dirty_files test would leave every loop test green, and the park would then revert over the user's work. Regression test in tests/loop-retry-park.bats: build an item, then edit (unstaged) and separately stage a file that an item commit touched, park, and assert that commit is not reverted, the file keeps the user's content and stays staged, the decision names it, and the other commits are reverted; plus one with a user-edited check file that survives the park.

Untested P129.1 behaviour. The validation rules for the parked list in plugin/lib/record.jq lines 138-148 (non-empty reason, unknown field, parked twice, both shipped and parked, current milestone parked exactly when in parked, a parked milestone owning a requirement, phase or plan) have no test that makes any of them fire (grep of tests/ finds none; the park tests only build valid records). The same holds for 'vbw milestone rename' refusing a parked milestone (cmd-milestone.sh) and for 'vbw status --json' carrying the parked ids (cmd-status.sh line 18). Removing any of these would leave the suite green. Regression test: in tests/record.bats a hand-edited record for each rule must fail validation with its message; 'vbw milestone rename X' on a parked milestone exits non-zero with a Next line; 'vbw status --json | jq .parked' lists M2 after a park.

The L3 loop scenario's git check for revert commits can still pass with none, and the honest-labelling branch is unpinned. After F176 the scenario (tools/l3-suite.sh scenario_loop) loops over the parked item's reverts, so with zero reverts 'the revert commits are in git' passes vacuously (reverts_ok stays true); only when n_rev is 0 does the result's not_tested gain the line saying the revert path was not run. No test in tests/l3-loop.bats reads that branch: a result with facts.revert_commits 0 and without that not_tested line, or the line deleted from the script, leaves tests/l3-loop.bats green. The committed loop.json has revert_commits 1, so today's result is honest, but the guard against a future dishonest one is missing. Regression test in tests/l3-loop.bats: every committed tools/l3-results/loop.json with facts.revert_commits == 0 must have a not_tested entry naming the revert path; and the scenario body must hold that conditional.

The loop report cannot be trusted for an item that was still running when the loop ended. plugin/lib/loop-report.sh line 43 prints every in-progress item's cost as 'in progress, not counted yet', also after the loop has ended (a ceiling stop, vbw loop stop, an unknown action, a refused ship all end the loop with the item still in progress). But the 'Loop total' line above it is loop_spend, which does count that item's spend (baseline to now). So after such a stop the report shows a total that no item line explains, and the item that cost the most (the one the loop was working on when it stopped) shows no dollars and no tokens, though VBW has the figure. The criterion says the report gives the loop's total and each item's cost in dollars and tokens, unknown only where VBW saw no figure. The same item also appears nowhere else (not in Shipped, Parked or Waiting for you), and the ceiling stop reason does not name it, so the morning reader cannot tell which item was left half done. Regression test, in tests/loop-report.bats: start a loop with two items and a ceiling, take the first to a point where figures exist and the ceiling is reached while T1 is in progress, let the step stop the loop, then assert the report's Cost section gives T1 a dollar and token figure that equals what vbw loop status shows (not 'not counted yet'), and that it names T1 as left in progress; with no figures it must say unknown.

Untested branches of the park remain after the F181 fix. plugin/lib/loop-park.sh decides what to leave alone from 'git diff --name-only HEAD' (staged and unstaged changes), leaves a check file the user changed ('left in place (you changed it)') and leaves a commit that 'does not revert cleanly'. The only added test (tests/loop-retry-park.bats, the F181 test, commit ffcdcfe0) appends to a file with a plain unstaged edit. Nothing stages a file, nothing edits a check file, nothing makes a revert conflict (grep 'staged', 'left in place (you', 'revert cleanly' in tests/loop-*.bats finds nothing but comments). The criterion says a file the user STAGED or edited is left as it is. Changing the dirty list to plain 'git diff --name-only' (unstaged only), dropping the vbw_dirty_files test on check files, or removing the conflict branch keeps every loop test green, and the park would then revert over the user's staged work. Regression tests to add in tests/loop-retry-park.bats: (1) stage (git add) a change to a file an item commit touched, park, assert the commit is not reverted, the file keeps the staged content and stays staged, and the decision names 'you changed FILE'; also stage an unrelated file and assert it stays staged after the reverts; (2) edit a check file of the item by hand, park, assert the file stays and the decision says 'left in place (you changed it)'; (3) make a later commit conflict with an earlier item commit, park, assert the decision says 'does not revert cleanly' and no half-done revert is left (git status clean of conflict markers).

Untested P129.1 behaviour remains after the F182 fix: 'vbw milestone rename' refusing a parked milestone. plugin/lib/cmd-milestone.sh refuses with '<M> has been parked: start the next one (vbw milestone start TITLE)', but no test runs 'milestone rename' on a parked milestone (grep 'milestone rename' in tests/ finds only kernel-work.bats, which uses a shipped milestone). The test named 'a parked milestone keeps its name, and vbw status --json lists the parked ids' in tests/loop-park-report.bats never calls rename and never checks the title after the park, so its name promises more than it checks. Removing 'parked' from the refusal branch would leave the suite green. Regression test: after a park, 'vbw milestone rename Other' exits 1 with a message containing 'parked' and 'vbw milestone start', and .milestone.title is unchanged.

Plan task left out: P129.1 task 2 says 'next.jq row 1 and docs', but docs/next.md row 1 still reads 'milestone shipped' only (line 103) and says nothing of a parked milestone (grep -i parked docs/next.md finds nothing); lines 16-18 about requirements of shipped milestones are likewise unchanged. next.jq line 93 answers action milestone for status parked, so the documentation of the decision table is now wrong for users who read it. Regression test: tests/loop-docs.bats (or a next-docs test) asserts docs/next.md row 1 names both shipped and parked.

Unrecorded change to the plan, and undocumented. P129.2 task 2 says the commits since the item's head that touch a file outside .vbw/ are reverted, leaving unreverted only a commit touching a file the user staged or edited. plugin/lib/loop-park.sh (commit f6d1c7c1) also leaves a commit that changes code and a .vbw file together ('changes the record too') and a commit that 'does not revert cleanly', so a parked item can keep part of its code in the tree. 'vbw show decisions' has no decision for it (D322 and D324 are the only loop decisions after D317), and docs/loop.md 'Retry once, then park' step 2 does not say a commit can be left and named; a user reading it expects the item's code to be gone. The behaviour is defensible (reverting a record-touching commit would corrupt the record) but it is a deviation until decided. Fix: record one decision (vbw decide) for the mixed-commit and conflict cases, and add a sentence to docs/loop.md step 1 that a commit it cannot revert is left, named in the decision and the report. Regression test: tests/loop-docs.bats asserts docs/loop.md mentions that such a commit is left and named.

tests/loop-lease-guards.bats cannot tell whether the protected-check-file rule works under a loop. The test (first test, line ~38) writes tests/notes.sh, which is protected but not among the build lease's files (src/greet.txt), and accepts either 'protected check file' or 'outside this run's files'. lease_write_denial in plugin/hooks/common.jq checks the plan's files first, so the denial always comes from the outside-files rule and the protected rule is never reached. Deleting the protected rule leaves this test green. The criterion lists 'a protected check file' among the writes a loop's run still denies. Regression test: a lease whose files include a protected check file (a fix run with new_tests, or a build whose plan file list holds it) must be denied with 'protected check file', asserted without the either-or.

The L3 loop scenario writes facts it did not measure. tools/l3-suite.sh scenario_loop passes the constants 'remotes: 0, tags: 0' into result_write instead of the counts it read (, ), so a failing run (a remote or tag present, passed=false) would still publish 'remotes: 0, tags: 0' in tools/l3-results/loop.json. Also the committed result (at 2026-10-13T00:13:07Z) predates commits e31332b7 (loop_kernel) and 469ef59c (guard change), so it describes older code. Regression test in tests/l3-loop.bats: the scenario body builds the facts from the measured remote and tag counts (no literal 'remotes: 0'), and a run with a remote present would write a nonzero fact.

The loop report loses a [human] item's requirement and commits, and its 'Waiting for you' entry, as soon as a later item opens. Cause: vbw milestone start (plugin/lib/cmd-milestone.sh line 37) moves every 'later' requirement into the new milestone (.milestone = new id, and del(.skipped, .later)). The loop opens the next item's milestone in the same step that ships the first (loop_open_item, plugin/lib/loop-step.sh), so for a list like T3 ([human]) then T1 the report (plugin/lib/loop-report.sh) looks up the shipped item's requirement by '.milestone == $i.milestone' (line 32) and its commits through plans_of($i.milestone) (line 21): both now find nothing. I ran those two jq expressions on a record shaped as the kernel leaves it (R2 [human] moved to M3, item T3 shipped in M2): output 'T3 milestone M2 req none plans []', so the Shipped line reads '(M2, none): ' with no commits. The Waiting section selects '.skipped == true' (line 41), which the move deleted, so it prints 'no skipped [human] requirement' while the user's judgment is still owed; if the loop then stops (ceiling, vbw loop stop) before item 2 reaches accept, the report never lists it. The criterion says the report names, for what shipped, the item, milestone, requirement and commits, and lists skipped [human] requirements as waiting for the user; docs/loop.md 'The report' says the same. Existing tests only use one [human] item at the end of the list (tests/loop-human-skip.bats) or a [human] requirement carried in before the loop (loop_project human), so none moves it. Regression test: in tests/loop-human-skip.bats start a loop with the [human] item first and an [auto] item second, take the first to its ship, let the step open the second item's milestone, then assert that .vbw/loop-report.md's Shipped line for the [human] item names its requirement id (not 'none') and its commits, and that 'Waiting for you' lists the carried [human] requirement; the fix has to keep the requirement and plans attributed to the milestone the item shipped in (for example by recording the requirement id and the commit list on the item when it ships) and to find waiting [human] requirements by their state (open, proof human, built in an earlier milestone), not by the skipped flag.

The sentence in docs/loop.md (Retry once, then park, step 2) that says three kinds of commit are left in place and named (you staged or edited the file, it changes code and a .vbw file together, it does not revert cleanly) has no test. Fix F188 asked for a regression test in tests/loop-docs.bats that fails if the sentence is removed. grep for 'left in place', 'revert cleanly', 'left and named' and 'D326' across tests/*.bats finds nothing in loop-docs.bats or any other docs test (the only hits are the behaviour tests in loop-retry-park.bats). Deleting the sentence from docs/loop.md keeps every test green, so the documentation can drift back to saying the item's code is always gone. Regression test: in tests/loop-docs.bats, assert docs/loop.md contains the three phrases (staged or edited, code and a .vbw file together, does not revert cleanly) and 'named'.

The F185 conflict test does not prove what F185 asked for. tests/loop-retry-park.bats 'a commit that does not revert cleanly is left in place and named; the clean ones are reverted' (line ~206) is titled as if clean commits get reverted, but its own comment and its assertion '! git log | grep ^Revert' show none is. It also never checks that a failed revert leaves no half-done state: no assertion on .git/REVERT_HEAD, conflict markers in src/greet.txt, or a clean 'git status --porcelain' (grep for REVERT_HEAD, '<<<<<<<', unmerged and porcelain finds only .vbw checks in parked_clean, which this test does not call). F185 listed 'no half-done revert is left (git status clean of conflict markers)' explicitly. The revert --abort in plugin/lib/loop-park.sh (the else branch) can be removed without this test noticing. Regression test: after the park, assert no .git/REVERT_HEAD, no '<<<<<<<' in src/greet.txt, 'git status --porcelain' empty for tracked files, and that the park commit exists; and add a case where one item commit conflicts and another reverts cleanly so the title is true (or rename the test).

vbw loop park refuses when a run (lease) is open, but nothing tests that branch. P129.2 task 3 says the command refuses with Next: for no loop, no item in progress, or an open lease. plugin/lib/cmd-loop.sh loop_park_cmd has the 'a run is open. Next: wait for it to end' branch; the only test of by-hand refusals (tests/loop-retry-park.bats line 143) covers the no-loop and no-item cases. grep 'a run is open' in tests finds nothing for loop park. Deleting the lease check lets a park revert commits and rewrite the record while a Dev is still writing. Regression test: start a loop, get an item in progress, open a run (vbw run start build ...), run vbw loop park, assert exit 1, 'Next: ', the item still in_progress, no Revert commit, and the record unchanged.

The cost half of P129.1 has no test. A parked milestone is treated like a shipped one in plugin/lib/costs.sh (costs_milestone_total returns the frozen total, else null, for an id in .parked) and in plugin/lib/cmd-show.sh (vbw show costs lists parked ids with status parked). No test file under tests/ that mentions parked runs vbw show costs or costs_milestone_total (parked appears only in l3-loop, loop-docs, loop-report, loop-park-report, loop-retry-park; none calls show costs). The park test only checks the frozen total in the record at park time. If the .parked branch in costs_milestone_total were removed, a parked milestone with no frozen figure would be priced as a live milestone and its cost would keep changing after the park, and vbw show costs would be wrong, with every test still green. Regression test in tests/cost-milestones.bats or loop-park-report.bats: park an item (a) with figures, assert vbw show costs --json lists the milestone as parked with the frozen total and that later spend in the session does not change it; (b) without figures, assert the parked milestone's total is null (unknown) and stays null after more spend.

The record format check for a loop item's own fields has no test that can fail. plugin/lib/record.jq (loop_item) validates milestone, head (40 hex), baseline, retried, reverts, left, req, cost, reason and at, but the only test of malformed loops, tests/loop-help-docs.bats test 4, edits just 8 things (.loop = {}, items not an array, a bad status, a bad ceiling, started_at, an extra loop key, a bad item id). P127.1 task 1 promised that this test 'lists the malformed loops that must be refused'. The newest clause, req (added in d6ba592f for F191: '(has("req")|not) or (.req|nonempty)'), and the earlier left clause can be deleted or loosened and every test stays green; the only req test (loop-human-skip.bats line 93) checks the valid case. The loop report's 'Waiting for you' section drops a [human] requirement that an earlier ship carried into the loop's milestone (not one of the loop's own items) as soon as the next item's milestone opens. Trace: such a requirement (loop_project human: R2) is open, proof human, in the current milestone, so vbw next says accept and the loop skips it (plugin/lib/loop-step.sh, accept case; skipped=true). vbw ship marks it later; the next item's 'vbw milestone start' (plugin/lib/cmd-milestone.sh line 38) moves it on and deletes .skipped and .later. plugin/lib/loop-report.sh then lists waiting requirements only from (a) shipped loop items with proof human, or (b) '.skipped == true and .status == "open"'. R2 is neither, so a report written after that point (a ceiling stop, vbw loop stop, a refused step or a park while the second item is in progress) prints 'no skipped [human] requirement' while the judgment is still owed. This is the second half of F191's instruction (find waiting [human] requirements by their state, not by the skipped flag), which the fix covered only for the loop's own [human] items; docs/loop.md line 290 promises 'the [human] requirements the loop skipped and you have not judged yet'. Found by reading the code paths; I could not run the scenario because the QA run's guard allows no scratch files. Fix direction: select waiting [human] requirements by state (proof human, status open, built in a phase of an earlier milestone, or skipped), the same predicate loop_matches uses for carried requirements.

So the loop approves a changed command (D315) and nothing in the record or git says so, against the criterion that the loop records that it approved on the user's behalf. Regression test (tests/loop-approve.bats): loop approves the contract, then the spec's test command is changed and spec sync run; after vbw loop next either a decision naming the loop and the command exists with an approval commit, or no command consent is granted; assert one of the two, and that the consent count never grows without a decision.

When the last item ships with the spend at or above the ceiling (default mode, no --finish-item), the loop reports 'ceiling reached' and answers 'stopped' instead of 'end of the list: N shipped, M parked' and 'done'. Evidence: plugin/lib/loop-step.sh lines 187-209: after loop_ship_item returns, the while loop re-runs; the ceiling check at lines 202-205 runs before the 'no waiting item' end-of-list branch at lines 207-209, and the check is skipped only for --finish-item. P128.1 task 3 and the criterion 'End of list: the loop stops after the last item's ship' say the ship with none waiting ends the loop with the end-of-list reason and {action: done}. Effect: nothing was cut off, yet the Stop hook message, 'vbw loop status', the record's ended.reason and the report ('Waiting for you': 'the loop stopped: ceiling reached') say a limit stopped work, and the answer is 'stopped', not 'done'. No test covers it: tests/loop-stops.bats has the ceiling cases only with an item still waiting (--finish-item case ends 'stopped' with T2 waiting, which is right). A regression test should: start a loop with one item and --ceiling 5, drive it to the prove step, raise the session figures above 5, run the proof, and assert the step answers done with reason matching 'end of the list: 1 shipped, 0 parked' and loop.ended.reason is that text. Fix: judge the ceiling only when a step or an item opening is still due (skip it when no item is in progress and none is waiting).

QA verdicts of phases that share a requirement interfere: the pass of P129 (R179, R180) at 12:51:03 closed F203, opened two seconds earlier by the fail of P128 (R179), because vbw qa record PHASE pass closes every open QA fix on the phase's requirements (plugin/lib/cmd-qa.sh, the .fixes map) whatever phase found it; a fail likewise closes another phase's fixed fixes. In a loop this repeats every round (P128 re-files, P129 closes) until the ceiling. Fix: a finding belongs to the phase whose QA found it (vbw qa finding PHASE REQ TEXT; a fail verdict adopts the untagged open findings on its requirements), a verdict changes only its own phase's findings (an untagged one keeps today's rule), the record allows and validates the fix's phase field, docs/proof.md and docs/record.md and the QA agent's instructions name the form. Regression test: two phases sharing a requirement; a finding of the first and then the second's pass leave it open; the first's pass closes it; the fail verdict tags an untagged finding.

Re-filed F203, which P129's pass closed (see F204): when the last item ships with the spend at or above the ceiling (default mode, no --finish-item), the loop ends with 'ceiling reached' and answers stopped instead of 'end of the list: N shipped, M parked' and done, because loop_step judges the ceiling before the end-of-list branch (plugin/lib/loop-step.sh). Fix: judge the ceiling only when a step or an item opening is still due, never when no item is in progress and none is waiting. Regression test in tests/loop-stops.bats: one item, --ceiling 5, session figures above 5 before the proof; the step after the proof answers done with the reason 'end of the list: 1 shipped, 0 parked', and loop.ended.reason is that text; the report says the loop ended on the end of the list.

The loop's outward guard (plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq, loop_outward) lets a push through when the redirect is written against the subcommand with no space: with a loop on, 'git push>out.log' and 'npm publish>log' are not denied (probed by piping the hook input through guard-bash.jq with a loop record: 'git push', 'git push origin main>/dev/null 2>&1', 'git push </dev/null' are denied, 'git push>/dev/null' and 'git push>out.log' are allowed). Cause: simple() in guard-bash.jq only splits a redirect off a word when the word starts with the operator, so 'push>out.log' stays one word and git_words reads it as an unknown subcommand. R180 and the plan say git push in any form is denied while a loop is on, and every outward command shares this reading. Regression test: in tests/loop-outward-guard.bats, with a loop on, 'git push>/dev/null', 'git push>out.log', 'npm publish>log' and 'docker push>x' must be denied with the pinned text (and 'echo hi>out.log' must stay allowed).

Found by L3 loop scenario run 12 (15:05): the session applied T1's contract with vbw apply --add and ended its turn before writing the check file tests/greet_test.sh (a model slip the small-change plan path allows); the Stop hook ran the loop step, vbw next answered contract (the contract is not ready: check file missing), and loop_step treats contract as an action it does not know, so the loop ended at 14:06:00 with 'contract needs you' after 29 seconds, T1 in progress and T2 waiting. A not-ready contract during the plan step is the session's own unfinished work, not a stop: the loop must hand it back to the session once (emit the contract step through the gate), and end only when the same unsatisfied contract comes back unchanged (asked once already). Regression test: a loop whose contract names a check file not yet written answers contract with the instruction and records what it asked; the same step again ends the loop naming that it asked once already; with the check file written after the first ask, the next step approves by delegation and moves to build.

The computer-wide limit can be lost in the middle of a run without a word, which the criterion forbids ('its output says once, in one plain line, that the limit was not in force and why'). The line is printed only by slots_open, when the run starts (plugin/lib/slots.sh lines 118-140). Later failures go through slots_take (line ~163: 'slots_apply ... || { SLOTS_STATE=off; return 0; }') and slots_give (line ~213: '|| SLOTS_STATE=off'); both turn the limit off and print nothing. slots_apply can fail mid-run in three ways: slots_lock gives up after 600 tries (about 30 s) when the lock stays busy (a waiting unit polls the store every 0.1 s and each locked step runs about 6 jq calls, so many waiting units across many sessions queue up on it, which is the heavy-load case this phase exists for); the folder becomes unwritable; another process leaves the file damaged. In each case the unit then runs with no slot and the user is never told. In a parallel run it is worse: slots_take runs in a runner subshell, so SLOTS_STATE=off stays inside that one runner and its stderr goes to the hidden N.err file. Also the 'lock gave up' branch is untested. Regression test: with the limit at 1 and the store made unwritable or replaced by junk after a run has started (for example by a unit of that run, or a hook between the first and second unit), prove/check/fix done must still pass and print exactly one 'vbw: the computer-wide limit was not in force: ...' line on the user-visible output; and a lock held by a live process for over 30 s must either keep waiting or print that line, never run silently without a slot. Fix direction: turn the failure into one shared signal (a marker file in CHECK_OUT that the runners write and the parent reads) and have slots_say print the line once at the end, and make the lock wait unbounded while its owner is alive (a live owner is not an error).

The output line added by commit 9aacd2ca (slots_say in plugin/lib/slots.sh:219, 'vbw: the computer-wide limit was not in force: <reason>; this run was limited by check_jobs (N) alone from then on', printed once at the end when the store fails mid-run) has no test pinning its exact wording. tests/machine-midrun.bats only counts lines containing 'computer-wide limit was not in force' (one per run), so changing the reason text, the check_jobs number or the 'from then on' ending would not fail any test. Criterion 5 of R181 requires each new output line to have a test pinning its exact wording and the condition that prints it. Regression test should assert the full line for both reasons: 'cannot write <store path>' (read-only folder case) and '<store path> is damaged (delete it to restore the limit)' (junk file case), with the real check_jobs value, in check, prove and fix done; and that the line is on stderr and printed once.

In plugin/hooks/session-start.sh the loaded-copy error message can be thrown away. When a --plugin-dir session cannot write CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, the hook sets context='VBW could not put the loaded copy first on PATH: run <tree>/bin/vbw ...'. Two lines later the old line '[ "$removed" -eq 0 ] || context="VBW removed ..."' assigns context without keeping the earlier text, so when VBW 1 command copies were also removed in the same start, Claude is never told to run <tree>/bin/vbw and its agents silently run the installed release (the user still sees the systemMessage). That line was safe before this phase because context was always empty there. Same pattern for notice: the 'project made by a newer VBW' branch assigns notice='This project was made by a newer VBW...' and drops the 'could not put first on PATH' message the user should see. Evidence: code read of plugin/hooks/session-start.sh after commit 10a93f0b (I could not run it: the QA guard forbids writes). Regression test: tests/plugindir-path.bats should start a loaded session with CLAUDE_ENV_FILE unset (1) with a VBW 1 command copy present in the Claude config folder, and (2) in a project whose record is newer than the kernel; in both the hook output must still name $PLUGIN_ROOT/bin/vbw in additionalContext and systemMessage. Fix: append (context="${context}...", notice="${notice:+$notice }...") instead of assigning.

plugin/hooks/session-start.sh line 56 (commit 10a93f0b): 'while IFS= read -t 1 -r line; do input=$input$line; done' keeps looping after the first JSON line. If Claude Code leaves the hook's stdin pipe open (the comment on lines 53-54 says it may, and the plan says 'read the hook input without ever blocking'), every session start waits a full extra second. Measured: printf '{"session_id":"abc"}\n'; sleep 4 piped into the hook took 1.03 s wall, 0.03 s CPU (same hook with </dev/null: 0.03 s). The hook never read stdin before this phase, so this is new latency at every session start, and no test pins the open-pipe case. The input is one line, so one bounded read is enough. Regression test (tests/plugindir-path.bats): feed the hook one JSON line from a producer that keeps the pipe open for 3 s and assert the hook finishes in well under 1 s and still records session s1 (and a --plugin-dir session still writes the PATH line). Fix: read a single line ('IFS= read -r -t 1 input || true') instead of looping. Minor, not in doctor: vbw doctor builds the session-record path from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID without the plain-name check the hook and status line apply (read only, so no write risk).

vbw mutate (plugin/lib/cmd-mutate.sh, lines 119-125, commit 8d26c179 / original 3be3c530) stopped refusing a changed-but-uncommitted check file whenever the lease kind is build. R188.5 says a break with a check file 'changed beside the break' is refused, writing nothing; the new code only keeps that refusal outside a build run. Inside a build run the checks still run on a detached copy of HEAD (plugin/lib/proofcopy.sh:91), so a Dev who strengthened tests/x.sh and re-ran vbw mutate before committing gets a recorded survivor from the OLD test, with no warning. That wastes one of the Dev's two strengthening attempts (dev.md: two attempts then vbw plan block) and records a false survivor. The plan's task 2 only asked for adding the survivor's files to the lease editable list, not for relaxing this refusal, and no test pins the relaxed branch (tests/mutate-command.bats:102-122 runs with no lease; tests/mutate-strengthen.bats never runs vbw mutate with an uncommitted check file). A regression test should open a build run, record a survivor, change the check file without committing, run vbw mutate, and expect a refusal naming the file (commit them first), nothing written to the record.

docs/workflows.md lines 213-216 (section 'The mutation check') say: 'The command refuses, and writes nothing, if the plan's files differ from their last commit, a file is outside the plan, or a check file is touched.' The first condition is the opposite of the code. plugin/lib/cmd-mutate.sh refuses when NONE of the named files differs from the last commit ('nothing to check: none of the named files differs from the last commit'), because the break itself is the difference; it never refuses because a plan file differs. Rule R188.3 reads 'nothing differing from the plan's last commit is refused'. A Dev or user reading the guide would think a dirty working file blocks the command, when a dirty (broken) file is what it needs. Evidence: L1, reading cmd-mutate.sh lines 105-118 against the docs text and the rule list in vbw show req R188. tests/mutation-docs.bats does not pin this sentence (it checks single words in the section, plus the one 'at standard and deep / never at express / never in a fix' line). A regression test should assert the refusal sentence says that a break which changes none of the named files is refused (words such as 'nothing' or 'none' with 'differs'), and be shown red with the current inverted wording.

tests/mutation-docs.bats, test 'docs/rigor.md gives express, standard and deep each its own content': the first negated line '! line_has rigor.md express "each rule" > /dev/null' is not the last command of the test, so bash errexit (bats) ignores it and it can never fail. Evidence: L1, 'bash -c "set -eET; f(){ return 0; }; ! f; echo reached"' prints reached; by reading, only the final '! line_has rigor.md standard nothing' is enforced. So an express row such as 'nothing, each rule: one small break per rule' keeps all 11 tests green although it says express breaks each rule (F227 asked that express and standard each keep their own content). A regression test should replace both negations with 'run line_has ...; [ "$status" -ne 0 ]' (or if line_has; then false; fi) and be shown red when the express row also says 'each rule'.

A late step with parts only moves its end for a build. Criterion (D424) says any step with parts: once its own pace (time so far / parts done x parts left) ends after the first end time, the current end moves to that projection and is marked later than usual; it can move again. Only plugin/lib/steps.sh step_plan_done does this, and it selects $n.kind == "build" (line 210). A fix step's parts go up in plugin/lib/proofsteps.sh proofsteps_fix_done (lines 193-204) and a proof's own parts in proofsteps_note_update (lines 116-127); neither projects the pace, so end stays equal to first_end and late stays false. Fix and proof both have parts (step_kind_has_parts, steps.sh line 75), and docs/panel.md lines 512-515 promise the move for 'a step with parts'. What shows instead: step_words prints 'until around HH:MM, later than usual' with an end time already in the past, never a new time. tests/step-note.bats line 73 only covers a build, and no test in tests/step-proof.bats checks late on a fix or proof. Regression test: seed 3 proofs (and 3 fixes) with history, start a proof of its own (or fix) of N units, back-date its started_at so the pace is past first_end, finish one unit (or close one fix) and expect end > first_end and late == true in the note, then a second unit moving it again, and never earlier than first_end.

The status line leaves out 'later than usual' when a step with parts is past its end but the kernel has not moved the end, while 'vbw status', 'vbw next' and the panel say it. Evidence: plugin/lib/steps.sh step_words and plugin/hooks/panel-step.js stepWords say '..., later than usual' when parts exist and (note.late is true OR the end is already past); plugin/scripts/statusline.jq step_line (line ~76) says it only when $n.late is true. The kernel sets late only in step_plan_done (plugin/lib/steps.sh), which handles builds only and only after a plan finishes. So a build whose first plan overruns its first end, any fix, and a proof past its end show a past clock time in the status line with no caveat, while Comms/vbw status say 'until around 14:20, later than usual'. docs/statusline.md ('A step with parts past its time reads until 14:35, later than usual') and docs/panel.md ('When a step with parts runs past its end time, VBW moves the end to this run's own pace and shows ... later than usual. It can move again') state this as always true; for a fix, a proof, or a build with no plan done yet the end is never moved. Regression test should catch: a note with parts, late:false and end in the past must make the status line first line read 'until HH:MM, later than usual' (as vbw status does for the same note), and the docs must say that the end moves only when a plan of a build finishes (or the kernel must move the end for fixes and proofs).

Status line and the other two surfaces disagree once a step with parts runs past its end and the kernel has not moved the end yet. plugin/scripts/statusline.jq step_line adds ', later than usual' only when the note has late==true. The kernel (plugin/lib/steps.sh step_words line 41) and panel-step.js stepWords say 'later than usual' when late==true OR the end is already past (left <= 0). The kernel moves the end only at 'vbw plan done' (steps.sh line 213: no change while done==0), so a build whose first plan overruns shows in Mission Control, Comms and 'vbw status': 'until around 14:20, later than usual', but in the status line a bare past time 'until 14:20' with no marker. The criterion asks the same marker on every surface for a late step with parts. tests/statusline-step.bats only covers late==true. Regression test should write a build note with parts {done:0,total:2}, late:false and end in the past, and require the status line to read 'until HH:MM, later than usual' as panel-step.js does for the same note and moment.

step_proof_units (plugin/lib/steps.sh, lines 359-361, added by P149.1 commit 166c87e0) builds the proof's unit names with one separate jq process per unit, appending to a growing JSON string. vbw next --json runs it every time the next step is a proof. A micro-benchmark of the same loop for 400 units took 1.5 s (this repo's full proof has 398 units, steps.json shows it); the cost grows with the square of the unit count (every spawn re-parses the whole list) and is paid on each vbw next, where the old code counted with plain arithmetic. The same phase already has the cheap design: prove_unit_names (plugin/lib/cmd-prove.sh) pipes the names through one jq (proofsteps_names). The two lists also disagree: step_proof_units names every TODO_CHECKS entry (held ones too) and every TODO_COMMANDS entry (unapproved ones too), while prove_unit_names, used when the proof really starts, leaves out held checks and commands the user has not approved. So next --json can size a proof by units that the proof then does not run. Regression test: with a fixture of 30 approved checks, count the jq processes step_proof_units starts (a PATH shim that logs each call) and require the count not to grow with the unit count; and a fixture with one unapproved project command and one held check must give the same unit names from step_proof_units as the proof's own note uses (parts and expected seconds equal between vbw next --json and the proof's note).

Lead review of P168.2 (2026-10-26): plugin/lib/cmd-doctor.sh, doctor_project, the hidden-file loop (while IFS= read -r hid; do doctor_line fail ...; done < <(cd "$VBW_ROOT" && record_hidden || true)) prints through doctor_line (a printf) in the shell that owns the process substitution's live child. The standard forbids a builtin write there (macOS /bin/bash 3.2 loses a write interrupted by the child's exit: CLAUDE.md, 'No builtin write while the shell has a live child'); tools/check-loop-writes.sh passes only because the write sits inside a called function, which its header leaves to the reviewer. Fix: collect the lines first (hidden=$(cd "$VBW_ROOT" && record_hidden) || true), then loop over the variable with a here-string (done <<< "$hidden"; [ -n "$hidden" ] first), so no child is alive while doctor_line prints; a pipe is not an option because doctor_line sets DOCTOR_FAILED in the main shell. Regression test, shown red first: in tests/hidden-record-commands.bats, cmd-doctor.sh has no loop fed by a process substitution that calls doctor_line (grep on the shell file, not JSON), kept narrow; the doctor fail case stays green under /bin/bash.

A listed path that sits INSIDE an ignored folder is accepted by 'vbw spec check/sync' but is not left out of the clean copy. Example: .gitignore has 'data/', the spec lists '- data/raw/'. Verify (plugin/lib/cmd-spec.sh spec_verify_leave_out) accepts it: git check-ignore succeeds on the parent rule and nothing is tracked/stray (I checked the same shape read-only in this repo: a_non_prod_docs/brandkit passes all three git checks). But plugin/lib/proofcopy.sh proofcopy_make lists ignored paths with 'git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory', which gives the whole folder as one entry 'data/'; the skip test 'case $p in $L | $L/*' only matches when the entry equals or is below the listed path, so 'data' vs 'data/raw' never matches and the whole of data/, raw/ included, is copied in. The user gets an approved contract line 'clean copy leaves out: data/raw/' while the big folder is still copied: the phase goal and criterion 4 ('skips a listed path and everything under it') and docs/proof.md ('skips the listed paths') are false for this case. tests/clean-copy-proof.bats only covers the listed folder being the ignored one, or its files ignored one by one. Fix idea: after copying an entry p that is a proper parent of a listed path L, remove $copy/L from the copy (or copy p's children one by one around L). Regression test: ignore 'data/' as a whole, list 'data/sub/', run vbw prove with the probe; the copy must hold data/a.bin and nothing of data/sub, and it must fail without the fix.

pathlib.Path(p).write_text('x') with p a variable is NOT refused, while pathlib.Path('src/pay.py').write_text('x') is. Cause: unreadable_calls in plugin/hooks/guard-bash.jq anchors Path with (?<![.\w]), so the 'pathlib.' form is skipped, but program_writes uses \bPath( and reads it as a write call head. The criterion says every call head program_writes reads is judged. Probe: run the Bash guard hook on 'python3 -c "import pathlib; pathlib.Path(p).write_text(1)"' under a lease: no answer (allowed). Regression test: a case in tests/guard-interpreters.bats where 'pathlib.Path(p).write_text' / 'pathlib.Path(d, "x").unlink()' on a build lease gets the 'cannot name' refusal.

A JS write called on any receiver other than fs/os/etc is NOT refused when the target is a variable: node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync(p, 'x')" passes, while require('fs').writeFileSync('src/other.js','x') is refused. Same for destructured calls (writeFileSync(p,'x') after const {writeFileSync} = require('fs')) and any 'x.writeFile(p, ...)'. Cause: program_writes reads the generic '.(writeFile|writeFileSync|appendFile|appendFileSync|createWriteStream|unlink|unlinkSync|rmSync|rmdirSync|mkdirSync|makedirs|rmtree|truncate)(' head on any receiver, but unreadable_calls only knows the receivers os|fs|File|FileUtils|shutil|Dir. require('fs').writeFileSync(...) is the usual node -e form, so the F323 hole stays open for Node. Regression test: node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync(p, 'x')" and a heredoc form must get the 'cannot name' refusal.

Ruby and Perl calls written without parentheses are NOT refused when the target is a variable: ruby -e 'File.write p, "x"', ruby -e 'File.delete p', ruby -e 'FileUtils.rm_rf d', perl -e 'open FH, ">", $p' all pass, while the same calls with a literal path ('File.write "src/pay.py", "x"') get the R76 refusal. Cause: program_writes allows an optional parenthesis after the os|fs|File|FileUtils|shutil|Dir method and after open/unlink/mkdir (\(?), but unreadable_calls requires a literal '(' for those heads (only unlink/mkdir/rmdir/rename with a $ target are handled without one). Paren-less calls are normal Ruby and Perl, and the goal names both. The docs/guards.md sentence 'a write whose target the guard cannot read ... is refused' is false for these. Regression test: ruby -e 'File.write p, "x"' and perl -e 'open FH, ">", $p' get the 'cannot name' refusal.
