Slot store notes (QA round 3 of P130, 2026-10-13, no criterion broken): vbw plan done also takes slots through the unit runner but may print the 'not in force' line twice on an unwritable store and never prints the end-of-run waited/lost line; a waiting entry left by a unit that lost the store stays until its run exits; each waiting unit polls the store every 0.1 s with several jq calls (CPU under heavy waiting). Judge with T141

Status line hand-back carries only the earlier status line's command: its padding and its own refresh interval are not kept, and VBW's 5-second refresh applies, so a slow earlier status line re-runs every 5 s in projects where VBW is off (QA of P134, 2026-10-14). Keep them when vbw statusline on writes the setting

The R152 rule (tests/release-run.bats: no default-run test file measures a duration) misses millisecond timers: it looks for SECONDS and date +%s, and for Time::HiRes only in proof-stale-links.bats, so a perl -MTime::HiRes timer in any other default test file slipped through (F220's first test, 2026-10-14). Look for Time::HiRes, gdate +%N and similar in every default-run file

vbw doctor builds the session-record path from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID without the plain-name check the SessionStart hook and the status line apply (plugin/lib/cmd-doctor.sh doctor_path); read-only and the id comes from Claude Code, so the risk is nil, but the rule should be one shared check (QA of P135, 2026-10-14)

The closing step (close run, and fixing's fix done without a session) runs on the Lead's model again, as the user chose it (owner 2026-10-14: 'I want to keep lead being who user selected. dont care about the extra cost'): undo D369's CLOSE_MODEL haiku in the five workflows and its docs (docs/workflows.md, docs/rigor.md) and tests (close-haiku-docs.bats, profile-lead-opus.bats); a cheaper close stays a brainstorm idea (B4) for 2.1.1

The loop opened T74 twice (2026-10-14 17:58): two Stop hook answers in one turn each ran 'loop T74 open' (commits b0dffb1c, e1769919), adding its requirement twice (R188, R189); opening an item must be idempotent. Also: a dropped requirement's id (R188, dropped by D378) was reused for a new one, so decisions naming R188 now point at the wrong requirement; ids of dropped requirements are never reused

Linux: Ctrl-C does not stop a vbw check that waits on the computer-wide limit (2.0.36 CI, run 38574239511, failed twice on Linux bash 5; passes on macOS under bash 3.2 and 5): tests/machine-recovery.bats 'R181: a run interrupted with Ctrl-C ends and gives its slot back at once' sees vbw still running 10 s after SIGINT to its process group. Reproduce in Linux (tools/test-linux.sh needs Docker running), find whether the kernel's INT trap (plugin/lib/slots.sh slots_traps) or the test is at fault, fix the root cause; CI must be green

Gate waits are not counted as 'waited' (P139.1 DEVN-02, 2026-10-14): when another vbw check of the same project holds the check gate, vbw check, prove and mutate wait at the gate without the 'waited' line, because plugin/lib/checks.sh counts only slot waits. P139.1 worked around it in cmd-mutate.sh (slots_take/slots_give mutate before the checks); fix the root cause in checks.sh and remove that workaround

A resumed session loses the loop's engine (2026-10-14 21:05): the loop's Stop hook (vbw auto gate) is declared in plugin/skills/loop/SKILL.md, so it exists only while that skill is loaded; after /exit and claude --resume the record still says 'loop on' but nothing drives it, and the session sat at approve for an hour. Running /vbw:loop again only says 'a loop is already on'. The loop must survive a resume (a plugin-level Stop hook that is inert unless a loop is on for this session), and SessionStart should say when a loop is on with no driver

Two limits do one job (P139.1 mutation finding, 2026-10-14): the check_jobs cap is enforced both in plugin/lib/checks.sh (checks_run_all) and in plugin/lib/proofcopy.sh (proofcopy_slots), so breaking either alone leaves the cap in force and no test can tell them apart; keep one owner of the cap

The mutation finish check binds only the last plan of a requirement (found in M33, 2026-10-14): plan done skips the missing-breaks check while another plan of the requirement is unfinished, so an earlier plan can finish with 1 of 10 rules broken (P139.2) and the gap lands on the last plan, which may not own the code (P141.2, docs). Each plan should owe the breaks for the rules its own checks cover

CRITICAL: a loop park can leave VBW unable to read its own record (2026-10-14 23:43, M33): the park reverts the item's code commits first and writes the record after; T74's commits included the record validator change for the new mutations field, so after the reverts the kernel rejected the record ('P139.1 has an unknown field: mutations'), the park's record write never happened, and the project was stuck with 22 reverts and an item still in progress. Restored by reverting the reverts (00:35). The park must reconcile the record before reverting kernel code it depends on, or refuse to park an item that changed the record's schema, and must never leave the record unreadable

vbw apply --patch drops a plan's recorded mutation breaks (2026-10-14): patching a reset plan (to add a file) erased its 19 recorded breaks, including the survivors that justified a strengthened check file; the next proof then flagged that strengthening commit (e120842e) as out of scope and the loop parked T74. Mutations are kernel-recorded evidence like status: a patch must keep them

Wording tests become fact tests (D399/D400, owner 2026-10-15): tests that pin sentences of docs/ or agent instructions are removed or rewritten to check the facts a user relies on (commands, settings, numbers, files, limits); behaviour tests stay

Loop stop rule (owner 2026-10-15): each loop item gets a time and spend budget from its size and the recorded times of past items; when it is spent the loop stops before its next step and reports where the item stands, instead of grinding on

Mutation check cost on slow test suites (owner 2026-10-15, for 2.0.39): each break re-runs the plan's checks, so the cost is rules x test time (cargo test at 3 min x 10 rules = 30 min per plan). By design, no measuring needed: a break runs only the fastest check covering its rule (durations from the run store, .git/vbw/runs.json); a check above a time limit is broken once per plan, not once per rule. Big gain on slow suites, none lost on fast ones

Status line where VBW is off sits near its 60 ms budget (2.0.38 CI, 2026-10-15): 60.2 ms on GitHub's macOS runner (OVER, shard 1 failed), 42 ms on the owner's Mac; the hand-back path (R184) is the slowest status line path. Make it cheaper before 2.1.0 (slower Macs of public users), or measure CI against a calibrated budget as the panel bench already is (VBW_PANEL_BUDGET_MS)

Deep-tier task breaks deadlock early plans (M34, 2026-10-15): a plan whose requirement's checks only turn green after a later plan wires the code cannot break its tasks (vbw mutate refuses red checks; --check takes only that requirement's checks), so its Devs block (P142.1, P145.1) and a loop retry would block again and park the item. The kernel should know it: a task break of such a plan is asked of the plan that completes the check (as T152 does for rules), or plan done accepts --none naming that plan without a hand-written reason

Blocker before the next push (owner, 2026-10-16 02:11): with claude --plugin-dir ./plugin (2.0.39 + M34) Mission Control opens empty in the real window: no tab row, no Now box; /vbw-panel says it is open; Comms works. The same record renders fully in the fake mod (L1), so the real-window render throws and the ui.render catch hands back the default. Regression from M34 (P144/P145 pane changes); find the cause with the real Claude Code (2.1.301) and pin it with an L3 scenario that checks the pane draws its tab row

Mission Control tab plan (owner sketch 2026-10-12, split out of R190 by D419): tabs Now, Plan, Proof, Timeline, Settings; Team, Decisions and Costs fold in (models to Settings, decisions inside each phase in Plan, run costs to Timeline, sound switch to Settings); Settings changes go through the kernel and are read back. Do before T95 (Sessions tab) and T96 (costs) so those are built once

Scope check false alarm that parked T94 (2026-10-16 03:28): prove_scope (cmd-prove.sh) scans all history against today's record; survivor_files(plan) drops a strengthened test file as soon as a check of ANOTHER requirement reads it. T94's plan reused R189's now-box/containment test files for R190 checks (C379/C380), so M34's shipped P144.3 survivor commits on tests/panel/r189/now-box.test.mjs became 'scope violations' and the loop parked T94 (its work reverted). Fix: a survivor commit stays in scope by the record as it was when the plan was done (or scope ignores plans of shipped milestones), with a regression test; T94 then reruns
Park keeps ids; scope skips park-undone commits (done 2026-10-16, T102 scope false alarm)

Loop time budget from the item's own road, not its size label (owner 2026-10-18 after T139 was stopped at 3h40m of a 2h48m budget: labelled small, really 11 plans in 3 phases, five network drops counted as time): once an item is planned, its budget is twice the kernel's road estimate (R191) for it; the stuck test counts progress (plans done, fixes closed) so time lost to dropped connections or waiting for the user is not grinding; before planning the size default stays. After T94

Dev unblock (user-project feedback 2026-10-16/19 + T138 evidence; owner agreed 2026-10-19; after T138, before T94; absorbs T159 and T124): (1) a task break of vbw mutate defaults to the plan's own rule checks and refuses only when those fail on unbroken code; (2) a fix may commit the protected check files of its own requirement (they still wait for one approval; no standalone check drop, which would remove protection unapproved), with provenance-true trailers instead of an old plan; (3) failing checks and commands keep their full output after the run and print the failing test names; (4) the mutate report says 'survives the approved check; caught by the pending one' when a strengthened check waits for approval

Proof speed on a Rust project (user-project feedback 2026-10-19; owner agreed 2026-10-19; after the Dev unblock item, with T129): measure on a user project why fix done reuses so little (17 of 184) and the CPU of VBW's own read/write tracking (jq near 100% for minutes, load 23-66; also seen 2026-10-19 here: vbw next over 2 min), then make the tracking cheap and count VBW's own work in the machine-wide limit

Mutation break file gets a fresh modification time in the proof copy (user-project feedback 2026-10-16; owner agreed 2026-10-19): cargo and other time-based builds otherwise test the unbroken build and report false survivors; regression test with a time-based build stand-in

The Lead cannot reword an approved rule (F269, 2026-10-19): vbw apply --patch matches a rule by requirement and text, so new wording adds a rule and the stale one stays; a shipped milestone's rule cannot be reached at all. Give rules a stable address (R188.10) that a patch can reword or retire, with re-approval, so a later requirement that changes behaviour can update the earlier rule instead of leaving it stale (R188.10 is superseded by R193 meanwhile)

L3 scenarios missing for M38 and M39 (owner 2026-10-19: push first, then these first): session names and the Sessions tab (holder named in the status line, Comms and vbw next; resume line), and M39 (a task break by own rules on an early plan, a fix committing its own requirement's check file with one approval, kept failing output named by vbw show fix). Each milestone should add its scenarios while built; find why M38 and M39 did not
tools/bump-version.sh --help bumps the version instead of printing usage (2026-10-19): unknown flags should print usage and change nothing

Panel render headroom (2026-10-20): R199's whole-row tab layout raised 'render, Comms and Mission Control' from about 0.44 ms to 0.47-0.51 ms CPU against the 0.5 ms budget (release run 2.0.40: 0.473). Profile the render path and win back headroom (measure the head once per width, not per candidate), so a slower Mac does not fail the release bench

Cores per heavy check (D340, M42 measurement): heavy test commands (cargo, make) each use every core, so several at once overload the Mac (load 23-66 seen). Decide from M42's measured core use: tell each command its share through the standard variables (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, MAKEFLAGS, GOMAXPROCS) or a per-check cores mark

Step estimates learn from idle time (2026-10-20, seen on a large private project: 'proving 32 of 174 checks, about 732 min'): a fix or build step whose run stayed open overnight or waiting for the user is recorded at its whole length (13 h, 18 h, 40 h), so the median estimate is hours too long. Time only active work (exclude waits for the user, approvals and other runs), or drop steps far beyond their size

Build pace (owner 2026-10-20, top after the push): VBW's step estimates leave out the mutation step (M42 waves ran 3-6x over: 7 min said, 60 taken); make estimates count it, make the mutation step cheaper (one break per rule, breaks in parallel), and never let fix done wait silently for a check-file approval the agent cannot ask for (M42 fix round sat 40 min)
Two proofs at once took 335 s wall vs 57.6 s for one (M42 after-measurement, limit 7, max held 7): find why sharing the computer-wide limit costs 6x

tests/machine-bookkeeping.bats orders events by the wall clock in whole seconds and is exempted file-wide from the R152 clock guard (ec91c964): order events with a sequence instead and drop the exemption
M42 shipped without VBW's QA review (owner D490, 2026-10-20): run the review on P161-P165 after the push and record its verdict

smallchange L3 (2.0.41, 2026-10-20) failed one fact: a one-flag change to greet.sh got QA tier standard, not quick, because the session proposed standard for its phase (P2 proposed: standard; P1 express). Passed with quick on 2.0.32. Find why the router proposes standard for a tiny change; a small change must stay small

A single proof uses about 1.9 of its 7 slots on average (T175 trace, 2026-10-21, 200-unit stand-in): units are launched one after another in checks_run_units (several jq runs and a 0.05 s poll per unit), so a proof could finish much sooner if units started as fast as slots free; measure, then fix

A proof still holds about 5.2 of 7 slots while units run (T179 after-trace, 2026-10-21): each unit's two locked slot-store steps (take p50 96 ms, give p50 52 ms under load, ~5 processes each, 0.05 s retries) and the gate mutex (p50 31 ms, 0.1 s retries) keep slots idle between units; make those steps cheaper (slots.sh, core.sh) to get close to the limit

Now box (R189) shows what VBW is doing and when the step started, but not its end ('until around HH:MM' sits lower in 'This step: ...'); when VBW needs the user it shows the short description, not the need sentence or the command (e.g. /vbw:approve); sentences below repeat it. A redesign must change the approved tests/panel/r189/now-box.test.mjs and r192/holder.test.mjs, and move the gate-command list from panel-lines.js to panel-view.js
Redraw assets/kernel-diagram.jpg (README): add the QA review step and the delivered-files check, and show the Devs as 'as many as the work allows' rather than exactly three

Slots held while units run, the rest (2.1.10 trace, 2026-10-24: 6.08 of 7 after the gate lock became a file; target 6.5): the store step runs jq inside its lock (busy about half the time, take waits p50 18 ms) and each unit change costs two steps; run the step's jq on a copy read outside the lock and lock only to compare and rename, or keep runners across units so a slot passes to the next unit in one step

Timeline during a proof (owner, 2026-10-25): while vbw prove runs, the Timeline tab says 'No VBW workflow runs in this session right now', which reads as if nothing is happening. Say a proof is running (checks done of total) and point to the Proof tab
Store the mutation check's time breakdown (R207) under the plan's mutation entry in the record, so vbw show plan can show where a mutation run's time went (Architect note, M43 planning 2026-10-26)

At vbw init, point out large git-ignored folders the proof's clean copy would copy, as candidates for the Clean copy section (Architect note, M43 planning 2026-10-26; the 500 MB line of R206 covers the slow-disk case after the fact)

vbw apply refuses a check whose rules are owned by two plans of one milestone that build one after the other (directly, or through a shared file): the earlier plan's mutation step finds the check red on unbroken code and the plan blocks (M43 2026-10-26: P166.1 and P168.1, each sharing its check file with the plan after it; fixed by splitting the files). The Lead's spec gets the same rule in words.
The own-work line (VBW's own work: X of Y min) shows seconds when the wall is under a minute: a mutation run takes seconds and reads '0.0 of 0.0 min' (M43 2026-10-26, R207.5)

check-loop-writes.sh sees only builtin writes in the loop body itself: a call to a function that writes with printf (doctor_line in cmd-doctor.sh, found 2026-10-26 in P168.2's hidden-file loop) passes unseen and is left to the reviewer. Teach the tool the repo's writer functions (every function whose body writes with a builtin, found by the tool itself), so such a call in a loop fed by a process substitution is refused like a direct printf

A full vbw apply (the planning workflow's) keeps a started plan's status and recorded breaks but drops its note (the blocked reason): seen 2026-10-26 on P169.3 after P170 was planned; the reason survived only in the phase's escalations. Keep the note with the status

A requirement whose rules name a plan on some rules only (mixed) leaves the unnamed rules' owner undefined: vbw show plan leaves them unmarked while the task break of a non-completing plan skips their checks (the Lead's known cost in P170, 2026-10-26). Have vbw apply refuse a mixed requirement (name a plan on every rule or on none), so the question never arises

A survivor of vbw mutate cannot be fixed when the rule's check file is shared with other requirements' checks (filtered cases in one file, as the lean-tests rule asks): vbw commit refuses the file as 'no other requirement's check file is the plan's to commit' (P170.5, 2026-10-26: tests/l3-taskbreak.bats holds C473 of R209 beside C463 of R207 and R193's cases). Let the Dev strengthen a check file that its own rule's check names, the edit waiting for approval as any check edit; the user sees the whole diff at the approval

Widen the R211 refusal: two plans of the same wave whose rules share one check face the same hazard as consecutive plans (the first Dev's mutation step runs the check before the other Dev has committed; a race, so it fails only sometimes). The Lead's brief already says a check's rules belong to one plan; the kernel refusal should cover any two open plans sharing a check (Architect note, M44 planning 2026-10-27)

Reuse lost on a root commit when a check runs ./script (2026-10-29, macOS): a test that executes ./greet.sh puts the project root's listing on its read list (sh greet.sh does not; present on main, 2.1.18), so any commit that adds a root file reruns every such check. Find what lists the folder (getcwd on exec?) and whether that read can be told apart from a listing the test depends on; measured with the scratch script ab-reuse.sh, both kernels

tests/mutate-time.bats R207 'the figures are measured' asserts a real second (b >= 1.0) in a file the proof runs untimed; it failed on an Ubuntu 26.04 runner in the 2.1.19 CI. Inject the clock as #719 did for the own-work case, or move the case to a timed file

Bench blind spot (F327, 2026-10-27): a uniformly slow CI runner passes the busy test (startup under 20 ms) yet fails every absolute budget (Ubuntu 26.04 shards 1 and 2 of the 2.1.18 release run, hooks at 20-21 ms, status line over 60 ms, same code 11-12 ms elsewhere). Give the bench a same-host reference (a budget scaled by the measured startup against a reference startup) or a second run on a fresh runner

Guard per-call cost (2026-10-27): R219's unreadable_calls regex is compiled into guard-bash.jq on every call and adds about 1.5 ms (git case 10.6 to 12.1 ms, interp 10.3 to 12.9 ms, A/B against v2.1.17). Keep it out of the common path (a second jq program run only for interpreter commands) or cheapen it

Workflow results (F325, 2026-10-27): a Dev that stopped on a hung command returned a placeholder 'blocked' result the workflow took as a report. The building and fixing workflows should reject a result whose commits or checks are empty with no refusal text, and rerun or name it as stopped

Empty-match refusal beyond bats (Lead note, M45): R220 refuses a bats --filter that matches no case; extend the same refusal to pytest -k, go test -run and node --test-name-pattern, and to the check vbw fix check writes

Refusal text for receiver calls (QA note, M45): the guard's unreadable-write refusal quotes the call from the dot (.write_text(p)) instead of from its receiver (path.write_text(p)); start the quote at the receiver

tools/bench-hooks.sh: the reference workload is compute-bound (a jq range of 30000) while the guard's cost is startup and parse bound, so on GitHub's Ubuntu 26.04 runner (jq 1.8.1) the reference ran at ratio 0.90 and every guard case came out 20.2–21.5 ms against the 20 ms budget: OVER, not slow (PR #739 CI, 2026-10-30). Shape the reference like a guard call (one jq reading a JSON document of fixed size with a program of fixed size) so its ratio tracks the hooks' cost; keep the nominal figure from the same shape

Guard gap: sed -i (and other in-place editors) on a file outside the run's lease passed the Bash guard while the Edit tool was refused (P186.2 Dev, 2026-10-31, plugin/lib/mutate-queue.sh); the guard-bash program should name in-place edits (sed -i, perl -pi, tee, redirections) as writes to their file argument

L3 mapnotrun judge: commands_lines in tools/l3-suite.sh reads the spec's ## Commands with sed and counts lines inside the <!-- --> example block (test: npm test, build: ...), so a command written only in a comment would be judged present; skip comment blocks and pin it in tests/l3-mapnotrun.bats (seen in the 2.1.21 run, result unaffected)

R231 did not reach its goal on Ubuntu 26.04: in PR #740 guard (git) / reference was 1.02 on macOS (17.0/16.7 ms), 1.33 on Linux bash 5 (12.0/9.0) and 1.63 on Ubuntu 26.04 (20.7/12.7), so the guard pays a cost on Ubuntu 26.04 the guard-shaped reference does not hold (guard cases 20.0-21.5 ms OVER 20). Find what (jq build or version, sh, the guard program's hot builtins) with a per-step profile on that runner before changing the reference again

Two CI flakes in PR #740, neither file changed since 2.1.20: tests/timed-bench-hooks.bats 'waiting is not counted' failed on a busy macOS runner (sh and jq startup 9.5 ms, 12.1 vs 39.1 ms against a 25 ms margin; measure once more before failing, as the bench does); tests/step-bench.bats R190 'step running' failed on Linux bash 5 shard 3 (the status line did not show the step once, VBW_BENCH_RUNS=1)

CI flake in PR #740 run 3 (Ubuntu 26.04 shard 2): tests/lock-exclusive.bats 'R190: a note lock folder left 5 s without an owner's id is taken over' expected 'taken after 5 tries' and saw 4; the test counts real-time tries outside the timed files (inject the clock, as R232 did for mutate-time)

#694 (2.1.23, owner yes 2026-10-31): opt-in MCP tools for VBW agents, per server listed by the project; read-only roles get a tool only when the user marks it read-only; writing roles get every listed tool under the guards; first probe how Claude Code resolves plugin agents' tools: with mcp__ names and wildcards. VBW builds; halindrome tests on a project with code-graph and context-mode servers (before/after tool counts)

decisions.text: QA re-check data adds no new record field and no schema change: a phase's QA pass stores one digest of that phase's own inputs (its plans' files, its checks' files, its goal, criteria, plans and rules, and the digests of phases it builds on) in the existing qa.tree field; the per-input digests used to name a reason are a clone-local cache in $(git common dir)/vbw/qa.json; without the cache the reason is 'its inputs changed'
decisions.why: A digest field in the record would need a new schema; VBW 2.0.17 requires schema 2 exactly when a check is alone and calls any other schema-2 record corrupt (R46). With qa.tree reused, 2.0.16/2.0.17 read the record and at worst re-check every phase (today's behaviour); the digest is computed from committed content, so every clone agrees which passes stand

Proof speed before (M42) on this Mac: stand-in (5000 files, 500 folders, 200 units); prove 86.29 s wall, own work 142.06 s (165%) (VBW's own seconds summed over parallel units, so above wall; 2.4 min of a 1.4 min proof); fix done after one file: reused 99 of 100 units (99 expected from the read lists; a fix of R1 judges its 100 checks, not the test files); jq 52.42 CPU s in 11142 processes; store 78042 bytes; written lists 1266537 bytes; vbw next 31.35 s with the store full; own-work steps: planning 6.22 s, copies 7.21 s, read tracking 121.78 s, saving 6.67 s, record 0.17 s. (a) cleared: jq process count is the same (906 vs 907) for 24 and 96 folders, since no unit of the stand-in lists a folder, so per-folder fingerprints cost nothing here; (b) confirmed: written lists reach 1266537 bytes (about 11 times the 114789 bytes seen with the later one-list-per-run store), and the cache-writing units inflate them; (c) cleared: store and record parsing is about 4 of roughly 55 jq processes per unit and the store is only 78042 bytes, so the cost is not there; (d) confirmed: vbw next takes 31.35 s because it redoes the proof's reuse planning on every call. Biggest own cost: read tracking is 86% of own work (resetting access times over 5206 files and collecting per unit), which the two named fixes alone do not remove.
decisions.why: Measured with tools/measure-proof-speed.sh at its default size on 2026-10-20, on the tree with the P162 speed changes (reads.sh list store, vbw next cache) taken out, so these are the figures before any fix; the same run on the tree with them in showed written lists 114789 bytes and vbw next 28.64 s.

Proof speed after (M42) on this Mac: stand-in (5000 files, 500 folders, 200 units); prove 57.58 s wall, own work 55.71 s (97%) (VBW's own seconds summed over parallel units; 0.9 min of a 0.9 min proof, from 2.4 min of a 1.4 min proof before); fix done after one file: reused 99 of 100 units (expected 99, the units whose read lists do not contain the changed file); jq 21.82 CPU s in 6289 processes; store 78042 bytes; written lists 131477 bytes; vbw next 3.18 s with the store full; own-work steps: planning 0.87 s, copies 6.12 s, read tracking 48.36 s (0.24 s per unit), saving 0.22 s, record 0.15 s; two proofs: max held 7 of limit 7. Before to after: own work 142.06 s to 55.71 s, read tracking 121.78 s to 48.36 s, jq 52.42 CPU s to 21.82, written lists 1266537 to 131477 bytes, vbw next 31.35 s to 3.18 s. Suspects: (a) cleared before and after; (b) fixed, the store keeps each run's list once; (c) cleared before and after; (d) fixed, vbw next reads the proof-units cache. The remaining cost beyond (a) to (d) was read tracking itself, all VBW's own, now fixed in plugin/lib/reads.sh by four changes, each with a regression test in tests/timed-proof-speed.bats shown red first: the folder-to-names map is built once per copy and not on every collection (collect 0.67 s to 0.17 s); a reset sets back only the files the last run moved, not all 5206; one walk of the copy finds every moved path (three finds a collection, not one per list); the first reset of a fresh copy no longer waits for the next whole second where file times are finer. Inherent and left reported: the first proof of a fresh clone says 'ran again: 200 of 200 units; top reasons: this clone has no earlier recorded run (200)', and each unit still reads every tracked file's access time once (the stand-in's units are built to read), now at 0.24 s per unit. One observation, not a target of this plan: two 200-unit proofs at once took 335.26 s wall together on the shared limit of 7 slots, against 57.58 s for one alone; the held count never exceeded the limit.
decisions.why: Measured with tools/measure-proof-speed.sh at its default size (default run, then --two) on 2026-10-20, with the finished P162 and P163 code and the P162.4 changes to plugin/lib/reads.sh. Machine limit 7 (10 cores). Figures from one run each, not averaged; the own-work total has about 5 s of margin under the 60 s target.

F320 diagnosis and fix direction: the R204 count in tests/scope-history.bats (shell commands traced with set -x, counted as lines starting with +) is a racy measurement, not a scope-check regression. prove_scope's process-substitution children and pipeline parts (printf, jq, git) inherit set -x and write their trace lines into the same trace file as the parent shell, at the same time, and bash writes a line in more than one call (the PS4 prefix, each word, the newline), so under load one process's line lands inside another's and its + prefix is no longer at a line start: grep -c '^+' then misses it. Fix in the tests, not the kernel: PS4 carries a marker no traced word contains, and the count is the number of markers anywhere in the trace (grep -o MARKER | wc -l), which a merged line keeps because the prefix is written in one call. Apply the same to the delivered-files trace count in tests/qa-delivered.bats (same pattern, same latent flaw). No tests/helper.bash change: 497 test files load it and the two trace functions stay local to their files.
decisions.why: Proof 3: 80 shell commands for 50 commits, 81 for 500, in a suite run under bash 5.3 at load 14-19 on 10 cores; the case passes alone. 48 reproductions of the case (16 under /bin/bash 3.2 quiet, 8 then 24 in parallel under bash 5.3 with 6 CPU burners, load up to 90) counted 81 and 81 every time, so the proof's 80 is a lost line, never an extra command: both projects run the same commands (the traces list the same 81, only n=50 vs n=500 differ in text). The traces show the children's lines (level +++) interleaved with the parent's (++) in one file, and the order at each site is timing-dependent: the child's printf line precedes the parent's 15 KB jq -n -c line in all 48 traces at that site and follows the parent's read lines at the others. 960 micro-runs of one jq call with a process substitution (bash 3.2, 24 parallel) produced no merge, so the race is rare; it is real because its only precondition is two writers of multi-call lines on one shared offset. Shown by: a reproduction copy of the test in the scratchpad keeping each trace, and the trace shapes above. Not shown: a merged line caught in the act.

items.text: Panel render headroom (2026-10-20): R199's whole-row tab layout raised 'render, Comms and Mission Control' from about 0.44 ms to 0.47-0.51 ms CPU against the 0.5 ms budget (release run 2.0.40: 0.473). Profile the render path and win back headroom (measure the head once per width, not per candidate), so a slower Mac does not fail the release bench

Proof speed on a Rust project (user-project feedback 2026-10-19; owner agreed 2026-10-19; after the Dev unblock item, with T129): measure on a user project why fix done reuses so little (17 of 184) and the CPU of VBW's own read/write tracking (jq near 100% for minutes, load 23-66; also seen 2026-10-19 here: vbw next over 2 min), then make the tracking cheap and count VBW's own work in the machine-wide limit

The Lead cannot reword an approved rule (F269, 2026-10-19): vbw apply --patch matches a rule by requirement and text, so new wording adds a rule and the stale one stays; a shipped milestone's rule cannot be reached at all. Give rules a stable address (R188.10) that a patch can reword or retire, with re-approval, so a later requirement that changes behaviour can update the earlier rule instead of leaving it stale (R188.10 is superseded by R193 meanwhile)
